# Melee — the build notes

**The archive. `CLAUDE.md` is the live rules; this is why each one exists.** It is not loaded
automatically — `grep -n` it for a symbol, a build number (`(m146`), or the words in his
report, and read the entry before touching that system. New notes go at the TOP of the
landmine list, in the same shape: what he said, what was actually wrong, what was measured.

## The bow: one mark, locks on archers, a full blast blows them apart (m1782)
*"The double reticle for the bow seems redundant -- we only need the one that shows the height and distance (the lock reticle is good). I can't lock
onto the archers, only the statues and the spider. A full charge with the exploding arrows should explode the archers -- those are powerful arrows."*
- The screen reticle (`#retic`) is off while the bow is out (`BOW.noRetic`): its marks are the landing emblem with its height stake, and the lock.
- `flyAim` with the BOW (`FLYAIM.bowAny`) takes a hostile body at ANY height -- archers on the ground, beasts -- not only one above him; the lock
  mark (`lockMk`) shows on him and the arc solves to him. A blown-apart body no longer locks (`flyFoe` skips `boomed`).
- `arrowBlast(P, dirH, full)`: a FULL draw's blast is `fullK` 1.35 wider, and every archer / horde body inside it is killed and blown apart
  (`limbBoom`). A part-draw blast is as before.

## The guardian's stone draws both sides (m1780)
*His close-up: "What is going on with the render -- he is see-through in various polygons."*
- `guardLoad` forced `FrontSide` (Tripo writes doubleSided on everything, m25's rule). But the hard-surface rig SPLITS the mesh at every bone
  boundary and `hs_caps.py` fills the open loops (`holes_fill`), whose winding is whatever the fill gave it, and the Tripo scan has inward
  triangles of its own -- so with back faces culled, those patches vanished and the far side showed through. The guardian kinds now draw
  `DoubleSide` (`Z.twoSide` 0 = culled). The spider never overrode its export's two-sided material.
- The root fix is in the pipeline (`bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals` after the caps, then a re-export) -- noted, not done.

## Turquoise is the flame now -- the bow, the sword, the debris; the Osari stay green (m1779)
*"I'd like this turquoise to be the flame colour for the other things that use the green -- the bow or the sword."*
- `gfire`'s default palette is TURQUOISE (1); `ofire` is the Osari's green (0), used only by the Osari's vanish / fade and the spider's acid spit.
  So the fire arrow (its trail, its burn, its head `hc` [.3, 1, .9]), sword-cut debris dissolving, statues waking, the guardian's and spider's
  breaks all burn turquoise. `killBlast` takes the palette (its flames, sparks and smoke -- `TURQ.shade()` -- turquoise; the Osari's green).
- The katana's left row is STEEL / FIRE / **JIN**: JIN is the blade fire (`BFL`) in turquoise; FIRE stays the orange (m1762). Both cores are the
  particle's own colour lifted.

## The guardian's and the spider's breaks burn TURQUOISE (m1777)
*"I like the turquoise in the guardian -- the green mist cloud needs to match it better colour-wise."*
- `gfire` takes a palette (`pal`): 0 the Osari's green, 1 TURQUOISE -- white-cyan -> turquoise -> deep teal, the hard-surface caps' colour.
  `tfire` is the turquoise call; every flame and spark in the guardian's and the spider's hit / cut / death / rock code uses it (their sparks
  [.5, 1, .55] -> [.3, 1, .9]). The flame's hot core is now the particle's own colour lifted (it was a fixed yellow-green), so the green flame
  is unchanged and the turquoise one burns turquoise. The spider's acid spit stays green.

## The wall by VELOCITY, angled jump-offs, the wall cam (m1776, DOCKET 17)
*"The camera on a wall run or wall jump -- jumping back and forth between opposite walls it was so scrunched I couldn't see." / "Change the wall run
again: entirely velocity and angle based -- if you have the speed it's a wall run, when the velocity finishes it's a wall sit, riding down the wall.
Straight up, straight over, diagonal or anywhere between is set by the angle he first hits the wall at, with what speed. And the jump away from
the wall is only ever orthogonal -- there should be variation."*
- **Prince of Persia** does it by animation: a fixed run along, a fixed climb up, a kick-off back -- speed and angle decide nothing there. His
  version is the physical one, which suits this game better than PoP's fixed distances.
- **`WRUN.mode` VEL (default; TOOLS > WALL: VELOCITY / STICK -- STICK is m1767's):** at the catch his velocity is turned onto the wall's plane --
  along it what he carried along it (`alongK`), up it what he drove INTO it (`upK`) plus what he was already rising. Over `runMin` 3.5 m/s it is a
  run in THAT direction (head-on = straight up, glancing = along, between = diagonal); the wall's gravity (`vG` 11) bends it and `vFric` bleeds
  the along part; under `keepMin` 2.2 (or `runMax` 1.6 s) it becomes the wall SIT (the slide). The pose follows the direction (steeper than
  `upAng` .9 rad = the run-up, else the side run). Under `runMin` at the catch: straight into the sit.
- **The jump off (`wrunJump`, both modes):** out along the normal (`wjOut`) PLUS along the wall the left stick's share (`jumpSide` 5 x its
  tangent component) and `keep` of what the run carried -- straight out, angled ahead, angled back. The run-up's back flip stays when the stick
  has no sideways part.
- **The wall cam (`stepCam`):** on a wall and for `camHold` 1.1 s after, the lens turns to look ALONG the wall -- between two facing walls, down
  the corridor with both on screen -- the way he is moving along it (else the nearer end), pulls out `camPull` 2.2 m and up `camEl` .12 rad
  (`cam.wallK`, eased). A drag outranks it.
- **Measured (Wall Park, the shipped frame):** head-on sprint jump: caught at 12.1 m/s up -> the run-up -> the lip. A shallow angle (stick
  .9 / -.4): caught with 6.4 m/s along -> a SIDE run along the face, sagging 1.1 -> .7 m, off its end. Falling onto it slowly: straight into the
  sit, skidding down. Wall cam weight .9-.99 on all three. (Harness note: a fake stick needs `far` set, or the left pad reads as HELD IN PLACE and
  the zoom charge pins him; and the stick is camera-relative, so reset `cam.az` between runs.)

## The katana's charge release, by the left stick, again; the bow's emblem flat (m1773)
*"Press up on the right stick to charge. Nothing on the left stick: a downward slash, he does not launch forward -- mostly in place, forward just a
little. Forward on the left stick and release: the launch, as now. The high attack: tap the left stick to jump and release, or hold down and
release, as now." / "Not liking the black pencil-thin line round the reticle -- a flat colour."*
- `chargeRelease`: neutral (`CHARGE3.dead`) = the same release with its travel capped at `CHARGE3.still` .6 m (`p.goStill`); forward = the full
  launch; left / right = the whirlwind (unchanged); down = the leap (unchanged); IN THE AIR = the leap. The charge is now HELD through a jump
  (the right thumb still down, `!grounded`), as it was through the dodge flips (m1761), so tap-jump-release is the high attack.
- `bowMkTex` drops its dark under-pass; the stake's foot drops its dark ring. (The sword's lock was always flat white.)

## The ledge hang measured off the body he is wearing (m1772)
*His screenshot, hanging on the Wall Park's wall: "The ledge hang definitely isn't lined up."*
- `LEDGE.hang` / `out` were fractions of RIG.height measured off ZAP's hang clip (m122). Grumbo is another body on another bake: measured
  headless, his hands sit **1.43 m** above his root in `ledge_hang_idle`, where the typed numbers put them at 1.21 -- so his hands hung 22 cm
  ABOVE the lip, in the air.
- Now `ledgeAt` uses `ledgeHands()`: both hands in his own frame, averaged over the hang clip, cached per body (and per `bodyK`, so a
  disguise measures its own). The root goes where those hands land ON the lip: wrists `grip` .04 m above its top, `onto` .06 m in over the edge.
  The typed numbers stay as the fallback. Measured after: hands at y 4.54 on a 4.5 m lip, 6 cm in over the face; rendered.

## A drawn bow no longer pins his chest through a flip (m1771)
*"Bow drawn and pulled back, I flick the left stick to flip -- the upper torso doesn't flip, only the legs. Lol."*
- `bowSquare` (m1746) turns Spine1 onto a WORLD frame every frame -- the aim heading and world up -- and the flips (`airFlipGo`, `cartGo`) turn
  the ROOT. So below the spine he flipped and above it the squaring put the chest back upright. It now stands aside while he flips (`p.aflip`,
  `p.cart`, `p.flip`), rolls or runs a wall; the bow, gripped in the fist, turns with the hands.

## The fist moves travel when they fly, not on frame one (m1770)
*"Flick the left stick -- the front handspring, the flying punch, the flip kick: the physical locomotion doesn't line up with the attack; it lunges
forward stupidly at the beginning and then the attack comes later. Line them up like we did the katana's lunges."*
- **Why:** every strike's lunge started at full speed on frame one and bled off over the beat (`carry`), while these clips crouch first and leave
  the ground a quarter to a third of the way in. So he slid forward standing, then flew in place.
- **Measured (headless, each fist clip, 48 samples: the hips' height and every limb's speed against the hips, as fractions of the clip):**
    melee_01  2.25 s  hips .53 -> .96 (.25-.46) -> .33 @.80, hands .33 / .58   flight  [.26, .76]
    melee_02  1.58 s  crouched .31, rising to .66 @.52, right foot @.35        hop     [.12, .52]
    melee_03  1.40 s  .53 -> .76 @.56 -> .38 @.80, right foot @.50 (flip kick) flight  [.36, .80]
    melee_04  1.96 s  level, hands @.29 / .35                                   strike  [.08, .36]
    melee_05  1.17 s  .57 -> 1.18 @.56 -> .58 @1.0, hands push @.13 (handspring) flight [.12, .86]
    melee_extra 1.0 s level, right hand @.27                                    strike  [.04, .29]
- **Now (`FISTWIN`):** the same distance, spent in the move's window: a FLIGHT at an even speed from take-off to landing (eased `ease` .12 at
  each end), a strike with the lunge's own shape up to the blow; nothing before the window (the opening velocity waits too). With the katana in
  hand the left flick's fist moves use the window as well (the katana's own front-loaded lash is skipped for them). `FISTWIN.on` 0 = as before.
- Not watched headless (SwiftShader frames ran 3-40 s; the run timed out) -- his phone is the test.

## The wall on the LEFT stick; the catch is immediate (m1767, DOCKET 17)
*"If you jump against the wall and do nothing, instead of immediately going into the pose he does a weird glitchy thing -- like he's falling but
stuck, then falling, then the pose. Something is fighting it." / "Instead of the flick on the right stick, it's entirely the locomotion stick and
the velocity and trajectory: do nothing -> he skids down it, ready to jump off; keep holding up -> he runs up it if the velocity carries, release
-> back to the slide; thumb right -> a horizontal run, still slipping down; come at it at an angle holding up or diagonal -> a horizontal run; to
run straight up you have to hit it straight on."*
- **The glitch:** the m1372 perch LET GO whenever the left stick was pushed past .6 -- and jumping at a wall, the stick is always pushed toward it.
  It let go, the wall's `cool` refused the re-catch for .35 s, he fell, caught again: the stuck/falling flicker.
- **Now (`WRUN.stick` 1):** any touch of a tall face in the air catches him at once (`wrunCatch`), remembering whether he came in HEAD-ON (`headK`
  .8 of his speed into it), the climb that buys (`upK` x his speed into it, floor `upMin` 4.5) and his speed along it (floor `sideMin` 4.5). Every
  frame the stick picks the state (`wrunWant`): at rest = the SLIDE; toward the wall after a head-on catch = UP (one climb per catch; spent -> the
  slide); along it (`sideK`) or toward it after an ANGLED catch = SIDE, the way the stick (or his travel) says, sagging but never faster than
  `sideFall` 2.2 m/s, `T` s of it -> the slide; pulled away = let go. A change re-faces him and re-ramps the pose (`wrunSet`, `R.t0`). The tap is
  the jump off from any of them. The right flick is the strike again (`stick` 0 = m1604's swipe).
- **Measured (Wall Park, the 4.5 m wall, the shipped frame):** no stick: caught at 1.4 m, held, skid down at ~.5 m/s. Stick held head-on: UP from
  1.6 to 2.9 m, the lip, onto the deck. Released mid-climb: up -> slide at 2.4 m, rose on to 3.6, held, skid. Angled: a side run along the face.

## The willow's shrine, its bark, its vines and leaves (m1764)
*"Make a shader for the willow -- the stump is just brown. You made a square raised part -- maybe build a shrine, don't make it square, spend some
time on the design. The vines -- the vine and the leaf maybe each want their own colour; in the snow they're hard to see."*
- **The shrine (`willowBuild`, `WILLOW.tiers`)**: a SHINBOKU -- two low ROUND stone tiers (r 10.5 and 7.5, each a .3 m rise: under his .357 step,
  so no stairs), a coping ring, concentric dressed PAVING on the tops with snow drifted only against the rim, the raked rings on the upper tier, a
  red-and-black TORII at the front (+z, the beam's ends upswept), the two stone lanterns flanking the approach, and a SHIMENAWA rope round the
  trunk with white zigzag shide. Colliders: each tier is `strips` 14 axis-aligned slabs. The Snowfield's pack (.55 m) buried tiers that low, so
  the shrine is SWEPT: the snow field fades to nothing over its footprint with a soft bank round it (`snowStage`).
- **The bark (`willowBarkTex`)**: wandering vertical fissures, silver-violet ridges, jade moss in the deep grooves, lenticels; map + bump on the
  tubes, which now carry a UV (`willowTube`, ~1.8 m of bark per tile). The glowing veins still run in the vertex colour.
- **The vines (`willowLeafTex`)**: the stem its own plum-bark colour; each leaf painted -- deep jade at the stem to bright mint at the tip, a pale
  midrib, a dark rim -- so they read on snow; the vertex colour only shades now, and the tip glow is kept to the LEAVES (`diffuseColor.g - .r`).
- Rendered headless from the front, above and at the trunk.

## Blade fire: real fire, on the blade, slower -- pass 1 (m1762)
*"The katana fire -- not green, an actual burning fire. It's not coming out of the right spot -- on the blade, a lot at the tip and the rest of the
blade. The particles are too fast, they come from a point and shoot up; they look low grade. A few passes on that fire."*
- **Where:** `bladeFireStep` spawned between the GRIP and `muzzleWorld()`, which on the katana is not the blade. It now uses the swing trail's
  own segment (`heroSword()` base..tip in the weapon group), weighted to the tip (`BFL.tipW`).
- **What:** its own pool, `BFL` (one draw): the flame atlas (`gfireTex`, soft tongues with a hot core), white-yellow core -> orange -> deep red,
  NORMAL blending (additive goes white on snow); small (`size` .1-.2 m, a third bigger at the tip), slow (`rise` .35-.8 m/s plus a gentle
  `buoy`ancy and a curl), short-lived; each takes `carry` .22 of the blade's own velocity and is spread back along the frame's sweep, so a swing
  leaves a ribbon of flame. One in ten is an ember. The left sub-menu says STEEL / FIRE.
- Measured headless: the pool was born dead at first -- the config's `life` range and the per-particle `life` array shared a name (now `lifeR`).
  Rendered: flame along the upper blade at rest, tongues trailing a swing.
- Next passes (open): a heat shimmer / glow card on the blade itself, smoke wisps off the tongue tips, the flame's own sound, his own sprite sheet.

## The katana's charge flips without letting go; the bow's arc over a low wall; the bow's emblem (m1761)
*"Holding up to charge and I flick the left stick, he does a layout flip -- which I don't mind -- but then he releases the attack even though I
haven't released. It should just do the flips, like dodging in parry mode." / "A wall in front of me, the terrace round the willow -- the reticle
stayed fixed on that little ledge." / "The rings are too thick -- something closer to the sword's stylised one, like our emblem, a different colour."*
- **The release was the GROUND test**: a katana charge is only held while `p.grounded` (`katC`, `kaimHold`), so the flip's take-off fell through
  to `chargeRelease`. Now any left flick while the katana charges goes to the guard's `cartGo` (side / front / back flips, facing kept), and while
  `p.cart` runs the charge is simply held. On landing: still held -> it carries on charging; let go mid-flip -> it releases on landing.
- **The ledge**: `aimPoint` walks the lens's heading from the muzzle and STOPS at the first box, so the terrace's low wall became the bow's target
  and every draw solved onto it. Unlocked (and not 3D aim / back aim), `bowSolve` now aims at the open-air point at full range -- what it already
  did in the open -- and `bowArc`'s flight shows where it really lands (on the ledge, or over it).
- **The emblem (`bowMkTex`)**: the three thick rings are gone; the landing mark is one plane, the sword lock's family (hand wobble, worn gaps) but
  its own: an arrowhead at the middle, a thin broken ring, eight fletching chevrons pointing in (one worn away), a hairline outer ring; every stroke
  dark-under-light so it reads on snow and on wood. Jade on the open, amber on a body.

## The carried bow turns with him; sound after leaving the app (third try); the unarmed right-pad zoom off (m1760)
*"When you flip or jump the bow doesn't follow the rotation of his body -- it stays straight up and down. If I leave the game and come back the
sounds are all muted. When you're unarmed and hold up on the right stick he does the run charge -- take that away for now, I trigger it by accident."*
- **Bow (`bowFist`, carried):** the m1748 diagonal is built off his FACING, which no flip turns. On the ground it is kept and remembered in the
  LEFT HAND's frame (`BOW.inHand`); off the ground, rolling, flipping or on a wall it rides the hand with that offset (`BOW.lockK`, eased over
  `lockT` .12 s), so it turns with the flip; on landing it eases back to the diagonal.
- **Sound:** m1699 rebuilt the context on the FIRST event after a return -- usually `pointerdown`, which iOS does not accept as a gesture that may
  start audio, so the new context was born locked. And m1097's 400 ms fallback rebuilt it from a TIMER -- outside any gesture, born locked too.
  Now: a return is answered only inside `touchend` / `click` / `keydown` -- a silent HTML <audio> is played first (that re-activates iOS's audio
  session after an interruption; WebAudio alone does not), then the context is rebuilt in the same gesture. `pointerdown` only nudges a resume,
  and the timer only flags the next real tap. The debug chip carries `AU<state><rebuilds>` (`AUrun2`, `AUsus1`) -- if it is still muted, that
  token says whether the context never woke (`sus`) or woke silent (`run`). Not testable headless.
- **Zoom:** `ZOOM.right` 0 -- the right pad held up, unarmed, no longer charges it. The LEFT pad's hold-in-place zoom (`LHOLD` ZOOM) still does;
  `mel.ZOOM.right = 1` brings the right one back.

## The bow points down the shot again; the arc is a line, not dots, with a height stake (m1759)
*"When you pull a bow shot he's 90 degrees to the wrong direction. I don't like the dots -- those balls look really out of place ... the arc shows
how a lighter shot goes up more, that's really smart ... maybe one height thing at the end, a depth plane ... half opacity."*
- **The 90 degrees was m1746's `bowSquare`**: it turned his CHEST'S FRONT to the aim, but an archer stands side-on and the arrow runs along the bow
  arm, so the shot pointed 90 deg left. It now turns the ARROW LINE (right hand -> left hand, levelled) onto the aim. Measured headless, drawn,
  camera at 3.14: the hand line's heading 3.14.
- **The arc (`bowArc`)**: the 40 pips are gone; the path is a thin translucent camera-facing RIBBON (`BARC.w` .05 m, `op` .45), thin at the bow.
  Under the landing ring, when the shot lands ABOVE the ground (a flyer, a wall, a body), a half-transparent STAKE drops to the ground with a small
  foot ring: its length is the height, its foot is where in plan. TOOLS > BOW ARC LINE / OFF (the ring and stake stay either way).

## Flyers overhead: the lens tips up, the gun and bow lock on, the lightning announces itself, an edge arrow (m1757)
*"Anytime we have a flying animal above you, or an archer, or a cannon ... the camera tilts to show them -- we need the same when an enemy is above you,
like this dragon flying overhead; it's just out of screen. I couldn't hit it at all. I couldn't even see when its bolts were coming."*
- **The up-look (`UPLOOK`, `upLookW`)** only ever answered SHOTS in the air (m1276) and a turret that had seen him (m1350). A hostile body ABOVE him
  (`flyFoe`: a flyer -- `d.fy` -- an archer, a beast; its middle more than `dy` 2 m over his chest, inside `flyR` 24 m) now tips it while it is there,
  weighted by its elevation; a flyer adds `flyEl` .14 rad more (`cam.upF`). Measured headless with the mech at 5.2 m, 6.5 m off: the weight reaches .96.
- **The aim (`FLYAIM`, `flyAim`, in `aimRaw`)**: the aim lock is off (m36) and the vertical assist only took MACHINES (m1259), so a gun or a bow
  held up at a flyer shot level under it. Now a `flyFoe` above him within `cone` .38 rad of the lens and 45 m is where the shot goes, at any
  elevation (the bow's arc solves to it). Measured: aimRaw lands at (6.8, 6.1, 9.1) on the dragon at (6.8, 5.0, 9.1), lock 1. On the ground nothing changes.
- **The lightning (`beastStrike`)**: a pale ring on the floor, under his own body, with no sign of who called it. Now the ring is solid with a dark
  rim and FILLS in as the strike comes, a thin column of light runs from the dragon's head to it for the whole wind-up, his head glows, and a crackle
  starts it.
- **`FLYEDGE`**: a flyer within 30 m that the lens cannot see puts a chevron on the screen edge pointing at it.
- **The loop it opens**: hits on the mech fill its stun meter and it DROPS to the floor (`cDown`, m974) -- shoot it down, then the blade. Still not
  built, his three ideas, for him to pick: a ninja flip UP to a flyer (the katana's high leap aimed at it), a rope it dangles to climb, mounting it.
- Headless note: the first frame after a new model becomes visible costs ~56 s of shader compile in SwiftShader -- that, not a loop, is what
  "hung" the wall probe (e4) too. Give such a probe 10 minutes.

## The Wall Park, and a run-up you can start from a stride away (m1751)
*"We still need to figure out a bunch of wall riding stuff so maybe some wall riding sandboxes ... definitely need to figure out the wall run."*
- **KORAJIN > The Wall Park** (`?w=forge&zone=wall`, `WPARK` / `wparkBuild`): five stations on the white floor, each colour-coded with a floor
  label. 1 LONG WALL (blue, 24 m, platforms at both ends), 2 TALL WALLS (yellow, 4.5 m with a deck and 7 m), 3 CHIMNEY (green, two 12 m walls
  2.8 m apart), 4 RUN-JUMP-RUN (purple, two walls across a gap), 5 CORNERS (orange, inside and outside).
- **What was measured before any change** (headless, the shipped frame): an UP swipe only started a run-up from within ~.7 m of the face, so
  at a sprint the window was about 0.1 s and a slightly early swipe did nothing. The run-up peaked at 2.1 m (base `upV` 7.2 against `gUp` 12,
  with the into-speed lost on impact). The side run lasted 1.13 s and covered 8.4 m.
- **The fix:** an UP swipe that sees a wall ahead within `WRUN.upReach` (2 m) is QUEUED for `upQ` (.4 s) with the speed he had (`upK` 1.25 x
  his into-speed, capped at `upMax`), and `wrunAuto` fires it when he reaches the face. Measured: the swipe at 1.7 m out queues upV 9.0; the
  run-up fires on contact (vy 8.8), peaks at 2.8 m, the hang catches the lip, and he pulls up onto the 4.5 m deck. The 7 m wall is out of a
  single run-up on purpose (the contrast; the chimney is the way up high).
- **Still open:** the long wall's 24 m is longer than the measured 8.4 m side run -- deliberately, so he can feel where a run gives out; if
  it should be crossable, the run's duration is the knob, not the wall. The e4 probe (several run-ups in one evaluate) hung twice headless;
  a single run measures fine. Nothing in DOCKET 17's dynamics is signed off; this build is the playground plus the first fix.

## The bow at rest, on his diagonal (m1748)
His (a red line drawn on a side view): "when he's just standing idle it doesn't need to be straight up and down -- hold it almost like he holds the
sword, in the middle." Carried, the bow's riser (still through the fist, m1746) now runs along a low DIAGONAL: the top limb up and AHEAD of him at
`carry.ang` .6 rad (~34 deg) above level, the lower limb trailing behind his hip, leaned `carry.out` .18 out from his side; the string faces up,
so the limbs' own curve lifts both ends (the back end flattens as in his line). Renders: both sides, the back, the front, walking.
## Arrows you can SEE and that HIT the targets; the arena no longer opens on a straw post; CINEMA.md (m1747)
His: "with any meaningful amount of speed you can't even see the arrow"; "I was shooting the test dummies -- you hit them with the sword and they
move; with explosive arrows they don't; the arrows don't hit things they're supposed to hit"; "when you start the arena the sparring dummy is the
first thing you see"; and should cutscenes be rendered in Blender or done in game.
- **What the arrows missed**: the straw targets (makiwara) were reached only by the blade (`dojoHit`) and bolts (`dojoShot`); arrows and the blast
  arrow's burst never asked. His arrows now test (per frame, at the head) the straw targets (`dojoTgtHit`: 1, 2 at full draw, 2x for blast), the
  machine (`vendHit`), the turrets (`turretMelee` -- it returned nothing; it returns how many it hit now) and, in the Hollows, `bldHit`. The
  BLAST knocks every straw target in its radius flying (2.5) and hits the machine, the turrets, the Hollows' buildings. Headless: a full-draw
  arrow took a target 3 -> 1 and knocked it (vx 4); a blast beside another took it 3 -> .5.
- **The tracer**: a solid streak behind each of his arrows, as long as the last .06 s of its flight (up to 4 m: a fast arrow draws a long line),
  in its colour lightened, normal-blended (additive vanished on the snow). Gone when it sticks.
- **The arena's first frame**: the four straw targets stood at the compass points at 10 m -- one at (0, 10), between the spawn (0, 8) and the lens
  at z 12.9. Turned 45 degrees; the first frame is Grumbo on the dais (render).
- **CINEMA.md**: the answer is IN GAME (the world changes -- fallen/restored, water, his kit -- and a video does not; portrait and landscape; the
  statue wake and part aim's lens already are cutscene pieces) and a proposal: REELS of shots (orbit, dolly, cut, track, close, back) with a
  title card, letterbox and a skip; place intros first.
## The bow IN his fist, and squared to the aim while he strafes (m1746)
His (screenshots on M1741 -- before m1744's no-second-pull fix had reached his phone): "his hand isn't around the bow like he's gripping it --
the bow is on the outer side of his hand; the angle isn't right from the back"; "it doesn't aim true down the muzzle when moving left or right
-- lined up stationary, but strafing he starts tilting, which he shouldn't."
- **The grip** (`bowFist`): the bow was placed at the WRIST bone (the hand's origin) and m1733 pushed it `out` .07 to his left -- outside the
  hand by construction. Now its riser goes through the centre of his curled fingers (the mean of Middle1-3 and Thumb2). Drawn, the riser runs
  along his knuckles (pinky -> middle) and the belly faces the shot; carried, the knuckle line is blended `carry.up` .75 toward upright.
- **The strafe tilt** (`bowSquare`, before the bow is placed): the strafe legs' hips lean and turn, and the drawn arms rode them off the line.
  The chest's frame (shoulder line, spine up) is turned at `Spine1` onto (aim heading, world up). Measured strafing left-right while drawn:
  chest ROLL 13.0 -> 0.0 deg, tilt 29.5 -> 10.5 deg (what is left is the lower spine's lean, under `Spine1`). `BOW.sq` 0 is the A/B.
- Renders: carried from the back and the side (through the fist), drawn from behind, strafing drawn.
## ROCKS BREAK: big -> chunks -> small -> dust, in every world's own stone (m1745)
His: "rocks in different forms -- the snow world, the red rock world, the grass world, the temples -- different styles of rocks that once
you slash them or shoot them or explode them break from bigger to smaller, placed just like you do plants, to add interaction."
- **In the plant library** (so anything that scatters plants can scatter them): the old `boulder` (mossy, everywhere in the forge) is now
  breakable, and three new kinds -- `rock_snow` (granite, a white cap), `rock_red` (banded sandstone), `rock_temple` (a cut, grooved, mossy
  block) -- which are also SOLID (a box each). `plantFlush` hands each one to `rockInit` (stone = `hp` x its size).
- **`ROCK`**: a blow (`rockHit`, a .22 s guard per rock) takes stone and throws chips, dust and a crack; at 0 the rock's INSTANCE is zeroed
  out of its batch (no new draw), its box goes, and `n` CHUNKS fly from it (3 flat-shaded blob shapes, one material per kind), tumble, bounce
  and settle (`rockStep`). A mid chunk splits into 3 small ones; a small one crumbles to dust. Chunks sink away (45 / 25 s); a broken rock
  grows back after 150 s when he is > 30 m off. Max 80 loose chunks.
- **Hits**: the blade's sweep and bolts (through `plantHit`: 1 stone), blast arrows (3), rockets (3), the whirl (1.5), the slams (2 / 2.5),
  the guardian's smash (3), and arrows (`rockAt` in `arrowStep`: .6, 1.5 at full draw; the arrow shatters on stone).
- **Placed**: the Snowfield -- 31 snow rocks in 9 clusters (SET ON the snow pack, `snowAt` x depth: at y .25 they were buried under up to a
  metre of snow) and 8 fallen temple blocks round the willow's terrace; the Red Hollows -- 39 sandstone rocks in 16 clusters, each on the
  real ground and only where that ground IS the terrain (`groundAt` within .3 of `hwHeight`), off the spawn and Grumbo's home.
- Measured headless: one blow 3 -> 2.16 stone; broken -> 4 chunks, all at rest on the snow in 2.5 s; a mid chunk -> 3 small; a small ->
  dust. Renders: the Snowfield rock before / bursting / settled; a Red Hollows sandstone rock and its red chunks.
- **And the willow's curtain vanished past ~45 m**: its alpha-tested leaf texture was mip-mapped, and the leaves' alpha averaged under .5 in
  the small mips. No mips on that texture now.
## The bow: no second pull, a flight ARC and a ring where it lands, arrows that can be seen (m1744)
His: "once you've initiated a shot and you move the left stick, he keeps pulling the bow back again -- strafe left or right and he pulls it
again; he should never pull it back once it's back"; "the crosshair should show an interaction with what you're aiming at -- it's hard to
see"; "in the Red ... I can't tell where the arrow would land if I released now"; "the arrows get lost in the background".
- **The second pull, MEASURED** (headless: hold the draw, strafe): standing, the draw is the whole-body `bow_draw` (1.07 s, done); the
  moment he moves the gait swaps to its upper half `bow_draw__ups`, which had never been playing -- it started at 0: a second pull. Moving
  forward then stopping did it again (a pose whose weight reaches 0 is STOPPED and rewound by `skinWeights`). `bowSync`, right after
  `rigAnim`: every copy of the draw is put at the DRAW'S OWN time (`bowT` x `drawRate`) each frame. Re-measured: switching between them all
  stays at 1.04-1.07 s. (`check:syntax` wants `rigAnim` within 4 lines above `rig.mixer.update` -- the first placement failed it.)
- **The ARC** (`bowArc`, one Points + a ring): `bowSolve` is now the one answer for the shot (`bowLoose` reads it too), and while he draws
  it is FLOWN in advance sample by sample until it meets the ground (`groundAt`), a wall (`boxRay`), a body / spider / guardian -- the same
  tests the arrow uses. Pips along the path; a RING where it ends, flat on the ground or facing him on a body, AMBER on a body (a hit), jade
  otherwise, tightening as the draw fills. **Not additive**: additive glow vanished on the white forge floor -- solid pips with a dark rim,
  a solid ring over a dark outline. Headless: the ring sat on the dweller's chest, amber, 9 m out.
- **The arrows**: his are x1.35, carry a glow sprite at the head and leave a bright streak (3 sparks a frame along the flight); the glow goes
  out when one sticks. The bow's 2D sight is bigger (54 px), heavier and jade (`#retic.bow`).
- Not done: his HOLD of the bow (the grip and the arm through the limb) still wants the stylised bow model he is making.
## THE SKY CASTLE, pass 5 of 6: the bastion towers and the curtain walls (Worker B)
A round TOWER on every bastion lobe (r <= 3.4, 9-17 m tall -- `(k * 5) % 9`, so no two tops are level), cream stone, banded, eight glowing
arched windows in two rows, a crenellated gallery, a flared red tiled roof (lathe, his tiles) with a gold band, ball and finial. Between
neighbours a crenellated CURTAIN WALL (1.4 m thick, its top a walk: walk tris) along the island's edge -- not across the front, where the
waterfalls run. Towers and walls solid. FOUND IN THE RENDER: every roof was a lathe built at the island's centre and never moved to its
tower -- seven roofs inside the keep and seven gold finials floating over bare towers; `at4(x, 0, z)` on the lathe. 4 draws.
## THE SKY CASTLE, pass 4 of 6: the keep (m1781, Worker B)
His sheet's FRONT and ARCHITECTURE DETAIL. On the plaza: a round HALL (r 10, 8 m, cream stone painted with the stone-block map, a plinth,
crenellations, glowing arched windows round it, a big arched wooden door to the front in a stone arch with gold strap and ring pulls) and
its roof a walkable TERRACE (walk tris); out of it the KEEP (r 4.8, 24 m, banded twice) -- 21 glowing arched windows in three staggered
rows with sills, a timber BALCONY ring under the roof (deck, railing, braces), a flared bell ROOF of red tiles (a lathe; `gcTex('tiles')`,
canvas scallop rows) with a gold band at the eaves, a gold ball and spire on top (~51 m over the plaza), and a red BANNER (`gcTex('banner')`:
gold hem, his white diamond in a diamond, a swallow-tail foot) hung on a gold rod down its front. Hall and keep are solid. 6 draws.
## THE SKY CASTLE, pass 3 of 6: the satellite islets and their shrines (m1778, Worker B)
His sheet: little rocks drift round the castle, each with a pagoda shrine, chained to it. Nine ISLETS (cream rock cones, r 3-6.2) at three
heights (Y0 -22 / -9 / +4) round the island at 1.45-2.2 R; green caps, bushes and ivy; seven carry an octagonal SHRINE -- a stone floor,
eight red posts, two flared red roof tiers with a gold band, a gold ball and finial, a lantern glowing under the roof. Every islet BOBS on
its own phase (`bobPatch` .7 m, the sky islands' swell) -- their own buckets keep `aBob` (7 draws); six hang off the rim on sagging iron
CHAINS (1 draw). Not walkable yet (getting up and across is a later pass).
## THE SKY CASTLE, landmass pass 3: the underside's spires and chained lanterns (m1775, Worker B)
Pass 2 of his six. His sheet's BOTTOM view hangs iron-and-brass spires and chained lanterns under the rock. Seven LANTERN SPIRES: stacked
tiers of dark iron drums with brass bands, discs and rings, glowing lantern cages every few metres (brass cap, a lit glass drum, four iron
bars, a brass bottom and finial), tapering to an iron spike -- the great one (30 m, x2.8) under the island's lowest point, six more (10-24
m) round it -- each hung from the REAL underside (the lowest lobe vertex within 2.2 m of its spot, `under`). And twelve CHAINS swinging a
lantern each from under the rim (a sagging tube, 3-10 m). Iron, brass and glow: 3 draws.
## THE SKY CASTLE, landmass pass 2: the rim and the ivy (m1774, Worker B)
His (after m1769): "run like 6 detail passes in a row". Pass 1 of 6. Every capped lobe's rim (`rims`, its outline turned into the island's

## THE SKY CASTLE, landmass pass 1 (m1769, Worker B)
His (after m1767): "start working on the building / flying island" (BUILDINGS.md THE SKY CASTLE; his sheet in images/korajin/ref/). `GCASTLE`

## The cave beast's detail pass (m1768, Worker B)
His (m1760): "there's like a weird monster in one of the caves that needs a detail pass". It was one squashed sphere, six cones, a sphere
head and a cone tail. Now a sleeping armoured cave SALAMANDER: eleven overlapping body segments (hide painted with the strata map, a pale
belly half-shell under each), bone plates down the spine, seven Jinra CRYSTALS (`hwCrystal`) grown out of its back that breathe with it and
flare when it wakes, four folded legs with three black claws each, a nine-segment tail curling round it with spines, and a head -- neck,
skull, snout, brow ridges, nostrils, swept-up horns with tips, eight teeth, glowing eyes set on the skull's surface -- and a JAW (its own
group, six teeth) that drops open when it wakes; the tail lashes when awake. Merged per material per moving part (~14 draws). The collider
is the body group's measured box. Still open: it does nothing but wake and roar -- no attack, no movement.

His (after m1765, five images): the sky castle is the next hero building -- after "the detail passes and optimization and the logistical

His (after m1763): "those floating lantern things... they just look like tubes, they don't even look like lanterns... make them mystical --

## Red Hollows: side-on collision, the cave chest and crystals, and the first weight cut (m1763, Worker B)
His (m1760 phone shots: in a red rock to the neck, inside the canyon wall, inside a hoodoo stack): "if you land on top of something you
don't go through it, but if you hit it from the side you go through it... stuck in the side of the mountain... stairs, my body goes halfway
through... the treasure chest needs a detail pass and it's 180 degrees the wrong way... plants in the caves look like pyramids... it was
chugging, maybe 20 fps". FOUND: (1) the wall columns are 1.5 m cells topped at their LOWEST corner, so a step carried him into the face,
and (2) the LEDGE GRAB took a column's top edge -- inside the cliff -- as a lip and pulled him up into the rock. Fixes: `hwTerrainOut`
(every frame in the Hollows): the land MESH height at his feet (`hwMeshH`: the same 2 m grid and diagonal as the walk triangles); more than
.45 m over his feet and he is put back on the last spot that was not (the free axis kept, so he slides along the face); skipped in a cave,
on a ladder, a ledge or a mantle. `ledgeFind` ignores terrain columns (`_wc` / `_sc`). The hoodoo stacks were one 2.6 m box under rocks up
to ~5 m wide: each piece is `hwSolid` now. The breakable red rocks' box .7 -> .9 of their radius. Headless walk (`stepPlayer` +
`homeStep`, 60 Hz): at 14 canyon-wall approaches he now stops at the face (the two over 2 m were cave mouths, where the check is off by
design); 0 of 6 rim rocks entered; the peak hike still reaches its top. The mound stairs' walk ramp starts at half a riser, so his feet
stop sinking into the treads. THE CHEST faces the mouth (it faced the wall) and has a detail pass -- painted planks, iron corner brackets,
rims and banded lid, rivets, a brass lock plate and keyhole, feet, spilled coins -- merged per material (5 draws). THE CRYSTALS are
`hwCrystal`: a tapered six-sided prism with an off-centre faceted point, not a cone. WEIGHT, measured from the spawn view: 1.31M triangles
-> 0.88M, 245 -> 239 calls. The worst offender was mine: m1755's detail-2 bushes (200k) -- back to detail 1 with sphere normals (they stay
round); the sky islands' trees detail 3 -> 1 and lobes 3 -> 2; bushes, reeds and cattails no longer cast shadows. Still open: the cave
BEAST's detail pass, the ladder top-out he fell from, and a fuller optimisation pass (171 shader programs, the home's 100k of timber).
## Red Hollows: the ravine walls, the rocks and the mountain are solid (m1759, Worker B)
His (m1751 phone shots, standing on the rim's moss with the cliff through his body): "going through the sides of the ravine, sides of
certain rocks, parts of the mountain -- we need to do some work with the colliders". A heightfield is a surface, not a volume (m1114):
inside a steep face's footprint the terrain is ABOVE him and nothing is under, so he slides in. m1114's columns only covered the canyon
wall BAND (`HOLLOW.floorW/E` .. + wall + 16). Now EVERY 1.5 m cell on the land whose corners differ by more than `HOLLOW.steep` (1.1 m,
~36 deg) gets the same column topped at its lowest corner (6,137 more; the band's 5,597 kept; caves skipped) -- gentle ground has none,
so walking is unchanged, and a too-steep face is a riser he cannot step. The peak's hike is cleared of them (2.6 m round `trailPts`).
And the 40 RIM LUMPS (3-8 m rocks) had NO collider at all: `hwSolid(geo, 1.2, base)` rasters a rock's own triangles onto 1.2 m cells
(height at the cell centre, barycentric) -- 3,904 columns. Headless walk test (`stepPlayer` at 60 Hz, no render): the hike reaches trail
point 69 of 70 at y 61; walking straight at six rim rocks from 12 m, 0 of 6 end up inside one (a low rock's edge can be stepped onto).
All lookups go through `boxesNear` (the grid), so 10k more boxes cost no per-frame scan.

## HAND-BUILT down to a tenth (m1754, Worker B)
His (m1753): "only apply it to one very specific point -- it looks like it's everywhere... just turn it off for now, multiply by .1, it's
so strong and it looks kinda not great". `HWWOB.amp` 7 cm -> 7 mm, under a new key (`mel.wob2`) so a phone that stored 7 cm starts at 7 mm;
TOOLS > HAND-BUILT cycles 7 mm / 7 cm / OFF. Still only the mill's materials. Next, if wanted: a single chosen piece, not a whole building.
## The spout is back, and the dock crosses the river as a bridge (m1753, Worker B)
His (m1752): "you removed the spout -- I did like the spout, a little extra waterfall... incorporate it in the new design"; "you can have
things cross the river like the dock -- just make bridges or make them go up in the air so a canoe could go under them". THE SPOUT: a
timber trough under the arch's roof (its underside 4.8 m over the water, clear of the wheel's top at 4.5), hung on iron rods, fed from a
stone head in the east wall, running UPSTREAM so it pours off its FRONT lip (z -bw - .3) -- the wheel's top moves -z, so the water meets
the paddles going their way; the sheet (`hwFallMat`, runnel then a v0 = 1 m/s arc) skims the wheel's front and lands in a boil in the
stream; it is inside the wheel's x span, so the boat lane beside the wheel stays open. THE DOCK: full length again (z1 = 13) and RAISED --
`dY` = water + 3.1 m; the deck climbs from the bank in .35 m steps (`deckY`; a thin collider on each riser), the T-head sits at that
height with an iron-runged LADDER down to the canoe moored at its end, and no post or brace stands in the boat lane (`lane`: -1..3.2 m
from the river's centre line on the home's side) -- two stringers carry the deck across it. River audit after: 0 points under 3 m (the
dock's z is 8.25 m clear now, the mill arch 4.5).
## The stream is continuous: a boat can go the whole way (m1752, Worker B)
His (m1750): "the stream continuous -- no point in the entire stream that a reasonable size boat could not go through... room where you
could go under the structure, almost like it was built over". MEASURED, not eyeballed: a headless audit walks z -160..160 every .5 m and
finds, across the river, the widest run of cells that are wet (`rwHeight` < sea - .4: a .4 m draft) with no BOX between the water and
sea + 3 (3 m of air). Before: the mill's z 63.5..65 had ZERO (the island filled the river, and the canyon stairs' rail colliders were
each ONE AABB of the whole sloped rail -- 16 m tall, spanning the river: an invisible wall, a bug on land too), and z -2.5 had 2 m (at
x1.4 Grumbo's jetty, T-head and moored canoe reached across the river). Fixes: (1) the mill's island is TWO halves (`CH` 2.5) with the
stream running between them straight through the base's arch (4.8 m wide, ~6 m of headroom); the base's side walls go down into the
water; the wheel hangs against the arch's east wall, its paddles in the stream itself, leaving ~3 m of channel beside it (the m1750
race, intake and kerbs are gone); (2) `wallStair` puts a rail box per tread instead of one per rail; (3) the jetty's length `z1` is cut
back until the T-head's corners stay 2.2 m short of the river's centre line on the home's side (`rv`; it is now about its minimum), and
the canoe is moored at the T-head's end along the bank. After: 0 points under 3 m; the narrowest are the mill arch (4.5) and the dock
(7.5); everywhere else 9.75. Still true and noted: the east canyon stair's flight passes through the mill base and over the channel (its
treads there are 3.2-7.5 m up, so boats clear it) -- a stair to re-route another day.
## The mill runs on the stream, and HAND-BUILT edges (m1750, Worker B)
His (m1749): "the whole idea was it was being powered by the motion of the stream -- weird that the wheel isn't actually in the stream";
"the spout -- the water is flowing off the backside of it"; and "very, very rigid straight lines... is there a way to solve this with a
shader rather than geometry... an erosion shader... make that perfectly generated straight line look a little less perfect". THE MILL:
the chute, its fall, the boil and the pool are gone. The wheel holder is turned 90 deg (axle ACROSS the stream, `wh.rotation.y`) and
lowered .4 m so its bottom paddles dip into a MILL RACE: one water ribbon from a stone intake upstream (z -9.6), through the arch in a
kerbed channel under the wheel, over a lip at z +9.6 and down into the stream (`hwFallMat` with `rep` 5 so streaks keep their size over
a long run; a boil under the paddles, another where it lands, spray). Water +z, and the wheel's existing `rotation.z -=` about the turned
axle pushes the bottom paddles +z, with the water. FALLEN hides the race (`A.water`). HAND-BUILT: a fragment shader cannot move a
silhouette, so it is the vertex shader (`hwWobble`): each vertex is pushed by a smooth noise of its own POSITION (never its normal, so a
box's shared corners move together and nothing tears), and the mill's `vbox` now SUBDIVIDES (~.6 m cells, max 14) so a wall has points to
bend. On the mill's wood, planks, stone and plaster for now. TOOLS > HAND-BUILT cycles 7 cm / 13 cm / OFF (`mel.wob`), live.
## The mill's fall lands in its pool (m1749, Worker B)
His (after m1742): "the watermill's waterfall didn't really look like it was pouring into the stream -- it had a straight line at the
bottom... make the water more watery like you did here". It was still the textured MeshBasic plane ending exactly at the pool's surface
(iy + .05), so its bottom edge drew a ruler line across a flat opaque disc (`0x6fc2d8`). Now: the sheet is `hwFallMat` (the refinery's
streaks, white-blue, `fade` 2 so it never mists out, `bot` 1 for foam churning in its last 15%) and runs .5 m UNDER the surface; a BOIL
(`hwBoilMat`: a soft disc of churning foam rings, 2.2 m) sits on the contact; and the pool is `hwPoolMat` -- rings spreading from where
the water lands, slow drifting streaks, deeper in the middle, a soft rim. The state switch hides the sheet with the rest (`A.fallMesh`).
## The waterfalls: cut out of the island, and water (m1742, Worker B)
His (m1741 screenshot): "make the waterfall actually cut out of the island and have it actually look like water". The refinery's Jinra
fall was a flat 2.2 x 40 m plane at R + .2 running straight down THROUGH the lumpy lobes. `gjFall` now: every island geometry is kept
(`islG`, via `pi`) so the rock in the fall's wedge (+-.16 rad round a = 2.4) is MEASURED -- the lip `r0` is the furthest rock in the top
3 m, and the throw `v0` is the least that clears every rock vertex below by .6 m (a ballistic arc, h = 44 m). The sheet is one ribbon:
a stone-lined RUNNEL across the cap from .55R to the lip (two low walls, two boulders framing the notch), then over the edge and out,
widening 3 -> 8 m. `hwFallMat` draws it: two widths of streak scrolling down at their own speeds, slow in the runnel, foam at the lip
and the edges, the last 45% fading to mist (the sparks follow the arc, mist puffs low). The sky islands' falls take the same material,
white-blue, riding their island's bob in the shader. `HWFALL.t` has one writer (`homeStep`).
## Red Hollows pass: the refinery's cone, the island falls, the doubled stripes (m1741, Worker B)
His (after m1740): "do the next pass and fix some stuff". The refinery island was still an inverted 14-sided CONE under its cap: now a big

every strata rock read WOVEN: the vertex-colour strata bands (`ghStrataCol`) and the painted strata map are two sets of bands that never

## Red Hollows: the tiling lines and the sky islands (m1740, Worker B)
His (m1733 screenshots): "fix some of this texture tiling -- on the rock it looks like lines, and on the cliffs the bluffs, more lines";
"this upside-down triangle cone thing -- those floating islands need to be broken up and made way more organic... shorter... irregular...
lumpy pieces sticking out... different textures". TILING: the rock map is horizontal STRATA, and the triplanar's top projection laid it
flat across every boulder's top as straight parallel lines (the barcode). For 'rock', 'cliff' and 'land' the TOP projection is now the
sand (dust on a ledge); the strata only run round the sides, where strata belong. And every sample goes through `hwTile` (`HW_TILE`): the
coordinate is warped by a slow sin field and a second sample at .37x, offset, is blended in by a broad noise, so the repeats of the cliff
map no longer line up. ISLANDS: the 7-sided cone + cylinder is gone. Each island is 2-5 LOBES (`hwIslLobe`: a noisy sphere, its top nearly
flat, its underside a round taper whose depth varies by angle so it hangs in uneven lumps, never a point), the main one only .6-1.1x its
radius deep; a grass cap cut to each lobe's outline (`hwIslCap`), round trees on top, 1-3 loose rocks hanging under it; alternate islands
are strata rock and red cliff. 5 draws for all nine (two bodies, grass, trees, falls). Render: from the rim, restored.
## THE LIVE TURN: watch the Red Hollows fall or rise, no reload (m1733, Worker B)
His (after m1731): "we need to build a transition between the two so you can actually physically watch one kind of rumble and shake and then
convert into the other one". The STATE button (and GOD > RED HOLLOWS) no longer reloads: `hwAgeLive()` flips `AGE.st` and `hwAgeStep` plays
it. `HWAGE.rumble` (1.8 s): the camera shakes, low thuds, dust bursts round a random place, and every chunk of every chunked place shudders
in place (`AGE.jit`, added to the chunk matrix in `rsChunkSync` and `ghomeRestoreSync` by `ageJit`). Then one boom and all four chunked
places (home, mill, merchant, refinery) play their own RESTORE show at once (`restorePlay`), forwards or backwards; the SKY CROSSFADES
(`rwSkyTo`: the other state's panorama loads into `uPanoB`, `uPanoMix` 0 -> 1 over `HWAGE.sky` 7 s while the sun's direction and the
sun/hemi colours follow, then B becomes A and the reflection map is rebuilt); the sky islands rise 140 m out of the valley or sink into it
(`HWAGE.isl` 9 s); and at `peakAt` the peak's paint floods back or drains (`hwPeakAge`, which keeps each mesh's own material in
`userData.m0` so the weathering can be undone -- `bldAge` alone could not). Everything else that reads the state per frame (the peak
fire, the shutters, the lamps, the wheel, the refinery's colliders) follows by itself. `?hs=` is dropped from the address with
`replaceState` so a reload lands in the state he turned it to. The timings are in `HWAGE`.

His: "a cool alien weeping willow -- a big one, with vines you can actually brush through, like actual chains, so there's a dynamic to it;

## PART AIM: the charge's lock steps between a big thing's parts (m1738)
His: "on bigger enemies -- bosses, big spiders -- the crosshair moves between their different hit points: his elbow, his hand, his face; you
move the cursor around while you hold the charge, so it's more refined what you're going for."
- `partsOf(src)`: a guardian/dweller -> head, chest, every standing arm's HAND and ELBOW (tagged with its arm), the knees; a spider -> the head,
  every walking leg's knee, every stump. The charge's lock (`markStep`) sits on ONE (`p.part`), the marker at x.55, faint pips (up to 12) on
  the rest. The mech proxy now carries its `src` so a lock knows WHAT it is on.
- **Stepping**: `by` 'L' = a FLICK of the left stick (out past .55 and back under .25 inside .35 s) -- because the left stick HELD picks the
  release kind (m1723) and a flick never means that; `by` 'R' = rolling the right thumb along the top of the pad past .5 rad (inside the
  trigger's 1.05 arc, so the charge holds). The step goes to the nearest part in that SCREEN direction (cos > .3, distance x angle penalty).
  TOOLS > PART AIM: LEFT / RIGHT / OFF.
- **The release lands on it**: `partHitAt` overrides the blow's hit point in `guardBlow` / `spiderBlow` while the charge (or its release) is
  live and the part belongs to that creature -- the arm of the chosen hand/elbow, the chosen leg.
- **The lens** (`partCam`, after everything, never writing `cam.pos`): a part well above him backs the camera off by .7 x the height
  and raises it, looking between his chest and the part. The marker is pulled out of the stone by the part's own thickness (`r`), else
  the depth-tested sight sat inside the guardian's arm, unseen (render).
- **A comment ate a declaration**: the first cut put `// m1738` mid-line in `guardBlow` and `spiderBlow`, commenting out `const p = player`
  after it -- `check:boot` cannot see it (it throws only when a blow lands); the headless charge found it at once.
- Headless (an awake guardian at 6.5 m, the katana charged): chest -> flick right -> elbow (arm2L) -> down -> hand -> left -> elbow -> left
  -> knee -> up -> elbow; released: `arm2L` 7 -> 0 and cut, the other three untouched. Renders: the sight on the chest, the elbow, the hand.

## the CAVES: solid floors and walls, and a lens that stays inside (Worker B)
His (m1724 phone): "the walls of the caves don't stop you, you walk through them"; "we need a smart camera that stays within the confines of
the inside of the cave -- right now it goes outside".
- **WHAT WAS WRONG (sim):** the walls DO stop him; what let him through was the FLOOR. The cave floor was only the carved land, and the land
  is a 2 m grid: where a carved vertex meets an uncarved one its triangles slope steeply up into the rock, and at such a point `groundAt`
  returned -1000 though the height said 1.34 -- he dropped through to y .17 at the tunnel/chamber join (x -27.4, z 15) and was then under
  and behind everything. Now each cave lays its OWN FLAT FLOOR in the walk store (`triAdd`, a .8 m grid over its whole volume), and the
  carve runs 2 m past the shell (was 1) so the land's slope is behind the walls. Same sim after: y 1.35 throughout, stopped by the wall.
- **THE LENS (`caveCamFree`, in the camera's `free`):** when the look point is inside a cave, the lens may only go back along its ray as far
  as the cave's own volume (walls in .35, under .95 of the vault, above the floor) -- or out through the open mouth into the canyon.
  Sim: standing 9 m in, the camera turned through five headings: inside every time (3.6-5.2 m back). Render: the shipped camera's frame.
## THINGS THAT FLOAT, FLOAT: the sky islands, the refinery's stepping stones, its island -- and you ride them (Worker B)
His (m1704): "if they're gonna be floating they need some wiggle to them". `bobPatch(mat, amp, speed)` lifts every vertex whose `aBob`
attribute is set (its PHASE, >= 1) by sin(t * speed + phase * 2.3) * amp in the vertex shader, so a merged bucket of many floating things
stays ONE draw and each rides its own swell; `HWBOB.t` is the clock (homeStep), `hwBobY` the same number in JS.
- The sky islands over the rim (restored only): each island (cone, grass top, waterfall) its own phase, 1.4 m, a ~20 s swell.
- The refinery's 14 stepping stones from the lookout: each its own phase, .28 m, ~7 s (`GJINRA.bob` / `bobS`); their COLLIDERS move the
  same way every frame, and standing on one carries him.
- The refinery's island already hovered .28 m (the RESTORE kit) while its colliders stood still -- his feet sank into it and floated
  off it by turns. Its boxes now follow the hover, and carry him too.
Sim (shipped frame, restored, standing still on stone 8 for 6 s): his y tracked the stone's top to the centimetre through a whole swell
(113.79 -> 113.31 -> 113.82), grounded throughout. Render: no shader errors (the shared rock/grass materials take `aBob` = 0 off the stones).

## the Red Hollows: CAVES YOU WALK INTO (Worker B)
His ask (after m1712): "make the caves something you can go in -- a continuous, actual physical hole; little treasures, maybe animals".
All five cave mouths (z -30 W, 18 W, -55 E, 40 E, 95 W) are now caves: a 7 m tunnel (5.2 wide, 3.8 high) opening into a chamber
(12 x 13 m, 5.6 high). How, since the canyon is ONE heightfield:

  so the walk store, the terrain triangles and the wall columns (`colMin` skips them) all follow with nothing special. `caveList`

## m1711 -- ARENA SPEED, THE INTERCEPT YOU EARNED, SWINGS THAT LAND, THE CHARGE SWAP (his arena report, 20 fps)
- **20 fps / chugging -- MEASURED (`?w=arena`, the game camera):** 1,033k triangles rendered and 104 calls.
  - ~900k of the triangles were the PLANTS: one InstancedMesh per kind over the whole world with `frustumCulled = false`, so every blade
    behind the lens and 80 m off was drawn every frame. Tallgrass 214k, frond 119k, grass 101k, shrub 98k, carpet 90k.
  - `plantFlush` now cuts each kind into `PLANT.cell` 32 m squares, each its own mesh with a real bounding sphere (plus a sway margin),
    so the lens culls it. `plantCull` hides small cover past `PLANT.far[kind]` (carpet 22 ... mound 45 m).
  - Result: **220-250k triangles**, 134-138 calls (the cells add calls; 28 m and 40 m cells measured either side of 32).
  - Every world using `plantFlush` gets this. `PLANT.cell = 0` before a load is the old way.
  - Not touched: 258 other arena meshes (164k) that are not merged. That is the next candidate if it still chugs.
- **The intercept still got hit (his: "I'd release at the right time and as I flew through the air the arrows would still hit me"):**
  - `deflStep` catches the locked arrow by a POINT distance once a frame. At 20 fps an arrow covers 1.3 m a frame and can pass between
    two checks, and any OTHER arrow was never covered at all.
  - Now `arrowStep` itself, while `p.inter` / `interHold` / a locked dash is live, CUTS every arrow whose path reaches him (1.1 m, 0.8
    of his height) and sends it back, with the same stop-dead beat.
  - **Not released in time, it still hurts and breaks the charge (m1704)** -- what he asked.
- **Swings that didn't land:**
  - **(a)** The spiders were not in `meleeLock`, so no tracking or lunge to them. They are now proxies in `mechTargets`.
  - **(b)** Their hit radius was the BODY (.38 of the width). Measured through real `meleeGo` swings with the katana: at 60 fps 4 of 5
    landed; **at 20 fps (50 ms frames) 0 of 5** -- the blade passed over a leg just outside the circle. `SPIDER.hitR` is now .48 (the
    leg span): 20 fps lands.
  - **(c)** The spider GUARDED 30% of the time after every stagger, for 1.1 s, so swipe after swipe clanged. Now `guardP` .12, for .5 s,
    or after `guardEvery` 3 hits in a row.
  - Osari bowmen measured fine: the first swing throws them 6-11 m, out of reach of the next.
- **The charge release, swapped (his: "I keep trying to do the lunge and it does the spiral"):** `CHARGE3.swap` 1 -- NEUTRAL lunges
  forward, FORWARD spins, DOWN is still the high leap. `swap 0` is m1688's way.

## m1704 -- A HIT BREAKS THE CHARGE; THE DRAGON SHOOTS LIKE A FIGHTER PLANE
**The charge (his: "when I'm charging up on the right stick and the enemy attacks, it auto-lets-go and I auto attack them -- that's too
easy, you'd charge over and over and never get hurt. If you don't release in time it should just f--- you up. The counter is the parry"):**
- **The cause:** the charge's hold branch needs `!p.knock`, grounded and so on. A blow that stuns or shoves broke those conditions, and the
  NEXT frame fell through to `else if (p.charge) chargeRelease()`. Every hit on a full charge was a free counter.
  It was never the arrow lock (`chLock`), which only acts on a real release.
- **The fix:** in `playerHurt0`, a blow that lands unguarded (dmg or push > 0) on a charge throws the charge away: no swing, a grey fizzle,
  `CHARGEBREAK.n`. A thumb still held starts a new charge from zero.
- **Measured** in the forge with the katana, the right pad held up for 70 frames (full charge):
  - clean release: swing
  - `playerHurt(5)` mid-charge, then release: NO swing in 50 frames, hp 100 -> 95

**The dragon (his: "the same as the normal shot -- press UP on the right stick to start it, let go and it shoots, and AIM WITH THE LEFT
STICK: the aimer is in front of the dragon, shoot like a fighter plane"):**
- m1703's FIRE toggle and thumb-dragged reticle are REMOVED. The right pad is the camera / flap / breath again.
- `dragGun`: right pad pushed UP (`gunUp` .72 inside `gunArc`) for `armT` .1 s COCKS a fireball. It stays cocked down to `gunKeep` .45
  (hysteresis). Dropping below that, or lifting, LOOSES it down his flight line (heading + pitch), grown by hold time to 1.7x.

## m1702 -- NEON GREEN SMOKE (his: "the green smoke has gone kind of dark... I want it glowing, neon, fluorescent. Instead of shades, HUES --
a little more turquoise, a little more slime green-yellow")
- **Why it was dark:** the smoke pool's shader outputs premultiplied colour, and its NormalBlending multiplies by alpha a SECOND time. Every
  puff's colour lands at roughly colour x alpha squared over the background, which greys a coloured puff to murk on white snow. Grey smoke
  hid this; a mid-green (m1697's "shades", .28-.48 / .78-.95) made it obvious.
- **Fix:** a second pool, `gsmoke`, built by the same `puffPool` and stepped by the same `stepSmoke`, blended premultiplied (One,
  OneMinusSrcAlpha). A puff's centre is its own colour at full strength. `smokeAt` takes the pool as an optional last argument.
  Grey smoke is untouched.
- **Colours:** `OSARI.shade` now picks a HUE: neon green 55%, turquoise 25%, slime yellow-green 20%, all at full green. It feeds the kill
  blast and the Osari vanish. The green fire's tail no longer darkens to .55.
- **Checked:** a headless render of a spider burst (bright, no dark core). **Not checked:** on his phone.

## m1701 -- THE SPIDER FIGHTS (his: "animate the spider attacks and hit reactions, maybe a jump and a block -- keep their current size --
let them take damage so I can beat them up, then an explosion of them; have them lose limbs... maybe they spit or shoot at you")
- **All procedural, on the same rig and planted-foot IK as the walk.** An attack moves the feet and body somewhere else for a moment.
  The body's pitch, lift and sag sit on `S.m` (the inner model). The root stays on the ground.
- **BITE** (inside `bite.r` 3.4 m): it rears up with the front pair lifted, then lunges `bite.lunge` 1.3 m with the front feet stabbing
  ahead. At the strike frame, anything within `bite.R` of the point 1.2 m in front of it takes `playerHurt(11)`. A guard blunts it and a
  roll clears it.
- **POUNCE** (7-13 m, 45% of the time): a crouch, then one ballistic arc to 1.4 m short of where he will be, legs tucked. Landing within
  `R`+.6 of him: 14 damage and a big push.
- **SPIT** (5-18 m): the abdomen cocks and a green-fire glob is lobbed at his lead. A direct hit does 8; a splash within 1.1 m does half.
- **GUARD:** after a stagger, a 30% chance (`guardP`) to raise both front legs for ~1 s. A blow on its front is then a clang and no damage.
  A full katana charge goes through it.
- **A BLOW** (sweep, bolt, rocket splash, slam, charged slam, whirl): a green flash (cloned materials' emissive), a knock along the
  blow, the body thrown back, any wind-up cancelled (`stag`).
- **LEGS:** every `cutEvery` 2.2 damage (or every full katana charge), the leg nearest the blow comes off. It is baked out of the skin by
  `limbBake` and thrown, and that leg's first bone shrinks away. The gait carries on without it: with fewer than 4 legs, one leg steps at
  a time. The body sags toward the gap and slows. With `minLegs` (2) left, the next blow bursts it.
- **DEATH** (no hp, or the blow at 2 legs): body, head, abdomen and the remaining legs are each lifted out as pieces (`spiderTris` sorts
  every triangle by its dominant bone once per proto) and thrown in a 1.25x green `killBlast`.
- `hp` 9. Everything is live on `mel`'s SPIDER table. **The SIZE is unchanged**, as he asked.
- **Checked headless** (forge, scripted frames through `frameBody`):
  - The bite took him 100 -> 89.
  - Blows of 1.3: legs 4 -> 3 -> 2, then the next blow burst it into 7 pieces.
  - The spit took 8 (apex 1.78 m).
  - The pounce landed 1.38 m from him and took 14. Its first version computed the flight time apart from gravity and landed 5 m
    short; the time is now `2*up/g`.
- **NOT checked:** any of it on his phone; whether the IK legs read well mid-lunge.

## m1699 -- AUDIO THAT COMES UP EVERY TIME (his: "if I go through the menu quickly and get to a game there's no audio; and if I leave the game and
come back, the audio is muted")
- **No sound after a quick menu:** the first touch built the context and decoded only the files ALREADY fetched. A file landing after that
  first touch was never decoded, so a fast tap through the menu left most of the bank silent for the whole session. Now a file that arrives
  after the context exists is decoded on arrival (`sfxDecode`).
- **Muted after coming back:** iOS can hand the context back reporting `running` while it plays nothing, so m1097's `sfxRevive` (which
  only acts on a context that is not running) saw nothing to fix. Now, once the page has been hidden (`pagehide`, `blur`, hidden
  `visibilitychange`), the NEXT TOUCH throws the context away and rebuilds it from the raw files (`sfxRebuild`) inside that gesture,
  whatever state it claims. Persistent voices (the hum) are rebuilt with it.
- **`sfxUnlock`:** a one-sample silent buffer started inside the gesture, plus a resume -- iOS's own reliable unlock. It runs on every
  build, and on any touch while the context is not running.
- `click` and `keydown` wake it too.
- Not testable headless (no audio device); his phone is the test.

His Tripo zip (`models/creatures/osari_spider.zip`). Auto-Rig Pro's rig is humanoid, so the skeleton is placed from MEASURED geometry
(scratchpad `spider/probe*.py`, `rig.py`):

  (`models/creatures/osari_spider.glb`, 635 KB).

  - when a foot's rest spot under the moving body is `stride` away, its DIAGONAL PAIR steps there (a little ahead), lifted on an arc over

  - every frame the bones go back to rest; each leg is solved by two-bone IK onto the ankle (the foot + the last segment's length up), the
    knee bent up and out, the last segment aimed down at the foot

## FRAME card in the Red Hollows: `TAU is not defined` in `ghomeFish` (Worker B; mine, since home pass 21)
His phone showed the FRAME card in the Red Hollows (stack ending frameBody -> frame). Reproduced headless with a stepped walk on m1667: the
leaping fish (`ghomeFish`, pass 21) used `TAU`, which is local to the BUILDERS, not module scope -- and the fish only leaps when its random
timer comes round (~seconds in), so `check:worlds`' 8 frames never reach it. Every time a fish leapt, the frame threw. Fixed (Math.PI * 2).
A scan of every top-level function for a `TAU` with no local declaration finds no other. Lesson for the boot gate: a throw behind a timer
needs frames, not a boot -- the headless walk (scratchpad `hcrash.mjs`, 1500 stepped frames) found it in one run.

## m1673 -- THE DRAGON FLIES: the lightning dragon's flight on his body, his wings flapping in code (DOCKET 5)
His: *"the fly sequence is not working -- it's him on flat ground going up and coming back down, clipped; it's not a loop, he doesn't even look

wings back; banks, one wing tucked; dynamic tail and wings."*
- **Measured:** both are 3ds Max bipeds. The shared `Bip001` spine / neck / head / legs differ at rest by 0-24 deg; the lightning dragon has
  NO arms, and the blue dragon's wings ARE his arms.
- **`dragFlyLoad`:** when the zone loads him, the lightning dragon's `idle_fly_1` -> `fly_idle`, `fly_fast` -> `fly_fast` and `idle_fly_2`
  are carried onto his body by rotation, rest-corrected per bone (blue rest x mech rest^-1 x mech).

## m1650 -- THE KATANA IN THE SNOW, ACTUALLY FIXED: a shader PROGRAM-CACHE COLLISION (every earlier diagnosis superseded)
His report after m1641: *"the sword blade is there but now the hilt is gone."* Isolated in the page with five boxes in the snowfield, each a
different material: Physical, Lambert, Phong and DoubleSide Standard all drew right, but the plain FrontSide **MeshStandard box came out
TALL and in the wrong place.** The cause: `MeshStandardMaterial.prototype.customProgramCacheKey` returns `'paint:1'` for every Standard
material, and the snow ground's material set its own `onBeforeCompile` (it displaces y from the depth map) WITHOUT its own key. So three
handed the snow's program to every plain Standard material with the same parameters, and the katana's blade and grip had their vertices
pushed to snow height. m1628's "buried", m1634's "mirror" and m1640's DoubleSide all only changed which program got picked; none of them
was the cause.
- Fix: the snow ground gets key `'snowpack'`. The same unkeyed hook was on five more materials, and each now has its own key: the dojo
  banners, the sky whale, the sky manta, the court tufts and the island land. The steel is back to m1634's grey (`0x8e99a7`, metalness
  .72), FrontSide.

## m1644 -- THE SWORD TASSEL (his: *"a little rope off the end of the handle with a fluffy ball on it, like Chinese swords"*)
A red cord off the katana's pommel, a gold bead, and a fluffy red pompom with a ragged fringe. It is a 5-point VERLET chain in world space
(`tasselStep`, `TASSEL`: seg .038 m, gravity, damping 2.2, 6 constraint passes), anchored to the pommel every frame, so it swings with every
cut, roll and jump. Three draws. It only hangs on the PLAYER's katana (`WEAP.worn.katana`), not on the rivals' or the dummies'. The pommel's
geometry carries `userData.tassel`, which is how it is found. If it throws, it switches itself off and the chip says TASSEL THREW.

## m1640 -- THE MISSING BLADE, FOUND THIS TIME: its faces shade as BACK faces (m1628 "buried" and m1634/m1637 "mirror" were both WRONG)
m1637's gunmetal still vanished in a render. So I tested it in the page, swapping the blade's material and nothing else:
- flat red MeshBasic: DRAWS
- green MeshLambert: DRAWS
- red MeshStandard, FrontSide: **INVISIBLE**
- blue MeshStandard, DoubleSide: DRAWS

The plain lit material vanishes even with no toon or paint patch. Under the physical BRDF its faces shade as back faces and blow out to white,
the sky's colour. Lambert doesn't do that, which is why the hilt (cylinders) and the dojo's sunset hid the cause. Fix: `side: DoubleSide` on
`katanaScene`'s steel (108 vertices, free), grey steel `0x6b7683`. Rendered: the blade reads in his hand on the snow, from the side and the front.
**Lesson: when a mesh vanishes, swap its material for Basic, Lambert and Standard in the page before theorising -- three renders settled what
three builds of guessing did not.** (The mega sword is built the same way and may share it; not touched.)

## m1637 -- THE SNOWFIELD'S MISSING BLADE, the real cause: a pure-mirror material (m1628's "buried" was WRONG)
His screenshot after m1628: the hilt and guard plain in his hand, held high, the blade gone -- *"it was always missing, it's still missing."* So it
was never buried. Measured in the page: the blade (`katanaScene`'s `steel`) was `0xd9dee5`, **metalness 1**, roughness .22. A fully metallic
surface has NO diffuse colour of its own -- it is only its reflection -- so on the snowfield, under a white sky with a white environment, the
blade rendered white on white and vanished; in the dojo it reflects the sunset and reads. m1634 tried `0x8e99a7`, metalness .72 -- a render
still lost it, so the blade was forced to flat RED in the page: it drew, full length, in his hand. So it is purely shading. m1637: gunmetal
`0x55606c`, metalness .5, roughness .32, `envMapIntensity` .45 -- dark enough to read against white snow. **m1628's snow-cutting by the held
weapon is REMOVED**: its diagnosis was wrong, and stamping a rim every frame piled the snow into tall spikes beside him.
**Lesson: when the hilt shows and the blade does not, look at the blade's MATERIAL before its position.**

## m1631 -- THE DRAGON RIDE: GRUMBO'S RIDING CLIPS (Forge-baked from his Mixamo library) and THE STRADDLE
His go-ahead on the plan: the library (`colinwillow/retarget-anims`, cloned beside zap, nothing raw committed here) has no riding clips, so a car
seat, edited -- what he did by hand before.
- **The bake**: `tools/agoblin_forge_prof.json` (the goblin profile's layers and adjust, `character` = alien_goblin_game.glb) ->
  `node tools/forge.cjs models/characters/alien_goblin_game.glb tools/agoblin_forge_prof.json models/characters/forged/alien_goblin_game.glb
  --lib ../retarget-anims/library/clips`. It REBUILDS his whole bake, so the profile carries his eight knock clips too (Colin's six from
  colin.glb + `Kip_Up` / `Corkscrew_Kip_Up`) -- **checked bit-identical to the old file, track by track** (max diff 0.000000 on 5 of them, all
  50 tracks). Library clips need `stem` + `name` in a profile entry; with `clip` alone the Forge drops them silently (it said "14 clips" and
  wrote 6 -- caught by reading the output back). .77 MB -> 1.31 MB, fetched only while he is the hero.
- **The clips**: `ride_seat` = Driving (hips still, hands forward: the reins); `ride_on` = Entering_Car 1.6-3.4 s, `inPlace`, x1.4 (1.29 s:
  the swing in and the sit); `ride_off` = Exiting_Car 1.3-3.6 s, `inPlace`, x2 (1.15 s); `ride_gun` = Sitting_Gun_Motion while the gun is held.
  (Measured first: Entering_Car's hips travel 90 units forward at a near-constant height -- a car seat, not a climb -- hence in place and only
  the middle.) The mount and dismount arcs now take the clips' own lengths (`dragClipGo`); `ride_seat` / `ride_gun` are taken off `ONCE` and
  RESET to loop (a ONCE clip that already ran sits paused on its last frame). Each falls back to `driving` / `in_air` without the bake.
- **The straddle** (`dragStraddle`, last in `dragRiderPose`): each thigh AIMED hip-to-knee at `thigh` (.5 out, -.8 down, .32 forward) and
  each shin knee-to-ankle at `shin` (.12 out, -.8 down, -.5 back) in the DRAGON's frame, on top of the clip, blended by `straddle` (0 = the
  clip's car-seat legs). The upper body is the clip's. Directions guessed, not rendered.
**Moves:** nothing ticked (box 2's look). Gates: check ok, zone boot ok. Shipped unverified.

## m1625 -- THE DRAGON RIDE: HIS CONTROL MAP (the right pad jumps and flies, the left pad moves, the camera stays on the right drag)
His: *"Tapping the right stick should have the dragon jump; double tapping has him take flight. If you tap and hold, he kind of jump-flies up
into the air and then slowly comes back down to the ground; double tap, he takes off and is actually flying like RollerGirl. Left stick
controls locomotion on the ground and in the air; right stick still controls the camera."*
- `D.air.mode` is `hop` | `hover` | `fly`. **Right tap** (`dragTapR`, routed from the right pad's tap whenever `p.dragon`): on the ground a
  HOP (`hopV` 10 up, `hopG` 22); off the ground from a hop or a hover it is the TAKE-OFF into the wingsuit flight (`dragFlap` -> `fly`) -- which
  is what makes a double tap "take flight" with no wait on the first tap; in `fly` a beat.
- **Right hold in place** (`dragHoldR`: down and `far` < .3 for `holdT` .25 s -- so neither a drag nor the gun's push UP): the HOVER, rising at
  `riseV` 6 with the wings beating while held (to `hoverMax` 3 s), then sinking at `sinkV` 2.2 back to whatever is under him.
- In `hop` / `hover` the left pad steers as on the ground, gentler (`airSp` 7); in `fly` it is the wingsuit stick as before.
- **Getting off** moved to the LEFT pad's double tap (`dragTapL` -> `dragTap`); the left tap no longer beats the wings.
**Moves:** nothing ticked -- his feel of the new map. Gates: check ok, zone boot ok. Shipped unverified.

katana's meshes sat at .38-.48 m in his hand at rest -- under the surface. Nothing was mis-rendered; the blade was in the snow.

## m1624 -- THE DRAGON RIDE: his first look (m1614 on the phone) -- the saddle, the plates, the lens, the dismount
His (screenshot at M1614 +3, i.e. three builds behind -- the riding, flying and fire are m1618-m1622 and had not reached him): *"When I got on
I'm pretty much in the dragon, can't even see me. The saddle is crooked. The armour kind of cuts into his body (I'll probably model that on
my own, but keep trying). I wasn't able to control him, or make him fly or jump. When I pushed the right stick he just got off again."*

  pose he is dressed in it is not. `dragKit.backQ()`: forward along Spine -> Spine2 as posed, level side to side. Pass 1's saddle (the dojo's
  too) and pass 2's cantle and lames sit on it.
- **The plates cut in**: the neck and tail shells now stand .018 H off the skin top and are wider (1.9 x the half-girth, not 1.5) on a wider
  arc (2.6 rad), so the edges come down outside his flanks instead of into them. His own armour model replaces all of it when he makes one.
- **The lens sat in the saddle**: it pulls back `camPull` 9 m (was 6), lifts `camLift` 1.6 m (was .4) and tips DOWN `camEl` .22 rad more
  (the one writer of `cam.el` picks the dragon's target when mounted), so it looks down onto the rider on his back from behind and above.
- **A push of the right stick threw him off**: a short push and release IS a tap. Getting off is a DOUBLE tap now (`offTap` .45 s; the
  first tap says "tap again"). The flick (fireball) and the held-up gun are untouched.
- The rider's clip choice goes ahead of a worn form's (`morphAnim`) when the skin has `driving`.
**Moves:** nothing ticked -- his look again at the newest build. Gates: check ok, zone boot ok. Shipped unverified.

## m1619 -- THE DRAGON RIDE, build 4: FLYING (DRAGON.md box 4)
- **The model is `wingFly`'s** (RollerGirl's wingsuit) on the beast, in `dragDrive`'s air branch (`B.drive.air = { v, pitch, bank }`): stick X

  it levels (`levelHL`); `v += thrust (cruise - v) - g sin(pitch)`, so a dive gains speed and a climb spends it; under `stall` 8 m/s the nose
  is pulled down whatever is held (no lift). Position integrates along heading and pitch. His root turns `YXZ` (yaw, then pitch about his own
  X, then the bank about his own Z) -- an `XYZ` root would pitch about the WORLD's X once he had turned.

  at its top. Touching one with the nose under .3 he is down and RIDES ON from there (ground riding on a pad keeps no rim -- run off and he
  glides). Below `cloudY` + 8: back to the dais. Getting off is meadow-only ("Land on the meadow to get off").
