  forearm's non-hand children) is AIMED root-to-tip at a fan in his own frame -- outward, swept back by its place in the fan (sorted by how far
  forward its tip rests), a little up -- blended in by `spread` (eased 0 -> 1 with flight), and the whole fan swung about his spine by a beat
  (`flapAmp`) plus a slow glide flutter. Guessed, not measured: no harness here can build his skin. His fly cycle replaces all of it.

## m1615 -- the dojo stops beaming him home off the gates; TOOLS > DOJO FX to find the 20 fps
- **"When I try to go anywhere other than the main dojo it spawns me back in the middle":** the four gate LANDINGS and their BRIDGES were drawn at
  floor height with NO collider -- he stood on the world's invisible floor at y 0, which is exactly what the off-the-edge rule (m1401: past the
  rim, at y < .35 -> beam home) exists to catch. They are real ground now (`safe` boxes), and the rule fires only when nothing real is under his feet.

  and the shadow pass). Not guessed at: **TOOLS > DOJO FX** steps the suspects off cumulatively -- FULL / NO SKY FX (every `bbd` card layer, the
  sun glow, the candles) / NO PLANTS / NO SHADOWS -- live, no reload; the FPS on the chip at each step names the cost. Then the fix is aimed.

  and the spider bots into HORDE.md.

## m1612 -- THE BEACON'S FLOOR IS DISPLACED GEOMETRY (his: "how do displacement maps work in three.js -- geometric or pixel? make this ground not flat")
The answer, for the record: three's `displacementMap` is GEOMETRIC (it moves vertices in the vertex shader, so it needs a dense mesh, and it never
touches collision); `bumpMap` / `normalMap` are PER-PIXEL (lighting only, the silhouette stays flat); parallax mapping is a per-pixel fake depth.
- **Geometric:** the canyon floor (was one .1 m box) is a 2.5 m grid lifted on the CPU into dunes and mounds (`isl3Fbm` + a smaller noise, 0 to ~2.5 m,
  never below the world's floor at 0). It stays FLAT within 3-8 m of the route's LOW pieces (tops under 3.2 m -- a dune cannot reach the rest), so
  no dune fills a gap or buries a slab. **Its triangles are walkable** (`bldTris`, 21,630 of them), so he runs over the bumps, not through them.
- **Per-pixel:** the sandstone's relief (m1600's triplanar bump) carries the cracks the vertices are too far apart for.
- First try flattened within 4-10 m of EVERY route piece: in a narrow canyon that was nearly all of it (no visible dunes). Route check still 63 ok.

## the LADDER REFACTOR, step 5: the hands meet the rungs (Worker B)
He said go on the clip pass. `npm run clips models/characters/zap_02.glb`: `climbing_Ladder` 0.792 s, 20 keys, 38 bones. Then MEASURED on the
shipped hero in the sim (the clip sampled like `mantleCurve`, and the hands' world heights read off the drawn pose while climbing):
- **WHAT WAS WRONG:** the clip's gripping hand falls past him at ~.44 m/s at 1x (one cycle pulls ~.35 m; m189's .73 was zap.glb), and
  the old rate (`speed / ref`, capped at 2.2x) drove the hands at ~.97 m/s while the body rose at 2.3 -- every hand SLID ~1.3 m/s up the
  rails during its grip.
- **NOW (`CLIMB.lock`): THE CLIP'S TIME IS A FUNCTION OF HIS HEIGHT.** `climbCurve` measures the cycle's rise; it is rounded to whole rungs
  of the ladder (`L.rung` {y0, s}; the yard's are .30, my Red Hollows ladders' .34; else `CLIMB.rungS` .30) and phased to the rungs. Still
  = a still pose; no speed can outrun the hands.
- **AND IT CALIBRATES ON THE DRAWN POSE** (`rig.climbFix`): the offline sample read the hands ~.25 m off where they draw, so each hand's real
  grip (its world rise turning to a fall) is measured against the nearest rung and the phase nudged until the pair sit evenly. Sim, ladder
  5 (20 m), after two grips: L +.09, R -.09 m, held for the whole climb. **Both cannot sit on .30 rungs**: on the drawn pose the two hands
  take hold ~.17 m apart; a per-hand warp (cosine bumps per grip) was tried and saturated -- it needed the clip to run backwards. A clip whose
  hands grip a whole rung apart would land both.
- **AND THE SPEED IS NOW THE ANIMATION'S SPEED**: 2.3 m/s would cycle the hands ~6x. TOOLS > CLIMB cycles .9 / 1.4 / 2.3 m/s (`mel.climbspd`),
  **1.4 by default** -- his pick. Ladder 3 (7 m): bottom to standing on top 5.6 s; top back down 5 s.
The feet are not locked (they follow the same phase; not measured against the rungs).
## m1604 -- WALL RUNS START FROM A SWIPE; the run-up's legs out to the wall
His (playing Level 1 v2): *"we need a way to initiate the wall runs so he doesn't just automatically wall run. If you're touching a wall and you swipe
the right stick directionally, he'll run that direction -- hit the wall at an angle and swipe for a horizontal run; straight on, swipe up, he runs up
the wall. If you don't swipe he does the thing where he's perched on the wall, can jump off or slide down -- it gets confused which one you're
trying to do."* And: *"the vertical wall run: his feet more forward, out in front, as if his hips are at 90 degrees, the torso straight up and down,
feet parallel to the wall."*
- **`WRUN.swipe` (1; 0 = the old tap / auto, the A/B):** `wrunTap` no longer starts a run (a tap by a wall is the jump; a tap ON a wall is still the
  wall jump); `wrunAuto` starts NO run by itself, and ANY touch of a tall face in the air is the perch-and-slide (m1372), stick or no stick.
  **`wrunSwipe`**, first in the right pad's flick chain after the board: a tall face within `swipeReach` .7 (or the one he is perched on): flick UP
  = the RUN UP (`upV`, or faster if he hit it fast), LEFT / RIGHT = a SIDE RUN along the face that way (the flick's world heading, `flickH`, onto
  the wall's tangent), DOWN = let go of the perch. No wall in reach: the flick is the strike, unchanged.
- **The run-up pose (`wrunPose`, kind `up`):** both `UpLeg` bones swung `upLeg` 1.35 rad forward about his own right axis (world space, on top of
  the run clip, so the legs keep stepping), and the drawn body held hipY x .82 off the face so the soles land on it; ramps in over .12 s. **The
  first sign was backwards** (headless render: legs swung out BEHIND him, away from the wall); flipped, the render shows the legs level into the
  wall and the torso upright.

## m1600 -- THE DOJO at 20 FPS: 1.62M triangles were grass; the invisible rim; wood and stone stop shining
His: *"20 frames per second... look at the draw calls and the triangles... a roughness map or displacement on the wood and stone, it looks shiny...
an invisible collider, I can't go anywhere, running into and hanging on an invisible thing, maybe left over from the original dojo."*
(His chip: 82 DC, 1,585k tris.)
- **Measured per mesh** (headless, scratchpad `dojoperf.js`; plant meshes are named `plant:<kind>` now): tallgrass 446 x 1,242 tris = **554k**, frond
  265 x 1,092 = 289k, grass 101k, shrub 98k, carpet 90k... = 1.62M, and EVERY plant cast a shadow, so the shadow pass drew all of it again.
  - `plantTube` takes `len` (segments ALONG it; it was always 12): tallgrass blades 4 along x 3 round, lighter seed heads; frond 6 x 4, lighter Jin tips.
    tallgrass 554k -> 214k, frond 289k -> 119k. **Total 1.62M -> 1.11M.**
  - `PLANT.noShadow`: tallgrass, grass, carpet, flowers, frond, stones, sticks, fern, jinbulb cast no shadow (~830k triangles out of the shadow pass).
- **The invisible rim:** 48 boxes 2.8 m wide and **6 m tall**, invisible, at W+.2, their inner face ~2.4 m INSIDE the visible rail, and across the
  four GATES (only the altar gaps were open). So a strip of stone he could see and not reach, gates he could not walk out of onto their bridges
  (m1430 opened the rail there, never the boxes), and 6 m tops to hang from. Now the guard IS the rail: 96 boxes 1.24 m at the rail's radius and
  height (1.15), open at the gates and the altar routes. The weapon racks got their own colliders (the dais is walkable to the rail now).
- **The shine (`triMat` relief):** the merged meshes have no UVs, so a stock bumpMap is impossible. The triplanar sample's brightness is the height;
  its screen derivatives tilt the normal (three's perturbNormalArb, `triBump`), and dark cracks are rougher than faces. ON BY DEFAULT for every
  wood / stone / sandstone / roof / marble map (`o.bump`, 1.4; 0 turns it off) -- so the ship, the home and the beacon get it too. The dojo floor's
  roughness .6 -> .86.

His words (relayed): "we still need to perfect getting onto the ladder and off at the top". Built on the Ladder Yard (step 1).
- **ON FROM THE BOTTOM** (`climbGo` -> `p.climbIn`): the latch rule is unchanged (push INTO the rungs from the FRONT, m170/m207/m1316), but he
  no longer snaps onto the rungs: x/z ease from where he stood over `CLIMB.inT` .22 s while the climb starts.
- **ON FROM THE TOP** (new: `climbTopTry`; there was no way at all -- `climbFind` only latches from the front, and on the top he is on the
  mark's side): standing on the top within `CLIMB.topR` 1.3 m behind the rungs, feet at the top, walking toward the edge (stick . front > .6)
  -> `p.climbDown` over `downT` .8 s: he walks to the edge turning round to face the ladder (0-.4), then lowers and swings in onto the
  rungs with a small outward bulge (.4-1), hands near the lip. `p.climbTop`: that same push AWAY from the wall now means DOWN (it used to
  mean "let go") until his thumb comes back to neutral.
- **OFF AT THE TOP** (`CLIMB.mantle` 1): when his hands reach the lip (root = top - the clip's first hand height, `mantleCurve().H[0]`) and
  he is still pushing up, the climb HANDS OVER to the ledge climb-up -- `stepMantle` with his hands pinned to the lip edge (m1043/m1051's
  `ledge_hang_to_get_up_over_ledge`, its own 1.05 s pull) -- and he comes up over the top onto his feet `topIn` .65 m in (or at his exit
  mark if that is nearer: the narrow ledge). Not pushing: he hangs at the top. `CLIMB.mantle = 0` is m1316's scripted arc (the A/B).
Sim (headless, the shipped `frameBody`, the stick driven): ladder 3 (7 m) bottom -> MOUNT at .4 s -> CLIMB -> OVER at y 5.8 -> standing on
the top .79 m in at 4.0 s; from its top -> TOPIN .8 s -> CLIMB down to the foot; ladders 1 (2 m: the pull from the floor), 6 (turned 45),
11 (the hatch) and 13 (the narrow ledge, now landing on its mark) all go bottom -> over the top. Chip: LAD<OFF|MOUNT|CLIMB|TOPIN|OVER>#n.

## the Red Hollows' sky and water, pass 1: his panorama over the valley, and a stream that flows (Worker B)
His ask: "work on the water shader, and apply the HDR from the other window". Only three 8-bit panoramas are in the repo (no .hdr/.exr);
he picked the dojo's PANO (`textures/sky_sunset_02.webp`) and the stream. `RW_GLSL` gains `uPano/uPanoOn/uPanoOff` and `panoAt(d, lod)`
(the dojo's equirect mapping, `textureLod` on a mipmapped sRGB texture): `skyFull` = the pano (the dome; below the horizon its cloud
sea, no painted sun disc), `skyCol` = the pano at mip 5 in a band just above the horizon (fog and every `rwPatch` material's fogTo),
new `skyRefl` = mip 3 for the water (mip 1.5 read as oil -- the render showed it). `rwPano` (from `rwBuild`, not in the lake style):
the offsets are COMPUTED so the pano's measured sun (u .310, v .638 from the top, the dojo's measurement) lands on the valley sun
(`RW.time.az`, elevation `RW.panoEl` 9 deg -- lower than the painted 18, it is a sunset), uSunCol / sun / hemi tints and the
environment intensity are the dojo's per-pano numbers, IBL by PMREM. TOOLS > HOLLOWS SKY cycles PANO / FIRE / PAINTED (`mel.rwsky`,
`?rwsky=`), PANO the default. Water: `uFlow` (0, .55) m/s in the hollows: the two finer normal layers drift downstream (+z, 1x and
1.6x) and a streak noise stretched along the flow adds foam in the shallows (dep < 1.5). Still a still picture here: whether it reads
as moving water is a phone question. Next on the water: foam rings at the rocks and the pier legs, the mill's pour, depth colour.

## m1584 -- THE X-RAY ONLY WHEN SOMETHING IS IN THE WAY (his: "it just looks like a sphere... things won't even be in front of the camera and they'll be see-through")
What was wrong: the x-ray (`kitCutMat`'s `uKXOn` block, m181 / m1352) thinned every tagged surface inside a 1.6 m world tube round the lens->him
line, ALL THE TIME it was switched on (kit worlds, the forge's buildings). In the open nothing occludes him, but a lamp, a post, a crate beside the
line still fell inside the tube and dithered -- "rendering issues everywhere".
- **Gated by a real occlusion test:** `kitXrayStep` casts three segments, the lens to his shins / chest / head (.35 / .62 / .92 of his height), against
  `BOXES` and `BDYN` (slab test, boxes under his feet ignored). Only when one is cut does `KIT.xrayK` rise to 1 (~.15 s); with none it falls to 0
  (~.4 s), and `xMin` = 1 - (1 - `xrayMin`) x k, so at 0 the shader thins NOTHING. One writer for `xMin`: this function.
- **A cone, not a tube:** the thinned region is .95 m round the line at HIS depth, shrinking toward the lens (`max(kxt, .3)`), and only for
  fragments at least .6 m nearer than him (was .35). What stands beside him stays solid.
- Colliders stand in for the visible occluder: a mesh with no box (pure decor) will not trigger it by itself. If he sees one, that is the next note.

## m1559 -- The First Beacon on HIS SHEET's layout (his third sheet, `beacon_grid.jpg`)
His: *"these don't really look the same -- is it hard for you to draw in reference from this photo?"*, then a sheet with a metre grid. The first two
sheets had no scale, so pass 1 took only the blueprint's heights and let each station land wherever its run arrived. This one has a grid, so:
- **`BEACON.sheet`:** the stations at the sheet's (x, z) and its heights; `beaconBuild` FITS each run between two of them: an L (the longer axis
  first unless `first`), a corner pad at the bend, the pieces in order (each piece's length found by a DRY run of the chunk function), a leg's slack
  filled by `beaconFill` with safe 3.5 m HOPS and even walks (never a bare 50 m walkway), and a run that cannot fit reported `SHORT` (the station
  then moves to where it arrives). New pieces: `ledge:H` (jump or double-jump catch, capped at the double's 4.3) and `drop:D`, so every height is
  the sheet's exactly: **S 0 | A 9 | B 4 | C 24 | D 28 | Z 14 | brazier 39.6**.
- **The sheet is ~2/3 of the size the moves need:** at 1.0, S->A, B->C and C->D came up 16, 6 and 11 m SHORT. `sheet.k` = 1.5 fits all of them
  (SA 58 m for 43 of pieces, BC 59/41, CD 36/21...). No jump was shrunk to fit.
- **The sheet's x is MIRRORED into the world:** +X is his LEFT (CLAUDE.md), so facing north the sheet's east has to be -x. The first top-down render
  came out mirrored against the sheet; flipped.
- The sheet's zip runs into the tower from 14 m, which no zip can do (they only go down), so: zip D -> a ZIP LANDING east at 14 m (`Z`), then the
  finale climb to the brazier. The old `plan` / `aim` / `go:` steering stays for reference but the build reads `sheet`.

## Grumbo's home, pass 30: breakable pots (Worker B, loop tick 7)
His queue item. Main's `smashAdd` is one Mesh per prop and is stepped only `inArena()`, so the home does its own, with no new draws: `pot()`
remembers its material and its index in that material's MG list; `ghomePotsDone` (after the merge) turns that into a vertex range of the
merged mesh (non-indexed, merged in order, so i0 = the counts before it) and keeps a copy of its positions. `ghomePotHit` (first thing
after the bells in `ghomeHit`, local frame like the orb) folds the range to the pot's middle, bursts clay in its own colour, thuds and
cracks, and pulls its box (only pots r > .32 have one). `ghomePots` puts it back after `GHOME.potFix` 25 s unless he is on the spot. The
ranges sit in the chunked buckets, so a pot on a fallen stall breaks where the stall is drawn (it carries its chunk attribute).
145 pots. Render: restored, right stall's shelf pots every other one smashed. Next: the rocks' 3rd pass.

## Grumbo's home pass 27 (Worker B): the restoration's colour, its bursts and its motes
- Pass 26's colour flood was faint: `restoreMat` tints a material's colour, and over still-saturated maps a tint barely shows. Every home material's shader now also takes **`uDrain`** (`GHOME.drain`) after `color_fragment`, the recipe of main's AGE: pulled 78% to its own luminance with a dust tint, darkened 20%. `uDrain = 1 - rsEase((t - .15) / .6)`, the kit's own colour curve. The rust colours went milder (35% to dust, x .85), because the drain does the work. Rendered headless: FALLEN is a dusty grey-brown ruin (pier and plants too); RESTORED is the full colour.
- **Landings**: as each chunk's own progress passes .985 on the way up, a mint `spkBurst` at its pivot, a thud, a small shake. It re-arms below .5. On a RESTORED start every piece is marked landed, so nothing bursts at load.

## Grumbo's home pass 26 (Worker B): the RESTORATION, live -- one set of pieces, fallen to restored on a plate
- His (relayed, and here): *"the opposite of fallen... the same pieces, so we can animate it... pieces moving in and fixing themselves"*, then the correction: *"not every building flies... the ground will be flying"*. Most buildings REVIVE in place, chunks of earth lift, ship-like buildings fly. So the home revives in place.
- **Chunks by vertex attribute, so the merges stay.** `put` tags every piece with `aChunk` (0 to 9, by where its bounding-box middle lands: `A.chunkOf`) and grows that chunk's bounds. Every home material gets an `onBeforeCompile` (its own kept: triplanar, wind, sway) that moves `transformed` and `objectNormal` by `uCh[aChunk]`. **Still 35 draws.** Chunk 0 (the mound, rocks, plants, paths, pier) never moves.
- **Main's RESTORE kit drives it.** `ghomeRestoreRig` makes one stand-in `Object3D` per chunk at its bottom-centre pivot (the RESTORED pose) and gives each a FALLEN pose with `restorePiece`:
  - the crown drops 3.4 m and tilts;
  - the turret topples 6 m with a 0.4-rad roll;
  - the stalls cave forward;
  - the front frame falls flat forward;
  - the crane falls over;
  - the hall, tower and store settle and lean.
  `at` staggers them in order. `ghomeRestoreSync` copies `T(stand-in) R(stand-in) T(-pivot)` into `uCh` every frame (from `ghomeSmoke`, which `homeStep` calls). Every material is `restoreMat`ed with a rust (metal to 0x6e4632, the rest pulled 70% to 0x6a5a4a, x .75). The kit's `R.g` is a scene-less group, so its lift (0) and hover never move him.
- **The plate**: a mint disc on the front path (local (3.2, 8.4)) is the rig's `R.trig`. Step on it and the show plays (8 s). Step again and he falls. The fires, lanterns and smoke come on only once he is whole (t > .95). The orb and its cable hide while fallen.
- **Start state** from AGE (`hsF()`: FALLEN unless RESTORED was chosen); `?hs=` for a look. The home is no longer `bldAge`-weathered; the rig owns his colour. Rendered headless at t 0 / .45 / 1: a slumped ruin, pieces in flight, whole.
- **Not yet**: the colour flood is faint (a tint over still-saturated maps), colliders stay in the RESTORED pose, no Jinra burst or sound in the show beyond the kit's own. Those are pass 27.

## Grumbo's home pass 24 (Worker B): the pier and canoe, third pass -- and m1442 threw every frame
- **m1442 WAS BROKEN IN THE HOME.** In pass 23 I appended a `//` comment to `function ghomeTumble(dt) {`, a one-line function, so its whole body was commented out. The next line's code then used `T` undeclared, `homeStep` threw `ReferenceError: T is not defined` on every frame, and `npm run check` passed it: the gate builds the home but never steps a frame. A stepped headless frame (this pass's canoe test) found it. **Fixed here.** This is the THIRD time this session that a comment appended to a one-line statement swallowed code (pass 9's orb sway, pass 23's lantern line, this). **Rule for this file: never append `//` to a line that is a whole statement or block; put the comment on its own line above.**
- **Fish.** Slim (.022 x h x .075), a flattened tail, an eye. They read as fish instead of pods.
- **Canopy.** Red awning cloth over the T-head's shore half on four posts (`awning`, so it is also walkable), sloping toward the water.
- **Net.** A 9 x 6 cord mesh draped over the rail between two posts, sagging and bellied, with red floats along the top.
- **The canoe lifts** (`C.hu`). Every 18-38 s it rises .5 m over 1.4 s, holds, and settles over 1.2 s: 6 s in all. The waves fade out of its bob while it is up. Drips fall from the hull. The runes go up to x5 brightness. A splash and a thud when it lands.
- Draws 35, walkable tris 5,868 (the canopy).
## Grumbo's home pass 23 (Worker B): the plants, second pass -- wind, grass, gravel, a tumbleweed
- **Sway.** `put` writes a `sway` attribute (each vertex's height above its own piece's lowest point) for any material with `userData.sway`. The grass (`straw`) and the reeds (`reedM`) bend in the vertex shader on `uWind` (two sines in x, one in z, scaled by sway^1.5). **The flag must be set before the first piece goes in.** Pass 20 had already put grass by the time pass 23 marked the material, the bucket mixed attribute sets, and `mergeGeometries` returned null ("a bucket would not merge"). It is set where the materials are made.
- **More grass**: 70 drifts of 4-8 tufts, bigger (1-1.7x). **Gravel**: 26 patches of 14 sandstone chips in `rockM`.
- **Tumbleweed** (`GHOME.tumble`, `ghomeTumble`): 26 random-walk tubes merged into one ball (one mesh, one draw). Every 8-20 s it comes in from local +x and rolls along the beach strip between the shop and the water (z 9.8-10.6), hopping at random and always over the pier's foot (|x| < 3.2).
- **A syntax slip, caught by `check` before the push:** two `//` comments put inside a one-line statement commented out the rest of it. That is the CLAUDE.md landmine about comments, and it cost one render.
## Grumbo's home pass 22 (Worker B): the rocks, second pass -- desert sandstone
- The rocks were in `stoneM`, the HOUSE's cream-and-lavender sandstone, so they read as more house. They now have their own `rockM` (vertex colours, no map; the repo's textures are all building materials).
- **`ghStrata(x, y, z, nx, ny, nz)`**, linear colour. Bands by height (y * 4.2, warped by noise, six-colour rust / ochre / cream palette, soft edges), so the layers stay level across neighbouring rocks. Dark VARNISH streaks (noise stretched down y) where the face is steep (ny < .5). Bleached tops above ny .8. A fine speckle. `put` calls `ghStrataCol` for any material with `userData.strata`. `hollowDress`'s boulders, hoodoos and rim lumps use it in place of one flat colour per rock.
- **First try was too pale and too wide:** bands every 0.6 m on rocks about a metre tall, in colours close to the sand, so the rocks vanished into the floor. Now bands are every .24 m and the palette is darker. The home's rocks still read soft: that is the third pass's job (more contrast, chipped edges).
- One new material: **35 draws**.

## THE RESTORATION KIT AND ITS DEMO -- ONE SET OF PIECES, A CINEMATIC LIFT (m1505)
*"When we say fallen... the opposite of fallen is literally lifted into the air, floating on jets. It can't be one or the other -- it has to be made of essentially the same pieces so we can animate it going up into the air, lighting, illuminating, moving in and fixing itself. Very cinematic. The transformation is going to be huge."*
- **`RESTORE`, the shared kit (KORAJIN.md THE TRANSFORMATION):**
  - `restoreRig(group, { lift, dur })`
  - `restorePiece(R, mesh, { p, r, hop }, at)`: the mesh's own transform is the RESTORED pose; `p`/`r` are its FALLEN pose in the same frame; `at` staggers it in the show
  - `restoreMat(R, mat, rust)`: the colour floods from rust and the emissive comes on
  - `R.jets`: they ignite and pour mint sparks
  - `restoreSet(R, t)` / `restorePlay(R, goal)` / `restoreStep(dt)`: `restoreStep` is called every frame
- **The timeline (t 0 to 1, `dur` 7 s):**
  - the pieces fly home between t 0 and 1 by `at`: lerp with a back-ease SNAP, an arc `hop`, a slerped turn
  - the colour floods over .15-.75
  - the jets ignite at .3-.5
  - the base heaves free at .45 (a shake, a thud, dust) and rises `lift` m by 1
  - then it hovers and bobs
  - Falling runs at 1.8x with the mirrored dust.
- **The demo (SPAWN > BUILDINGS > Restoration Demo, forge (-180, 120)):** a hero-kit shrine of 23 moving pieces: an island base, a stone floor, 4 posts, 4 walls with red bands, 2 roof halves, a ridge, a finial, a lantern, a banner, 4 bronze jet pods with mint flames. Its own materials, so the rust flood is per building. Step on the MINT PLATE to raise it; step again to drop it. `mel.restoreSet(mel.RESTORE.on.R, t)` poses it.
- **Rendered at t 0 / .35 / .6 / 1:** scattered rusted pieces, then mid-flight, then assembled with the roof landing, then floating on four jets. The first try had the roof halves pitched inward (the x-rotation sign); fixed.
- **Not built yet:** a camera move for the moment (the shake is it for now); colliders that ride the lift (he can't stand on it in the air yet); cracks that heal (the pieces are whole).

## THE DOJO, PASS 16: CLOUD BANKS, NOT COTTON BALLS (m1465)

- **The cloud shader shades by height in the BANK:** `(vWy - base) / bankH`, plus a little noise. The whole bank goes from a dark, FLAT base (fragments below the base fade out) to lit tops, so it reads as one mass.

## THE HOME GATE STEPS FRAMES NOW (m1444)
Worker B, m1442: *"homeStep threw a ReferenceError on every frame and the gate passed it -- it builds the home but never steps a frame."*
- **`MEL_WORLD=home` now steps frames.** After `buildHome()` it steps 8 frames: `frameBody()`, then `homeStep(1/60)` directly. homeStep sits behind `rig.ready`, which never comes in node, so frameBody alone does not reach it.
- **`ctxRender` is stubbed** inside the hook, because the boot stub's renderer has no `info.memory`. We are gating the frame's logic, not the GPU.
- **Proven:** a planted `undefinedThing.x` in homeStep gives BOOT FAIL `ReferenceError`; without it, boot ok.

## THE BOOT GATE NEVER BUILT A WORLD PAST `init()`'s AWAITS -- NOW IT BUILDS THE HOME (m1427)
Worker B (m1424): *"`MEL_WORLD=home node tools/boot.mjs` printed boot ok while ghomeBuild was throwing."* There were two holes, and the second was bigger:
- **The throw is caught.** `buildHome` logs `HOME BUILD THREW` and carries on. Now every logged line containing THREW fails the gate.
- **The builder was never reached.** `init()` awaits asset loads that never resolve in node, so this gate only ever evaluated MODULE-SCOPE code. That is how it caught the arena's BDYN (m1401), and why it could not see the home. `MEL_WORLD=home` now appends `globalThis.__bootWorld = () => buildHome()` to the module and awaits it (capped at 4 s).
- **Proven:** a planted `throw` in the ghomeBuild try gives BOOT FAIL `logged: [melee] HOME BUILD THREW`; without it, boot ok, and the home reports 26 draws.
- `check:worlds` boots the home too now. **A world whose builder sits behind an await needs its own `__bootWorld` line** -- add one when a world's build starts to matter.

## THE PLANT LIBRARY, PASS 1: A SHARED KIT THAT SWAYS AND TAKES A HIT (m1425)
*"Plants of various sizes and styles that are dynamic, move, flow in the wind, but you can also kinda hit them."* PROPS.md is the program (families, sandboxes, ten passes each).
- **`PLANTK`:** eight types, each with `make()` returning parts built by `plantPart(geo, col, sw, fl, gl)`. `col` can be a hex, an [r,g,b] array or fn(x,y,z). The array case was missed at first and the Jin bulb drew BLACK.
- **One InstancedMesh per kind** on the one `plantMat()`. Wind: an offset in WORLD space mapped into instance-local space with `transpose(mat3(instanceMatrix)) / scale^2`, so a turned plant still leans downwind.
- **`iB` per instance:** bend x/z, phase, stiffness. `plantStep` runs a spring per plant (k 34, damp 3.2) and writes only the moving ones.
- **The hooks:** `plantHit` from the katana's sweep (before the inArena branch) and from the top of `bldHit` (bolts and rockets; it never returns 1). The brush is his velocity when he is inside a plant's `r`.
- **Colour rule:** the saguaro and the agave started near Jin mint and were pulled to sage and olive. Mint is the Jin's alone (KORAJIN.md).
- `mel.PLANT`, `mel.plantLibBuild()`, `mel.plantHit(x, y, z, r)`. The library is at (200, 120) in the forge; building it puts him at its entrance.

## THE DOJO, PASS 8: THE ATMOSPHERE -- CLOUDS, GOD RAYS, SKY LANTERNS, FAIRY FLECKS, SUN, BROKEN FOG (m1419)
*"Big fluffy clouds, god rays, those floating lanterns, little fairy glowing flecks, a nice sun, a subtle glowing fog... moody, a sunset vibe... with an opacity texture so it's broken up, not 100% one linear section of fog; it has values to it."*
- **`bbd(list, {frag, move, aspect, add, order})`** inside dojoBuild: ONE instanced camera-facing card per layer (`iC` = centre + size, `iS` = seed). The look is in the fragment shader and the drift is in `move` (vertex). Five layers, five draws.
- **Clouds:** 16 cumulus banks at r 170-400, 9-16 puffs each, big at the base and piling up. The edges are eaten by fbm, warm on top and toward the sun, lavender in the shade, fading to the horizon colour.
- **Fog:** 46 wide cards low round the dojo and islands. The alpha is the product of two fbm octaves drifting in time, so the fog breaks into wisps and banks with VALUES. It glows peach toward the sun and lavender away, and fades out within 14-40 m of the eye so it never sits on the fight.
- **Sky lanterns:** 70 at r 34-154, rising (wrapping at 70 m) and drifting, a flickering flame at the base and a halo. They fade within 6-18 m of the camera, because a lantern rising past the lens is a big flat yellow block.
- **Fairy flecks:** 260 additive motes over the floor (r < 40, y .4-9.4), gold and some cyan, twinkling.
- **God rays:** 7 open cones along the sun vector, merged and additive. A view-facing edge falloff, faded at both ends, slow streaks. The first try at .16 was invisible; it is .3 now.
- **Sun:** an additive radial-gradient sprite (320 m) kept on the sun line, 700 m from the camera (`D.sunG`).

  and rebuilds every building that stands.

  roughness 1, metal mostly gone, every emissive dead; a basic (glow) material drops to 22%; Points hide. The wrapper calls the source's own
  `onBeforeCompile` first, so `triMat`'s triplanar survives, and takes its own program key (`...AGE` / `...AGEm`). Instanced plants are left alone.
  A tint alone was measured first and barely read on the painted maps: multiplying a colour cannot desaturate a texture.

## THE SHIP AS A MODEL: `shipModel()` FOR THE DOJO (m1469, WORKER A)

His (relayed by the dojo session, then confirmed here: *"Yes"*): the ship flying slowly round the dojo islands in the arena, close enough to
jump aboard. The dojo session owns the placing, the flight and the moving deck; this build only makes the ship reusable.

- `shipBuild` is split. **`shipMake(vis)`** is the whole build into a Group at the origin facing +Z and returns `{ g, O, tris, climbs, rings,
  gulls, coreM, flags, sparkAt, chimney }`; `shipBuild` calls `shipMake(0)` and does what it always did (scene, `bldTris`, BOXES, `boxGrid`,
  `SHIPZ.on`, the fish/whale/serpent, `bldXrayTag`, spawn). **`shipModel(opts)`** calls `shipMake(1)`, which registers NOTHING: no
  `kitClimbAdd` (ladder, hatch, the three sails), no `gringAdd`, no `smashAdd` (the barrels are still drawn), no gulls, no `SHIPZ.engHalo`.
  It returns `{ g, deckY, deck: every solid box in the group's LOCAL frame (165), tris: the ramps' walkable triangles, local (54 floats),
  flags, coreM, step(dt, t) }`. `step` runs the cloth and the core's pulse.
- **`triMat` GAINED A `local` OPTION** (object-space triplanar, its own program key `tri<scale>L`). World-space triplanar on a MOVING model makes
  the wood grain crawl across it. Inside `shipMake`, `triMat` is a local wrapper that adds `local` only when `vis` is set, and `triMatG` is the
  real one. The sea ship is unchanged (its ship-local and world frames coincide anyway).
- **`hwBanner` caches on itself, not on `HOLLOW`.** Measured: calling `shipModel()` at module scope right after `arenaStage()` threw
  `Cannot access 'HOLLOW' before initialization` (a blank page), because `HOLLOW` is declared ~40,000 lines below. With the cache moved, a
  temporary module-scope call in `?w=arena` boots clean, and the ship renders over the islands textured (165 deck boxes, 54 tri floats, 72
  children). The sea ship still boots onto its deck with its 7 climbs.
- **Open (the dojo's side):** placing it, flying it, the deck as moving boxes. No airship form exists yet (no wings or sails out). Not signed off.

His: *"I'm not in love... it feels little and sneaky like a snake, kind of sharp. More Chinese dragon, more alien, more big and exaggerated
features. I don't want it to feel scary at all -- inviting, but not cartoony."*

- **THE HEAD, REDONE** (scaled x1.7, so it is now well wider than the neck): a big ROUND skull (1.68 half-width at the cheeks) over a short
  BROAD snout with a bulbous NOSE (two round nostril lobes), the snout tip now closed (the old loft ended in an open ring that read as a white
  disc). The mouth sits closed in a soft line, opening only a little as it breathes, with TWO small blunt fangs (no rows of teeth). BIG
  forward-set EYES (0.5 discs turned .85 rad forward) with a new painted eye (a large ROUND pupil, amber-to-turquoise iris, two highlights;
  the slit pupil read as sneaky) under relaxed LIDS (a squashed skin cap) that BLINK every 2.5-6.5 s. Deer ANTLERS (a beam and two tines a
  side) with GLOWING tips, which are the alien touch, and glowing tips on the WHISKERS too. Long drooping whiskers that SWAY, bushy fin BROWS,
  big cheek frills, a six-lock MANE round the back of the head and a three-lock BEARD under the jaw.
- **SILKY FINS:** `serpent_fin.webp` regenerated as a soft scalloped koi-like membrane, coral at the root to peach-gold and pale turquoise at
  the tips (transparent, cropped to a solid root). The torn red one read as aggressive.
- **BIGGER:** the body radius is x1.25, the dorsal fin taller, and the rear lifts the head to 11.5 m.
- **IT LOOKS AT YOU:** while rearing, the head turns toward the player (80% at full rear) and tips slightly down, as if curious.
- Measured headless: in the first cut the head read SMALL beside the neck at x1.0, so it is x1.7; the whiskers stuck straight out like cat
  whiskers, so they droop now. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP, PASS 12d: THE SEA DRAGON, FROM HIS REFERENCE SHEET (m1448, WORKER A)

His (a concept sheet: a horned sea dragon, mosaic scales, cream belly, torn red-orange fins, rearing out of the sea): *"you could use
this to create the sea dragon monster thing."* The serpent becomes that dragon:

- **TEXTURES FROM HIS SHEET:** `images/serpent_skin.webp` regenerated through the images EDITS endpoint with his sheet as the input image
  (`gpt-image-1.5`): purple-blue spine with a row of orange scutes at the top, teal/green/violet mosaic scales with orange flecks, cream
  ribbed belly plates at the bottom. `serpent_fin.webp` is a TRANSPARENT torn membrane (dark spines, red-orange fading to gold, holes),
  cropped from the band the model drew it in to a solid root, and used with `alphaTest` .4 (no sorting, crisp tatters). The eye is the
  pass 12c iris re-hued GOLD. `serpent_glow.webp` is DELETED (the new skin has no lateral line).
- **THE BODY:** 120 rings (54 m), thicker (1.7 m at the shoulders), arches every 18 m at +/-3.4. The dorsal ribbon is ~2 m tall and leans
  back, and the fin map's torn top edge is its silhouette.
- **THE HEAD** (scaled x1.3): a broad blunt snout with NOSTRIL bumps and a ridge of four nose spikes, a heavy BROW over each eye, upper and
  lower FANGS among rows of teeth, a red PALATE and TONGUE (`mouthM`) inside the open jaw, main horns swept back and cheek horns, long
  whiskers, three chin tendrils, and torn fins at the cheeks, on the crest and under the jaw. `shipFan` is now a ribbon from an inner row
  to the edge (it was a fan of triangles from one root vertex, which smeared the fin map into zigzag stars).
- **THE REAR**, the sheet's pose: once the head is near the surface, every 14-24 s for 7.5 s, the first 17% of the body is pulled in over its
  base (to 22% of its spread) and lifted on a QUARTER SINE to 9.2 m, so the neck climbs VERTICALLY out of the water and arrives LEVEL at the
  head. A burst of spray at the base. The jaw opens wider while it is up. Frames are now built from the BENT positions with PARALLEL
  TRANSPORT from the head back (not from the path's tangent and world up, which flips on a vertical neck), so the upright neck keeps its
  dorsal fin at the back and its cream belly to the front, like the sheet.
- **Measured headless:** the first rear pointed the head straight UP (forward y .95): the lift was blended by `w` as well as `R`, so
  the top of the neck stayed steep. Blended by `R` only, forward reads y .23 and the head is level. The first horns were 3.4 m white tusks
  standing up out of the water; they are thinner, swept back and tinted.
- `mel.SHIPZ.on.serpent`: `rearT = 7.5` rears it now (if the head is up); `rear` is the live 0..1. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP, PASS 12c: THE SERPENT IN PAINTED TEXTURES (m1439, WORKER A)

His: *"We might need custom textures."* Four generated, hand-painted textures in `images/` (OpenAI images API: `gpt-image-2` returned
"upstream request failed" every time, at `high` and `medium` quality; `gpt-image-1.5` at `auto` worked; `gpt-image-1` no longer exists):

- `serpent_skin.webp` (1024^2, 252 KB): the serpent UNROLLED, spine with bony scutes at the top, iridescent teal scales with a lateral
  line of cyan dots, cream-gold belly plates at the bottom. Made seamless left-right (roll by half, cross-fade the old centre over the
  seam). **UV: u = metres along the body / 3.5, v = .5 + .5 * sin(angle)**, so the top of the image is the back and the bottom the belly
  on both flanks (mirrored), on the body tube AND the head/jaw lofts. Vertex colour is now white except for a .78 band shade along the back.
- `serpent_glow.webp`: the lateral-line DOTS lifted out of the skin (the brightest row between 38% and 49% down, found by counting
  bright pixels; a first wider band also caught scale highlights) into an emissive map, so the dots glow exactly where the paint has them.
- `serpent_fin.webp`: a spined membrane, 8 spines a tile, laid one per 6 body rings and one per ray on the fans. The canvas fin is
  kept only as a grey-gradient ALPHA map (opaque at the root, thinner at the tip).
- `serpent_eye.webp`: a slit-pupil iris on a flat disc in the socket ring. A hemisphere eye showed mostly its dark border, and the disc
  maps the picture exactly.
- Tapers sample the paint at a fixed v: the horns take the gold belly plates (banded), the whiskers the teal scales (`tv` .7); every
  tooth's uv is pinned to the belly, so the teeth read cream-gold instead of striped.
- `images/` is already in `bump.mjs`'s `DIRS` and `.webp` is in `EXT`: all four are hashed (`grep serpent_ index.html` in `ASSETS`).
- **Moves:** the serpent. **Open:** no mouth interior colour any more (the jaw lofts are skin-painted), and nothing reacts to it. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP, PASS 12b: THE SERPENT REBUILT -- ONE SKIN, A REAL HEAD (m1433, WORKER A)

His: *"Do a pass on the monster, it's pretty ugly, low quality lol -- we need like 600,000 passes."* m1416's serpent was 44 instanced
ellipsoids, triangle fins and a head of stacked primitives. All replaced (the path `shipSerpentP` is kept, so it still loops the ship and
the arches still stand still in the sea):

- **ONE CONTINUOUS SKIN:** a 110-ring x 20-side tube rewritten every frame along the path (positions AND analytic normals, no
  `computeVertexNormals` on the body), its cross-section a keeled back over a flattened belly, rolling slightly into its weave, with a
  breathing pulse. Static vertex colours (dark back with bands, teal flanks, cream belly) under a painted SCALE map (canvas, overlapping
  shaded scales) and a glowing lateral line drawn in the EMISSIVE map, so the photophores cost no meshes at all.
- **A REAL MEMBRANE:** one ribbon down the back (a spine every 6 rings, scalloped edge, swept back, rippling), a ventral ribbon on the
  last third, and both grow into a TAIL FAN at the end. Its texture is a gradient membrane with a dark spine and fainter rays.
  Pectoral FANS behind the head flap.
- **A LOFTED HEAD** (`shipLoft`): a skull that widens at the cheeks into a tapering snout, BROW RIDGES pushed out over the eyes, a hinged
  lofted JAW with a red mouth and its own row of teeth, upper teeth along the skull's edge, sunken eyes (a dark socket ring, a glowing eye,
  a slit pupil), spined FRILLS, curved tapering HORNS and long tapering WHISKERS (`shipTaper`). Merged into one skin draw plus one
  membrane draw (plus the jaw and eyes). Helpers: `shipSerpentTex`, `shipGeo`, `shipLoft`, `shipTaper`, `shipFan`.
- **Measured headless:** the first render had the body and then the head INSIDE OUT (you saw the inside of the tube from above). The body's
  rings run counter-clockwise about forward and advance BACKWARD; the head loft and the tapers advance FORWARD, so they need the opposite
  winding. Both are now right: the skin is solid from above, the side and below.
- **Moves:** the serpent. **Open:** the eyes are cartoonish, and nothing reacts to it. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP, PASS 12: THE SERPENT FISH (m1416, WORKER A)

His: *"long, elongated serpent fish"* (one big sea creature per pass; the whale was pass 11).

- `shipSerpentMake` / `shipSerpentP` / `shipSerpentStep`, `SHIPZ.on.serpent`, in `Z.seaG` (rocks with the sea). About 46 m: 44 body
  segments in ONE `InstancedMesh` (banded teal back, scaled flank stripes, a pale belly in vertex colour), a continuous dorsal SAIL (one
  translucent fin per segment, heights varied), a glowing lateral line (instanced), and a head that is its own group: a long skull and
  snout, a JAW that opens and shuts with teeth, glowing eyes, two fanned FRILLS, swept-back horns, and two long trailing WHISKERS. 3 draws
  for the body, plus the head.
- **THE BODY FOLLOWS ONE PATH.** Segment i sits at `P(T - i * sp / v)`, where the head was a moment ago, so the arches stand still in the
  sea and the body slides THROUGH them (that is what reads as a sea serpent rather than a wobbling tube), and a dive starts at the head and
  runs down the body. `P` loops the ship at 55-85 m (radius breathes) with a 2.6 m weave, 6.5 m/s; arches every 16 m of path at +/-3 m;
  a slow envelope (period ~140 s) brings it up for roughly half the time and takes it down to -10 m. A splash where a segment breaks the
  surface (throttled to one every 0.12 s). Hidden when every segment is deeper than 2.5 m.
- **Measured headless, not guessed:** the first cut had the segments at 0.78 x their spacing and read as a string of BEADS with separate
  triangle fins; at 1.45 x they overlap into one body, and per-segment fins join into a sail. The arches went 2.2 -> 3.0 m so they stand
  clear of the waves.
- `mel.SHIPZ.on.serpent`: `ph` (phase: `W.ph = 37 - mel.SHIPZ.U.uTime.value` brings it up now), `dir` (+1/-1, which way round it loops).
- **Moves:** THE SHIP pass 12. **Open:** the mantas that swim AND fly (pass 13), other ships / a harbour / air creatures. Nothing reacts to
  the serpent and it never comes at the ship. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP: THE SEA STOPS TILING FROM AFAR (m1411, WORKER A)

His (screenshot from far out, zoomed): *"you can see the repetition -- is there any way to break that up with a few different sizes of
noises or variations?"*

Two causes, both in the sea shader. (1) The fine ripple / foam / lace / glitter noise (periods 0.2-3 m) kept drawing at hundreds of
metres, where it can only ALIAS -- that is the dot grid. (2) The five vertex sines ARE periodic, and their gradient `vG` was the whole
normal at middle distance -- that is the regular weave. Fixed by: `hf` fades every fine term out over 40-260 m; `vG` gives way (to 30%)
over 25-220 m; what replaces it is `big`, two noise octaves (22 m and 9 m) on TURNED lattices (`RT`, `RU` -- value noise on an
axis-aligned lattice shows its grid), strongest far; and a `macro` noise (180 m and 60 m, also turned) scales all of it (`chop`
.45-1.45) so there are glassy calm stretches beside choppy ones, tints `deep`, and a slow drifting cloud-shadow darkens patches by up
to 20%. Headless from (-150, 70, -150) toward the island: the grid is gone, the far sea reads as irregular patches. Near the ship it
looks the same as before. Not signed off.

## THE SHIP, PASS 11: FOAM, AND THE FIRST BIG SEA CREATURE -- A GIANT ALIEN WHALE (m1409, WORKER A)

His: *"I'm wondering if we can do foam on the water too... spend some time doing passes on developing one big sea creature at a time,
like giant alien whales."*

- **FOAM** is two more terms in the sea shader, both merged into the existing `foam` (so the ship's hull-ellipse discard and the fog still
  apply): `streak` -- wind lanes, a noise stretched along the wind and bent by a second noise so they curl rather than slash (the first
  cut was 15:1 and read as RAIN on the water; it is ~5:1 and warped now), masked by a slow patch noise and faded with distance; and
  `lace` -- whitecaps on the crests.
- **THE WHALE** (`shipWhaleMake` / `shipWhaleStep`, `SHIPZ.on.whale`): 46 m long, a lofted body in `Z.seaG` (so it rocks with the sea,
  not with the ship), a spine of ridge plates, a row of glowing cyan spots that pulse (`glowM`), a hind group that BENDS and flukes that
  FLICK. A four-state loop: `under` (invisible, swims to a random spot 70-150 m out) -> `rise` (4 s, eases up from -14) -> `cruise`
  (13 s at y -0.55 so the back and ridge break the surface; 2-3 BLOWS from the blowhole, a column of spray bursts and a sound inside
  150 m) -> `dive` (6 s, pitches down, the tail arches, a fluke SPLASH at 3.4 s) -> `under`.
- **MEASURED HEADLESS, NOT GUESSED:** at y -1.4 only the ridge plates showed; at -0.55 the back reads. And forcing `cruise` from the
  console showed the body invisible -- `R.visible` was only ever set by `rise`. It is set from the state every frame now
  (`R.visible = W.st !== 'under'`), so any entry into a state draws right.
- `mel.SHIPZ.on.whale` is live: `st`, `t`, `x`, `z`, `h` (set `st = 'rise'` to call it up).
- **Moves:** THE SHIP pass 11. **Open:** the serpent fish (pass 12), the mantas that swim AND fly (pass 13), other ships / a harbour /
  air creatures after. The whale is not yet tied to the ship's own wake and nothing reacts to it. Not signed off.

- **The orb had not swung since pass 9.** Pass 9 put `bgateStep` and its `// pass 9: his back door` comment on the same line as the orb's sway, so the sway sat inside the comment. That is the landmine about a behaviour that lives only in a comment. It is its own call now (`ghomeOrb`).
- **The orb is a pendulum.** A damped spring at omega^2 = g / L (2.25 m of chain) toward the wind's sway. A blow pushes it away from the striker, in the home's own frame. Measured headless: a hit from 3 m on +x took it to 0.79 rad, and it settled back into the wind inside 4 s. Clamped at 1.1 rad.

The back door goes through `bgateHit`, so it breaks and mends the way the arena's gates do. The orb takes a knock with a clang and sparks. Each of the 24 stall bells rings at its own pitch (a high `clang`, cooldown .15 s). The bells are merged geometry, so they do not move.
- Draws unchanged (26). `MEL_WORLD=home node tools/boot.mjs` is ok.

## THE SHIP, PASS 10: THE SCENERY REBUILT -- NO MORE CONES (m1404, WORKER A)

His: *"I'm not loving the background scenery... it feels very low rent... take a cone, flip it upside down and call it a floating island and
it looks so goddamn geometric. Break up the flat surfaces, make the rim eroded, differences in ground textures, bushes, trees... the
underside, pieces missing, different materials... and the island is just a circle."*

**`shipIsle`, one seeded generator for every island** (pure THREE and vertex colours; it runs at module scope from `shipSea`):
- **The OUTLINE**: a radius per angle from eight random harmonics, with NOTCHES bitten out. On the sea island they are coves; on a floating
  island they are the bays a waterfall leaves by.
- **The TOP**: rings from the middle to that outline, rolling ground from layered value noise, painted per vertex. Grass is in three greens,
  with dirt patches and rock where the rim or the heights are.
  - A floating island's rim CRUMBLES down.
  - The sea island's ground falls to a beach and under the sea (two skirt rings).
- **The UNDERSIDE** (floating): a cliff of STRATA.
  - Twelve levels down, each ring tapering by a noisy power and ledging in and out.
  - The taper is split into 2-4 LOBES, so it drips into several points instead of one cone.
  - It is banded in four rock tones under a root-brown lip.
  - Broken CHUNKS of rock float beneath, and VINES hang off the rim.
- **LIFE**: pines (stacked cones), broadleaf trees with blob crowns (a fifth of them CHERRY BLOSSOM), bushes and boulders, set on the
  ground's own height. All of it is one vertex-coloured mesh per island.
- **The SEA ISLAND** (R 95):
  - a mountain with a plateau summit and the pagoda on it;
  - beaches round a real coastline with coves;
  - **SURF** on a strip that follows that coastline, its streaks scrolling and working up and down the beach;
  - six jagged SEA STACKS, wet-dark at the waterline, with foam round their feet;
  - **a HARBOUR** in the first cove: a pier on posts out over the water with lanterns, two houses with tiled roofs, and a red torii on the
    sand.
- **EIGHT floating islands** now, up from six (two small near ones). Three carry pagodas and five pour waterfalls from a notch.
- **The haze** is pushed out (fog 380-1250, camera far 1400), so the islands at 300-600 m keep their colour.
- **Checked headless**: boots, builds, no errors; close renders of a floating island, the sea island and its coast. The first render had
  the strata washed nearly white, the sea stacks pale boxes, and the pagoda oversized on a needle peak; all three are fixed.

**Queued (BUILDINGS.md, THE SHIP)**, from the rest of his message:
- foam and the first big sea creature, a giant alien whale;
- a serpent-fish;
- mantas that swim AND fly;
- later: other ships, a bigger harbour, air creatures for the airship.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## THE SHIP, PASS 9: FLAGS THAT FLOW (m1399, WORKER A)

His: *"are they actually flowing in the wind, are they rigged like actual flags?"* They were not. Each was a flat plane swinging whole,
and the masthead "pennants" were the banner texture turned on its side, which read as stiff boards.

- **Every flag is CLOTH now** (`shipFlag`, `shipCloth`). Each keeps its rest shape and is bent every frame:
  - two travelling waves (a long one and a fast small one) run from where it is tied to its free end, growing with the distance from the
    hoist, so it ripples and snaps;
  - a slow shared GUST swells and slackens every flag on the ship together;
  - a pennant streams out in a gust and DROOPS as the wind drops;
  - the side banners belly out and sway along the hull.

  Their meshes got the segments for it (24 x 2 on a pennant, 2 x 12 on a banner), and normals are recomputed, so the light rolls across the
  folds.
- **Real pennants, rigged**: a dark staff with a brass ball stands on every masthead's finial. Each flies a 6 m pennant with its own
  texture (`shipPennantTex`): red, a cream chain of diamonds between two cream lines, weathering, and a SWALLOW-TAIL cut into its free end.
  - They stream forward, the same way the wind fills the sails (it blows from astern), and swing a little on their staffs.
- The stern banner on its pole flows the same way.
- **Checked headless**: boots, builds, no errors; renders of the mastheads and the side banners.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## THE SHIP, PASS 4: THE RENDERING BANDS FIXED; REAL SURFACES (m1377, WORKER A)

His (from the deck, m1375): *"a bunch of areas are having this weird rendering issue -- I think this happens when two objects overlap... we
need to texture things with real wood textures and metal textures, concrete textures and fabric textures."*

**The bands were the SUN, not the overlaps (mostly).**
- The sunrise put the light 7.5 degrees over the horizon. At that grazing angle every shadow-map texel stretches about x7.7 across the deck,
  which gives the stair-stepped light/dark bands and the sawtooth acne in his screenshot.
- The DRAWN sun stays low in the sky (`uSun`). The LIGHT now stands at about 27 degrees (its y floored at .5), with `normalBias` .07.
- **Real overlaps fixed too**, coplanar faces that z-fight:
  - the deck strips each overlapped the next by 2 cm, top to top; they butt now (as do the hold's floor strips);
  - the forecastle's deck plate sat exactly on its box's top; it stands 2 cm proud now;
  - the stern castle's walls ran up INSIDE the quarterdeck slab; they stop under it now.

**Real surfaces.** Six textures authored for the ship (`images/ship_*.jpg`, 17-115 KB each, tileable by construction: periodic noise and
wrapped joints, made with numpy + PIL):
- deck planks: honey-brown boards with grain and rings, staggered butt joints, nail holes, tarred seams;
- hull timber: dark reddish boards with rivet rows (the hull, the castle walls, the masts, and darkened for the beams and battens);
- brass: brushed riveted plate with green patina (the guns, the gold trim, the finials);
- red lacquer: crimson with faint grain and worn spots (the band, the rails);
- slate roof tiles: the pagoda roofs;
- **the SAIL**: crimson canvas with weave, stitched seams, patches, frayed dark edges and a white square-spiral KEY CREST (his reference's motif).

How they go on:
- `put` now lays WORLD-SPACE UVs on every piece: the face's dominant axis picks the plane, and the material's `userData.uvS` sets metres per
  tile. So one texture density runs across every merged box, strip and the lofted hull, and the deck's boards run fore and aft.
- The sails keep their own 0..1 UVs, so the crest is centred on each.
- The old dark seam strips across the deck are gone (the texture has its own seams).
- I tried to generate photo textures through the image API first, but the account has no credits (`credit_balance_exhausted`). If he
  wants photographic ones, the files can be swapped in place under the same names.

**Checked headless**: boots, builds, no errors; side and deck renders show the textures.

## The MOVE TABLE, measured (STEER 000 step 1, WORKER B)

His ask (via the main session): *"put worker B on the move table"* -- LEVELDESIGN.md layer 0: every move AND combo, how high and how far,
measured from the shipped physics, so the level generator sizes every gap from a number instead of an eyeball.

**`npm run moves`** (`tools/moves.mjs` + `tools/moves.page.js`, about 30 s):
- **Boot.** The `tools/play.mjs` pattern. It boots the shipped `index.html` headless in the Building Forge as Grumbo (`agoblin`, 1.4 m),
  with a handle spliced beside `mel` and a fake clock. It steps `frameBody()` at 60 fps, with `Math.random` seeded.
- **Every move goes through the PADS.** Real `PointerEvent`s go into the shipped `bindStick`: tap, flick (centre to rim in a frame), hold,
  release. The left pad steers by world direction (the inverse of `stickWorld`). So each gesture is read by the game's own code: the
  sprint is the right pad held while running, the long jump is letting go of it, the backflip is the hold at rest, and so on.
- **Test geometry** for each row is pushed into `BOXES` on the empty floor and taken out after: 40 m faces, two faces 4.6 m apart, a bar
  (`hbarMake`), ledges, risers, drop platforms.
- **Output.**
  - `tools/moves.json` holds every move's `h` / `d` / `air` / `comfy_h` / `comfy_d` (80%), plus the speeds and the raw rows.
  - The table between LEVELGRID.md's MOVE TABLE markers is rewritten.
  - `npm run moves jump bar` runs only those rows and prints them raw.

**The headline numbers (max, comfy):**
- **Basic jumps.**
  - jump 2.72 m up.
  - run jump 7.44 m across.
  - LONG JUMP (sprint, let go) 13.7 m.
  - double jump 5.01 m up, 12.5 m at a run.
- **High jump.** The backflip, at full charge, is **6.66 m** up.
- **Air kicks.** Each one holds his height and dashes about +4 m.
  - run + double + 3 kicks: 26.5 m.
  - zoom + double + 3 kicks: **36.8 m**.
- **The high bar at a full pump** (giant swings): **14.8 m** up released near the horizontal, **23.9 m** across released just past the
  bottom.
- **Wall run UP** (the lip his hands reach):
  - run, with the tap: 3.3 m.
  - sprint: 4.5 m.
  - long-jumping into the face: 10.7 m.
  - zoom: 11.6 m; zoom-jumping into the face: 13.4 m.
- **Side wall run.** 6.9 m along the face at a run; the kick off it goes 7.5 m.
- **Wall-slide chain.** +2.07 m every kick, between faces 4.6 m apart, with no limit found.
- **Ledge.** The highest top he gets onto is 4.47 m from a jump and 5.86 m from a double.
- **Step.** .38 m (`MOVE.step` is .40 at his height).
- **Falls.** No fall damage up to 24 m; over about 3 m it is the hard landing, 1.15 s pinned.

**Found while measuring (not changed):**
- The right tap at a face is a wall run, not a jump.
- A jump at a face with the stick at rest is the m1372 wall slide.
- A kick thrown on the way up throws the rest of the climb away. The kicks are timed at the top.

SHIPPED: tools only; the game is untouched. The numbers are measured headless, not on his phone.

## THE SHIP, PASS 2: IT RIDES THE SWELL; THE HOLD; CLIMBABLE SAILS; ROPE SWINGS (m1374, WORKER A)

- **The ship rides the swell, by holding the SHIP still and moving the WORLD.** `shipWave` is a JS twin of the sea shader's five waves (the
  same numbers, `SHIPZ.WV`). Each frame it is sampled at the bow, the stern, both sides and the middle, giving the pitch, roll and heave a
  46 m hull would take (eased for its mass; `rock` 3 on the angles). Those are applied INVERTED to the sea (`Z.seaG`) and the sky dome.
  - So every deck, collider, ramp, ladder and body aboard stays exactly where it is, and he is CARRIED for free. No collider has to rotate:
    an axis-aligned box cannot pitch, and that is why the ship itself does not move.
  - The horizon and the water heave and tilt round the deck, the way they do from a real deck. Measured headless: pitch ~1 degree, roll
    ~1.3 degrees, heave +-.3 m.
- **THE HOLD**, below the main deck from the stern castle to the forecastle (20 m):
  - a plank floor at .7 m, walls where the hull is, bulkheads at both ends;
  - frames and deck beams, lanterns hung down the middle, cargo stacked, hammocks slung, and barrels to smash (`smashAdd`);
  - **a HATCH** cut in the main deck forward of the mainmast, with a coaming round it and a ladder up (`kitClimbAdd`, exit mark on deck).
    You drop in, or climb.
  - **The sea shader cuts the hull's footprint out of the water**, so the hold is dry.
- **The SAILS are CLIMBABLE.** The battens are the rungs: climb up the forward face of each sail to its yard. **Every YARD and BOOM is a
  walkable beam** (.5 m, a balance beam, named as one) out across the ship.
- **Rope swings:** stays run between the mast tops, main to fore and mizzen to main, and a GRAPPLE RING (`gringAdd`) hangs from the middle
  of each, so you can swing from one mast to the next.
- **The spawn** moved to (0, -.5), aft of the mainmast. The old spot was over the new hatch: the first headless run spawned him in the hold.
- **Checked headless** (the zone boots and `shipBuild` runs with no page errors; he stands grounded on the deck), and rendered from the side,
  the deck and inside the hold.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED. Next: pass 3, foam and wake, bow spray, the sun on the water, gulls, an island.

## FLOATING ISLANDS, NOT CONES (m1407): `floatIsland` AND `islandDress`, SHARED

His (to this window and the Ship's): *"The upside-down floating islands -- you take a cone, turn it upside down and call it a floating island, and it looks so goddamn geometric. Break up that shape: erode the outer ridges, break up the line with rocks and dirt and boulders and trees and shrubs, inflate and deflate, take chunks away, add chunks... big land masses, small, medium -- art direct."*

- **`floatIsland({ R, depth, seed, detail, flat, lobes, ...colours })`** returns `{ geo, topAt(x, z), rimR(a), R }`. It starts from an icosphere (detail 3-5), all in VERTEX COLOUR, so every island in a scene is ONE material and one draw.
  - **THE TOP:** squashed to a gentle terrain (`topAt`) inside an irregular outline (`rimR`: low-frequency wobble plus NOTCHES), with grass in two greens and dirt patches.
  - **THE RIM:** a dirt band, then a CLIFF band (the first 16% of the underside hangs nearly straight down).
  - **THE UNDERSIDE:** tapers to `lobes` hanging tips. Each part follows ITS lobe by direction (sharpened weights, `pow 6`, after the first try averaged them back into one cone). It has stepped ledges (terraces), big lumps, deep ridged cracks, banded STRATA in five warm rock colours darkening toward the tips, and MOSS dripping from the rim.
- **`islandDress(put, I, x, y, z, { cherry, pine, rocks, shrubs, roots, seed, clear })`** adds:
  - cherry trees (trunk, branch, five pink blossom clusters)
  - pines (three tiers)
  - noise-displaced boulders and low shrubs
  - thin two-segment hanging ROOTS (the first ones read as straight sticks)
  - `clear` keeps the dressing off a central radius (the dojo's dais, a pagoda's base)
- **`isl3Mat()`** is the shared vertex-colour material.
- **In the dojo:** the platform's own island (grass and shrubs round the dais, 26 roots), the altars', the stepping stones', the pagodas' (cherry, pine, boulders), and the seven drifting platforms (still standable). Plus TWELVE art-directed scenery masses: two great ones (R 26 and 30) behind, a chain of medium ones low and high, small rocks, and a near-twin pair.
- **Checked headless:** three render rounds. Round 1 read as cones with pale rock. Round 2 added terraces and strata, still one cone. Round 3 added sharpened lobes, the cliff band and stronger strata.
- **Open:** a big island's underside can still read as one dominant point from below. More passes will add carved arches and chunks off the mass, and waterfalls.
- **For the Ship's worker:** these are global functions; use them for the sea's islands and the sky.

    - stairs (+4.2 in 14 risers of .30)

    - a side wall run over a 6 m pit

    - a drop of 6
    - a zip (34 m, down 8)

A sign on each says the chunk and what it asks of him, in the move table's terms. **This is for him to walk: which ones feel right, which are too easy or too hard.** His answers adjust `MOVEC.ask` per chunk before the solver uses them.

## THE SNOWFIELD, PASS 1: TRACKS, PILES, FLAKES THAT BOUNCE OFF HIM (m1384)

His: *"a convincingly good snow simulation where you're trudging through the snow, the tracks, the snow piles up, but there's also snow in the air, bouncing off your character, fluttering, super elegant."*

- **KORAJIN > The Snowfield** (`?w=forge&zone=snow`). `SNOWZ` and `snowStage` are declared above `arenaStage()` (the TDZ rule), and `snowStep` is in the forge step line.
- **THE PACK:**
  - **The depth map:** a 160 m field with a 640² byte map, 25 cm a texel, 0 to 0.55 m. The ground stays at y = 0 for walking, so fresh snow is knee-deep on him.
  - **The surface:** a 400² plane displaced in the vertex shader by the map, with normals from the neighbouring texels. It is tinted blue in the hollows, with view-dependent SPARKLES (a hash on a 2.6 cm grid, reseeded by the camera's position, so they twinkle as you move).
  - **What carves it:** the TOE BONES wherever they dip into the snow (radius .17, down to 8%), a PLOUGH under him at speed, a roll (radius .7), and a hard landing (vy < -6: a 1.1 m crater plus a puff of 40).
  - **Rims:** pile up round every cut (`rim`, `rimAdd`).
  - **Refill:** snow falls back in at `refill` .012/s (about 80 s to fill a track).
- **TRUDGING:** in deep untouched snow (over 35%) his speed is scrubbed by `exp(-drag * depth * dt)`. His own track is free.
- **THE AIR:**
  - **Flakes:** 5000 soft points in a 34 m box wrapped round the lens. Each falls at its own speed, flutters on two sines, and drifts in a wind that GUSTS.
  - **Bouncing off him:** a flake inside his body's capsule (r .5, his height) is put on its skin and BOUNCED outward and up, harder when he runs into it.
  - **Landing:** a flake that lands goes back to the top.
  - **Kicked-up puffs** (a 600 pool with gravity) come off footsteps in fresh snow and off landings.
  - **Size:** points are sized in world metres from the lens (`uPx`).
- **Checked headless:** it boots, and a stamped line of footprints and a crater render as blue-shadowed hollows with the flakes in the air (two renders).
- **Live dials:** `mel.SNOWZ` (`drag`, `refill`, `flakes` (rebuild), `wind`, `gust`, `flutter`, `fall`) and `mel.snowStamp(x, z, r, to)`.

## THE TEXTURE LIBRARY: GENERATED MAPS, TRIPLANAR ON CODE-BUILT GEOMETRY (m1379)

His: *"start generating texture maps for the endgame assets -- the wood, the marble, the stone, the metal -- so the game starts having a bit more depth"*, and he topped up the OpenAI credits.

- **Generated with his key through the environment's proxy:** `gpt-image-2` (NOT `gpt-image-1`: listed by /v1/models, but generations say "does not exist"), 1024², quality medium, a prompt for a seamless, flat-lit, top-down stylized game texture. Parallel requests fail at the proxy ("upstream request failed"), so generate one at a time.
- **Made to tile offline** (scratch `seam.py`): it measures the wrap seam against an ordinary pixel step. Over 1.8, it blends in a half-offset copy towards the edges.
  - wood_planks: 2.91, blended
  - bronze: 1.54, kept
  - red_cloth: 1.05, kept
- **Saved:** WebP q84 in `textures/` (79-427 KB). **`textures` is in `bump.mjs` DIRS** (the landmine).
- **`triMat(name, { scale, color, rough, metal })`:** a MeshStandardMaterial whose map is sampled by world position on three planes, blended by the normal. That is because our merged code geometry has no UVs (`put` strips them). Use it on anything code-built.
- **SPAWN > BUILDINGS > Material Swatches** (at 110, -150): a block, a ball and a plank of each map. Rendered headless: wood, bronze and cloth read correctly on all three shapes.
- **m1381 + this build: ALL EIGHT are in.**
  - **Streaming fixed the proxy failures.** A plain request failed as "upstream request failed" about half the time; streamed (`"stream": true`, `partial_images: 1`, the way `blender-addons/pipeline/imagegen.py` does it), all three remaining maps came through first time.
  - **The roof tiles** (seam 4.6x, the worst) are healed by INPAINTING (scratch `heal.py`): roll the map half a tile so the wrap seams cross in the middle, mask a band along the cross, `/v1/images/edits` repaints just the band, and the original pixels are kept outside it. It tiles because its edges are the untouched interior. A plain blend had left a smeared column. **Use heal for any structured map; blend only for organic ones.**
  - **The sandstone** is cream with lavender spots, made to match Grumbo's home.

## GRID LEVEL 1 THREW ON SPAWN SINCE m1359 (m1368)

His: *"I tried to spawn Grid Level 1 and it just turned into a black screen. I can faintly see through it."*

- **What was wrong:** pass 4's rope was made with `Object.assign(new THREE.Mesh(...), { position: new THREE.Vector3(...) })`. A three.js `position` is read-only (`Object.defineProperty`), so the assign THREW halfway through `lvgBuild`. Half a level and the dimmed menu were left on screen. Passes 4 to 10 (m1359-m1365) never reached him.
- **Found by building it, not by reading:** headless Chromium, the forge, `BLDG.list` lvg1 `.build()` inside a try. The stack named `cellBuild`, line 23696. After the fix the same run builds clean and steps 3 s of frames with no page error.
- **Rule:** never `Object.assign` a `position` / `rotation` / `quaternion` / `scale` onto an Object3D. Use `.set()` / `.copy()`. A grep of `Object.assign(new THREE.Mesh(... { position` finds no other case.

## THE FORGE'S PEAKS WERE INSIDE THE FORT (m1366)

His (with two screenshots at the Timber Siege Fort): *"it's interfering with the background, like grey box stuff that you don't even know what this stuff is. I don't think it's intentional?"*

- **What was wrong:** the grey shards were the forge's backdrop mountains (`forgePeaks`, m1132), not grey box.
  - The rings were at 250 and 330 m, but each peak is a cone whose BASE radius was 0.9-1.5x its height (70-150 m). So a 120 m peak on the 250 m ring reached in to ~50 m from the centre.
  - That was fine while the forge was small. The x1.5 spread put the fort at (-70, 100), and its front yard runs to z 50, right inside them.
- **Measured, not guessed:** I built the fort in headless Chromium and rendered it from above and from the side. The peaks cut straight through the fort's yard and tiers. After the fix, the same shot shows the fort clear on the white floor with the peaks on the horizon.
- **The fix:**
  - the rings move out to 380 and 470 m
  - a cone's base is 0.55-0.9x its height (`PEAKS.wide`), so the nearest rock is ~250 m out
  - the forge floor goes from 400 to 640 m square (the buildings run to ~200 m)
  - the camera's far plane is 900 in the forge, so the peaks are not clipped
- **Landmine, again:** a mid-line `//` swallowed the rest of the `PEAKS` line, and the syntax gate caught it. Use `/* */`.

## GRID LEVEL 1, PASS 8: HAND OVER HAND ON A LONG BAR (m1363)

His: *"monkey bars, dynamics, rope, climbing, and swinging"*.

- **New cell kind `'mbar'`:** a pit crossed by ONE LONG BAR running the way you are going (cell + 3 m, so it reaches 1.5 m over each ledge), at ledge + 2.55 m. Jump at the edge to catch it.
- **The shimmy:** on a long bar (`B.len` > the high bar's 2.6 m), the left stick's SIDEWAYS push moves him along it at `SHIMMY.v` 2.2 m/s. The stick's up/down still pumps a swing, and a tap still lets go.

  - the catch, the hook and the clamp all read `B.len`, so every old bar is unchanged
- **NOT MEASURED, A DIAL:** which way the stick moves him. His right is computed as `-axis * face`, but the lens is not behind him on a bar. If it goes the wrong way, set `mel.SHIMMY.side = -1` (or tell me and I flip it).
- **No hand-over-hand clip yet:** he slides in the hang pose. That is greybox. A real monkey-bar clip is a slot for the art pass.

## GRID LEVEL 1, PASS 7: CATAPULTS UNDER THE ROUTE (m1362)

His: *"catapults rockets turrets"*.

- **Three catapults on the GROUND** (`cats` in `LVG1`: (5,5), (8,8), (2,8)), under the raised route, so they lob UP at you on the high moves.
- **How they fire:**
  - each turns slowly towards him and fires every 5-6.5 s when he is 6-55 m away
  - it aims at where he will be (60% of his velocity times the flight time)
  - the flight takes 1.7 s plus 1 s per 30 m, under a gravity of 20
- **Telegraph:** a RED RING where the stone will land, which tightens and brightens as it comes. Out of the ring or in a roll, and you are safe.
- **The hit:** 18 damage with a big push and lift, plus dust and smoke. The stone also calls `bldHit` with a 2.2 m radius, so it breaks anything breakable where it lands.
- **Killing one:** drop to the ground and smash it (its base is a `smashAdd`, 8 hp, never rebuilds). The choice is the risk: going down costs you the climb.
- **Still open:** a stone landing on the boss keep's legs (once they are unshielded) hurts them. Luring a stone onto them is a trick, not a plan.

## GRID LEVEL 1, PASS 6: THE BOSS KEEP FALLS WHEN ITS LEGS GO (m1361)

His: *"knock down a building... fully destructible buildings... the boss... crumbles"*.

  - **Shielded until the boss door opens** (3, 6 and 8 done): a pink cylinder round each leg, and hits do nothing (`S.cool` is held).
  - **After that,** each leg is a `smashAdd` piece with 10 hp that never rebuilds.
  - **Each leg lost tips the keep towards it** (.05 rad per leg).
- **When all four are gone,** the keep falls:
  - its collider and gun go
  - it tumbles and lands in dust and smoke, with a big shake
  - E is marked done, with a beam
  - the wreck sinks and is gone after 4 s

His: *"archers across certain places"*, *"catapults rockets turrets"*.

## THE GRID LEVEL: A LEVEL PLANNED AS LOGIC FIRST (m1356)

His two blueprint images, and: *"start with the game logic of the level first -- the path, the beats, the gates and buttons -- and add the towers and streams and archers later."*

- **LEVELGRID.md is the system and the plan.** `lvgBuild(spec)` turns a spec (an ordered path of `[col, row, Y, tag]` cells on a 10 x 10 grid of 7 m cells, heights Y 0-3 at 4.5 m, plus branches and beats) into a playable GREYBOX:
  - pads coloured along the path
  - one-level steps as ramps, two-level climbs as ladders
  - numbered beat markers
  - the mechanisms: guards, a tower (2 archers + a gun), a BUTTON → DRAWBRIDGE over a gap, a CANDLE → GATE, a ZIP to the end, and a BOSS DOOR that opens when `spec.need` (3, 6, 8) is done

## BREAKABLE RAILS -- S3b, FIRST IN THE COURTYARD (m1354)

- **`bldPieces(g, mat)` / `pieceAdd(P, geos, box, O)` / `pieceDone(P)`:** thin breakable things (rails, balusters, slats) gathered into ONE merged mesh, a vertex range each. Each piece has its own solid `noCam` collider, kept in `O.boxes` so the builder's mapping and clear see it.
- **`pieceHit`** (in `bldHit`) breaks a piece in `PIECE.hp` 1.5 hits:
  - its range collapses to its own centre
  - its box leaves the world
  - splinters and a crack
  - it comes back after `PIECE.fix` 50 s, not while he stands in it
- `skinStep` and `pieceStep` now run every frame in the forge, not only inside the hall's step.
- **The Courtyard's rails are runs of breakable sections**, each about 1.2 m with a top rail, a mid rail and a baluster:
  - both halls' balcony fronts and ends
  - watchtower deck A
  - deck B (around its south opening)

  They were solid .95 m slabs with drawn balusters.

## BREAKABLE ROOFS OVER RAFTERS -- S3a, FIRST ON THE DOJO HALL (m1353)

*"The frame of the roof stays, but the pieces that make up the roof are destructible. If rockets are shooting at you, or you're fighting up there, they're shooting pieces of the roof off -- maybe you go back up and rebuild it. I like exposed rafters."* (BUILDINGS.md STEER S3)

- **`bldSkinRoof(g, cx, cz, EX, EZ, hR, mat, rafM, opt)`** cuts a roof surface `hR(x, z)` into PANELS of about `SKIN.pan` 2.4 m.
  - Each panel is a vertex RANGE of one merged mesh, so the roof is still one draw, plus its own walkable triangles (`bldTris` per panel).
  - Under them are RAFTERS: a timber beam along every seam of constant x, drawn and WALKABLE (`SKIN.raf` .3 m wide, about 9 cm under the tiles).
- **`skinHit`** (in `bldHit`, so his rockets, bolts and strikes reach it) takes `hp` 2 off a panel. At zero the panel's vertices collapse to a point (no draw cost) and its triangles leave the walkable store, with debris, dust and a tile clatter.
  - **Their rockets break panels too** (`turretShotBoom`). That is the point: being shot off the roof.
  - A strike at his chest never breaks the panel he stands on: the vertical reach is `.5 + rad / 2`, enough for a blast, not for a sword.
- **Panels come back** after `SKIN.fix` 45 s, never while he stands where one goes. That is the "rebuild" for now; a worker doing it is a later step.
- **The Dojo Hall's roof is the first skin.** It was one mesh and one set of triangles. The fascia, the ridge and its horns are unchanged.
- **Next:** S3b (breakable rails, balusters and gates), then S3c (every roof, as S2 reaches it).

## FIVE FROM HIS COURTYARD WALK (m1352)

His screenshot: a red wall broken into a grey checker. Plus: walking through ground geometry, a launch off the ladder top, stuck on a zipline, archers shooting through roofs.

- **The grey checker was the X-RAY, dithering a wall that was not in the way.** The m181 dither thinned any surface nearer the lens than him inside a SCREEN circle round him, so a side wall beside him became a checker. It is now a world CAPSULE round the lens→him line (1.6 m): only what actually stands between the camera and him thins.
- **Walking through ground geometry.** The court and the castle drew their kerbs, rim stones, moss, plinths and lantern bases with `solid` 0.
  - `lowSolid`: any box standing on the ground (y0 < 5 cm), 12 cm to 1.2 m tall, with a real footprint, is now solid and `noCam`.
  - It is applied in `courtBuild`'s and `heronBuild`'s `box`. The other builders have their own helpers. **Tell me which buildings still let your feet sink**, and I'll add the rule there.
- **The ladder's step-over launch.** It carried him all the way to the exit mark, which can be metres in (more at ×1.5). It now carries him only `CLIMB.overD` .9 m in from the rungs, rising `overUp` .12, in `overT` .32 s. If it's still too much, `mel.CLIMB.overD` can go lower, or 0 for a plain stand-up.
- **The zipline.** A tap on either pad already let go, but there was no obvious gesture.
  - Holding the left stick hard DOWN for `ZIP.dropT` .45 s now lets go too.
  - The shimmy is quicker: `up` 1.6 → 2.6 m/s.
  - There is still no hang animation.
- **Archers through roofs.** `losClear` walks the eye→chest line in .45 m hops and calls it blocked at a solid box OR a walkable surface it passes through. That second check matters because roofs, decks and bridges are triangles, not boxes.
  - An archer only starts a draw with a clear line (cached every .25 s).
  - If the line closes while he aims, he holds the shot instead of loosing. He "knows you're there", but cannot shoot through the roof.

## THE LENS TIPS FOR A SENTRY GUN TOO; THE LAST 2D SEND-BACK (m1350)

*"When I hit the archers' arrows and they ricochet, I don't know that I want them to go straight back -- let's do it for now, but it's a little unrealistic and makes it easier. Also when the archers shoot at you your camera bends up so you can see the arrows coming, but it doesn't do this with the rockets, and it should."*

- **The camera.** An arrow lobs for 2-3 s, so the m1276 ease (`UPLOOK.in` .32 s) has time to arrive. A rocket covers a tower's height in about 1 s, so the lens was still turning when it hit.
  - `upLookW` now also tips the lens for any SENTRY GUN that has SEEN him from above: its eye is red (`T.see`), it is within range + 6 m, and it is at least `UPLOOK.dy` above his chest.
  - The tilt holds for as long as the gun tracks him, BEFORE it fires, at `UPLOOK.gun` .85 of an arrow's tilt. The warning is the gun's attention, not the shot.
- **Arrows still go straight back** (his "let's do it for now"). He finds it a little unrealistic and easy. That is a taste call left open: the alternative is the ordinary glance for a late block, and a straight return only for a perfect parry.
- **The third send-back path was 2D too:** the auto-deflect (`deflectThreat`) sent turret rockets home on a level line. It now uses `turAimHome` (3D) like m1348's two.

## A KNOCKED-BACK SHOT GOES HOME IN 3D (m1348)

*"There's a turret launching rockets at you, I countered one and it sends it back on the 2D plane. It doesn't go back up at the turret, but it still thinks it hits the turret even though it's 50 feet below it."*
