## 3D AIM OWNS THE WHOLE RIGHT PAD, WITH ITS OWN CIRCLE (m1345)

*"I keep trying to aim it upward and it won't -- it aims down but not up. I touch the right stick in 3D and he jumps, or I push up and it shoots instead of aiming the cursor up, or I push down and he blocks. 3D mode takes over the whole stick. And when you click 3D aim it unfolds into its own circle up there, centred on what used to be the flick-up position."*

- **Why up never worked:** m1327 armed on the 2D trigger (the thumb pushed UP to the rim) and then read pitch from travel beyond that point. There was no room left to go up.
- **`aim3Stick` now owns the right pad in 3D AIM:**
  - a touch takes the gun up: no tap-jump, no flick, no guard, no back-step on release
  - sideways turns the lens (stepCam's ordinary drag)
  - up/down drives the PITCH at `pRate` 1.2 rad/s, ±`pMax` 35°, with a 12% dead zone
  - lifting the thumb FIRES if it was held at least `minT` .12 s
  - the pitch then eases back to level
- **`#aim3ring`:** a red circle "unfolds" above the right pad (where the flick-up used to point) whenever 3D AIM is on with a gun. It opens fully while you aim, and its dot shows where the shot is pointed: up/down is the pitch, sideways is the thumb.
- **The 2D aim keeps m1344's walk-backwards tilt.**

## 2D AIM: WALK BACKWARDS AND THE RETICLE RISES (m1344)

*"The 3D aim thing is not working as it's supposed to. Another idea: in 2D, the normal aiming mode, what if your reticle nudged slightly upward when you walked backwards -- as you're walking backwards it slowly edges upward, and as soon as you stop walking it goes back to level."*

- `aimBackPitch`, in the ordinary 2D aim (with 3D AIM off):
  - while AIMING, the left stick's component pointing AWAY from his facing, past `BACKAIM.at` .35, raises the shot's pitch at up to about `rate` .55 rad/s × 1.6 at a full pull, capped at `max` 32°
  - anything else eases it back to level (`back` .3 s half-life)
  - since aiming faces him down the lens, "backwards" is the left stick pulled down
- **Tilted, the shot leaves along the lens's bearing at that pitch** (`p.gDir`, the 3D aim's own path through `aimPoint`). The lock and machine assists step aside (`aimRaw`), so the tilt is what you get. The lens tilts up with it at half the pitch (`BACKAIM.cam`).
- The 3D AIM toggle is untouched. He says it is not working right; what is wrong with it is an open question for him.
- **Live on `mel.BACKAIM`** (`rate`, `max`, `at`, `cam`). `on: 0` turns it off.

## 3D AIM IS THE 2D AIM PLUS A PITCH (m1327)

*"Go back to the auto shoot upon release; leave the left stick to jumping. The aimer should never move to the side of the screen -- it always stays centred. It doesn't need to work any different than the regular game: pushing left on the right stick already turns the camera left. The only difference is your view can slightly gimbal up or down... when you let go it eases your camera view back to parallel to the ground. It might just become the default."*

- **`aim3Gun`'s own trigger is out of the loop.** That was m1282's always-aiming with a left-tap fire, and m1293's absolute "drawing tablet" cursor. In 3D AIM, `stepKit` now runs the ORDINARY 2D trigger: hold up to aim, release to fire, sideways turns the lens (`flyAim` no longer includes 3D AIM).
- **The left tap is the jump again** (the `aim3Fire` branch is removed from the left tap).
- **`aim3Pitch` adds the one difference:**
  - While aiming, the thumb's travel up or down from WHERE IT ARMED is a pitch RATE: `pRate` 1.1 rad/s at `pSpan` .3 of the pad, with a 12% dead zone, held to `pMax` ±25°.
  - The shot leaves along the lens's bearing at that pitch (`p.gDir`, yaw always 0), so the reticle stays centred.
  - The lens tilts with it: `cam.el` drops by `pCam` .85 of the pitch.
  - On release the pitch eases back to level (`pBack` .25 s half-life).
- In 3D AIM there is no lock-on assist: `aimRaw` already returns the raw line when `aim3Live`, so where you point is where it goes.
- `AIM3.cam.el` is 0 now. The old over-the-shoulder dip is gone, because the view should be the 2D one.
- **If the pitch feels slow, or the wrong way up,** the numbers are live on `mel.AIM3`: `pRate`, `pSpan`, `pMax`, `pCam`.

## THE KORAJIN "TAP TO START" WAS OFF CENTRE BY ACCIDENT (m1319)

*"The tap to start button on the Korajin screen is off centre. I think that might've been intentional, but I don't like it."*

It was not intentional. The pill was centred with `left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`, but it also runs the `splashPulse` animation, whose keyframes set `transform: scale(...)`. An animated transform replaces the static one, so the translate was lost and the pill's LEFT edge sat at the middle of the screen.

- It is now centred with `left: 0; right: 0; margin: 0 auto; width: max-content`, which no animation touches.
- The right padding is trimmed by the trailing letter-spacing, so the words sit in the middle of the pill.
- **The lesson:** never centre with a transform on an element that also animates a transform.

## THE WHIRLWIND, CONTINUOUS AND STEERED (m1317)

He took back m1316's "one spin": *"Link probably does three. The problem is ours does one, then he stops, does another, stops... they need to be continuous. And I want to control it -- launch forward with it, like a tornado, moving around."*

- **What was actually wrong, MEASURED** (the hips' yaw track of `katana_360h`, read straight off `samurai_game.glb`):
  - the clip is 3.2 s
  - the hips turn -15° by 0.2 s and -301° by 1.0 s
  - then they crawl to -360° over the remaining 2.2 s
  - Each spin played the WHOLE clip in .5 s, so it was a turn followed by 70% settle, three times. That is the stop he saw.
- **Fix: only the turning window per spin.**
  - Each spin plays `from` .078 to `to` .3125 of the clip (-25° to -301°, i.e. `turn` 276°). The first spin starts at 0, so it keeps the wind-up; the last plays on to `last` .36, a short settle.
  - At each restart the body's heading (`p.faceH`, its one writer here) drops by 276°. That exactly cancels the pose snapping back, so the eye sees one unbroken rotation.
  - Each spin is .42 s.
- **2-3 spins again** (`spins` [2,3] by charge).
- **It LAUNCHES:**
  - `WHIRL.go` 8 m/s (70-100% by charge) along the way he faced at release
  - it bleeds off at 1.1/s
  - the left stick steers on top at `TORN.speed`, so it travels and can be driven round
- R 3 + 1 by charge, dmg 3, power 1.1.
- **If the spin reads backwards or jerks at each join**, `WHIRL.turn` is the number. It is live on `mel.WHIRL`.

## LADDERS AND THE WHIRLWIND, FROM HIS X4 WALK (m1316)

He walked the octagonal pagoda (X4). Three notes on shared systems are fixed here. Scale and stairs went to BUILDINGS.md's new STEER.

## Shots hit buildings whether or not a turret is standing (Worker A's finding)

`boltHit` only called `turretBlast` (and with it `bldHit`) `if (TURRET.list.length)`. So with no turret anywhere, a bolt or rocket could
not touch any building's blocks, bells, levers, gates or props; buildings with a sentry gun were shootable only by accident. It now always
calls it. Worker A (X4, all 10 passes done: m1274-m1298) found it at m1289. SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## His notes off the pagoda's zipline (m1279 on his phone): the zipline was FROZEN, shimmy, the bars, the 3D aim, the aim assist

- **"I can grab the zipline but I can't move."** That was a REAL bug, and every zipline in the forge had it. At m1193 the brake's comment
  was written mid-line: `// m1193: pull back to BRAKE K.u += K.v / K.L * dt; p.grounded = false;`. That swallowed the one line that
  advances you along the wire, so from m1193 on you hung where you caught it. (CLAUDE.md's landmine: *a behaviour asserted only in a
  comment is not a behaviour.*)
- **Shimmy up (`ZIP.up` 1.6 m/s).** The left stick pushed FORWARD on a zipline now climbs hand over hand toward its high end, and you let
  go at the top. Pulling back still brakes; otherwise you slide.
- **"I keep getting caught on the high bars."** The pagoda's balcony bars (pass 4) are OFF (`GPAG.bars` 0).
- **Monkey bars.** Queued as R10, the move first and then the pieces.
- **3D aim, ABSOLUTE** (*"like a drawing tablet's screen mode: the stick is a mini version of the screen"*).
  - **The mapping.** Where the thumb is on the pad IS where the cursor sits in the view: the pad's rim is `absYaw` 42 degrees across and
    `absPit` 32 degrees up/down. A .025 s ease only takes the jitter out, and letting go leaves it there.
  - **No zoom.** The lens stays the ordinary third person (`AIM3.cam.dist` 1, no shoulder offset, a mild pitch tilt).
- **"In regular shot mode the aim assist rockets it up onto the tower."** A machine now only pulls the 2D aim up or down if it is within
  `MECHAIM.maxEl` 15 degrees of level.
- **"If it's going to catch onto a guy it should show you."** While the gun is up and its aim is LOCKED (on a body or a machine), the
  charge's sight (`lockMk`) sits on the target in red. If the target is above him the lens tips up to it (`upLookW`).

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1289 -- Octagonal Block Pagoda pass 6 of 10: the guardians (X4, WORKER A)

All of them can be killed:
- **Two STONE LIONS of blocks** (komainu) sit on stone plinths either side of the gate, inside the fence (`opagLion`).
  - Come within 8 m and their eyes light red. They drop off their plinths and hunt you round the COURT RING, the strip between the
    pagoda's plinth and the fence.
  - Within 3 m they LEAP (a thud, an arc); landing on you hurts for 9 and knocks you back. A roll dodges it.
  - Leave the court and they walk home and go back to sleep.
  - Hit them with shots or swings (`opagLionHit`, through `bldHit`): 8 hp. A hit flashes them and wakes a sleeping one. At 0 they SHATTER
    into a dozen tumbling stone blocks.
  - They re-form on their plinths 60 s later.
  - Each has a moving collider (`BDYN`), so bolts stop on them.
- **Three ARCHERS** (`archerPost`) hold corners of the walks on storeys 1, 3 and 5, clear of the bars and chains.
- **A SENTRY GUN** on storey 5's walk.
- **A MONK** (a samurai with his katana) stands his post in front of the shrine altar until he sees you.

**A FINDING FOR MAIN (not changed, it is MAIN's code):** a BOLT only reaches `bldHit` at all when `TURRET.list` is non-empty.
`boltHit`'s first line is `if (TURRET.list.length) turretBlast(...)`, and `turretBlast` is what calls `bldHit`. So any building's
shootable things (blocks, bells, levers) are deaf to bolts unless some turret exists somewhere. X1 has a sentry gun, and so does X4 now,
which is what makes its blocks shootable. Melee does not have the gate.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED. Next: pass 7, the light.

THE BLOCK STYLE's third rule, *"every block can BREAK"*, now covers the whole building:
- **The eave courses are blocks.** Each face's course is cut into ~.75 m segments, each with its own turned collider.

  - Shoot out a run of the eave and the climb route has a gap in it.

- **The red band under every eave is blocks** (~.7 m each).
- **Posts are stacks of blocks.** The eight corner posts of every storey are four blocks each, the porch posts three, the fence posts three.
  Break a low one and the ones on it come down (`up`).
- **They REPAIR.** A block that has been dead 20 s flies back in from a little way off, scaling up as it lands (`opagStep`).
  - One every .15 s, the LOWEST first.
  - Only onto a block that is there (`dn` alive), so nothing is put back floating.
  - Never into him.
- **Draws**: the breakables are one InstancedMesh per material (cream, red, teal, tile, edge, dark).

## 3D AIM: the LEFT tap fires (his)

*"In 3D AIM make the left stick the fire stick -- tap it to fire -- instead of auto-firing when you let go. The left tap was only an extra
jump, because jumping and firing with the right stick was hard in my old game."*
- **Always aiming.** With 3D AIM on and a gun out he is ALWAYS aiming: the over-the-shoulder lens and the reticle are up.
- **The right thumb only MOVES the cursor** (the m1278 rate). Letting go leaves it where it is. A fast drag never becomes a sword flick.
- **The LEFT TAP fires** (`aim3Fire`): the launcher's rocket on its cooldown, or the blaster's charge (it charges while he aims).
- **The RIGHT TAP is the jump again.**

## The robot tiers, a hop that bends, and the charged WHIRLWIND (his notes)

- **Tiers (`TIER`, `tierLook`, `tierHit`).** *"Peons break into pieces with one charge hit; medium guys about three hits; big guys about
  five."*
  - **The roll.** Every horde body gets a tier at spawn (`HORDE.mix` 50 / 35 / 15):

    | tier | size | colour | blows to break |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | PEON | x.82 | dull grey | 2 |
    | WARRIOR | x1 | as is | 3 |
    | BRUTE | x1.32 | dark red | 5 |

  - **The count.** A charge, the whirlwind, a slam or a rocket counts as 2 (`TIER.big`), so ONE charge shatters a peon. At the count he is
    BLOWN APART on the spot (`limbBoom`). Limbs still come off cut by cut on the way. The blows are debounced 140 ms, so one swing is one
    blow.
  - **Not yet.** Armour pieces and symbols on the brute (R8, boss armour, is the place for those).
- **The one-legged hop bends.** *"I wanted him to bend down and then release; right now it's straight-legged."* It is a hop cycle now:
  - CROUCH: he sinks `hopSink` .16, and the standing leg folds at the hip, knee and ankle
  - PUSH and flight: up to `hopH` .34, the leg tucked
  - LANDING: he absorbs it, folding again

  The bones are bent after the mixer. Slower too (`hopHz` 1.7). `LIMB.hopSign` = -1 if the knee folds the wrong way: which way a Mixamo
  knee bends is a phone question.
- **THE WHIRLWIND (`whirlGo` / `whirlSpin`, `WHIRL`).** *"A full 360 Link-style whirlwind... charge it, and if you're pressing forward when
  you release he launches; if you don't, he spin-attacks."*
  - **Release with the LEFT STICK AT REST** (or pulled BACK): 1-3 full spins of `katana_360h` depending on the hold.
  - **Every spin** strikes everyone within `R` 2.6 m (+.4 at a full hold), all the way round, outward, and hits turrets, walls and
    props round him.
  - **Steering.** The stick steers him slowly through it (the tornado's rule).
  - **Release while PUSHING the stick** = the launch, as before. "Back" whirls for now; it is a slot for its own move.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

  - the pavilion, the fence and the gate guards moved out to suit

  A new rule, **ROOM TO FIGHT**, is at the top of BUILDINGS.md for every building and both workers.
- **"Why is the camera so close, there's nothing behind me."** It was the EAVE LIP of the roof above (pass 4's ledge box), hanging at
  head height just beyond the rail, plus the rail itself. Both are now `noCam` (the m1088 flag `camHit` already honours), so only real
  walls stop the lens.
- **"Keep the rocket launcher, not the blaster."**
  - The left wheel's GUN is now the LAUNCHER (`KIT3.hide` takes the blaster, and the hammer and the board as before).
  - The right row's ROCKET button is gone, because the launcher has no modes. The 3D AIM ring stays.
- **The 3D aim, as he meant it.** Once enabled:
  - TOUCHING the right pad arms the shot at once (no hold).
  - The thumb DRIVES the cursor as a rate: held off-centre it keeps travelling, `rate` 1.7 rad/s at full past a `dead` .12. Let the
    thumb rest and the cursor stays put, so no auto-aim is involved.
  - Lifting the thumb fires.
  - The next touch within 1.5 s picks the cursor up where it was.
  - In 3D AIM with a gun out the right TAP no longer jumps: it is the trigger, and the left tap still jumps.
- **The charge's lock reticle.** No more spinning squares (`lockMk` is a Sprite now, drawn once to a canvas):
  - four brush-cut corner BRACKETS, a thin broken ring, tick marks and a diamond pip at the centre
  - it SNAPS in when the lock is made and closes and breathes as the hold fills
  - at full it goes hot gold with an outer glow (`lockGlow`)

  The floor ring he likes is unchanged.
- **The look-up: earlier, with more ease.**
  - `tta` 2.2 -> 3.4 s, so it starts sooner.
  - The weight is now a smoothstep over the whole lead time rather than a ramp.

## m1261 -- the air-swipe hook chases a MOVING bar (the zeppelin "imaginary collider")

*"With the zeppelins flying around, I'd high-jump and swipe and just be grabbing onto an imaginary floating nothing... a weird collider of
nothingness, I could never actually get up."* It was the HOOK (m1063, `barHook`), not a collider:
- **What went wrong.** The flick picked the zeppelin's trapeze bar and dashed to where the bar was ON THAT FRAME (`tx`/`tz`/`ty`, fixed).
  A zeppelin carries its trapeze about a metre on in the dash's .2-.4 s.
- **What he saw.** He arrived at empty air, `hbarCatch` (within `grabR` .5 m) refused, and the fallback `p.vel.y = 0` held him there for a
  beat: hanging on nothing, every try.
- **The fix.** `stepHook` re-reads the bar's position every frame (the stored `u` / `side` on the live `B`), so a moving bar is caught
  and a still one behaves exactly as before.

His next direction (noted in BUILDINGS.md): a 10-PASS experiment on one building, aiming for much more visual interest and much more
function. He is sending a reference image of a tower. SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1260 -- the charge locks onto ANYTHING it is aimed at, and SHOWS the lock (his report, with a screenshot at m1253)

*"The charge up on the right stick doesn't really lock onto things. If I'm trying to hit this box and I'm clearly targeted on it, it should
indicate that I'm indicating it with some sort of lock, and when I let go my guy should launch and hit it -- not launch directly through it.
Whatever he's indicating: a turret, a human target, a box, a wall."*

- **Found: the KATANA's charge never drew its target at all.** `markStep` only showed the floor ring for `s.charge`, which is the
  hammer's flag. The blade has no `charge`, so with the sword out the lock was invisible even when it existed, and that reads as "it
  doesn't lock". It now draws for `s.charge || s.blade`.
- **A lock ON the target (`lockMk`).** A diamond bracket now sits at the target's middle, facing the lens and drawn over everything. It
  spins and closes in as the hold fills, then goes hot and steady at full, the same reading as the floor ring (which stays).
- **The charge locks onto more (`meleeLock(..., wide)`, `mechTargets(0, wide)`).** As well as people and machines (m1249), it now locks
  onto:
  - every standing SMASHABLE (crates, pots, barrels, landed supply drops), aimed at its middle
  - every breakable WALL, at the point on it nearest him

  The release is solved to stop at arm's length from its surface, so he launches TO it, not through it. Only the CHARGE gets crates and
  walls; an ordinary swipe still lunges at people and machines only.

Known gap: the parachute crate in his screenshot is still FALLING, and a falling crate is not a smashable until it lands. Above
`MECH.dy` 2.2 m nothing is a charge target, because the dash is flat. SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1259 -- three big buttons, the gun's row, the 3D AIM, and ROBITS' vertical (his request)

*"We definitely don't need the skateboard... we can get rid of the club. I want these things big, convenient and simple: one button switches
you from unarmed to ballistic to melee -- three buttons above the left stick, big and easy to hit. When you select ballistic it has the
sub-options above the right stick. One of those options is a toggle between 3D and not 3D: a little more zoomed in, still not first person,
you can aim in three dimensions. Press anywhere on the right stick, it locks in a shot, you aim around, let go and it shoots."* And about
ROBITS: *"the aiming was on a 2D plane, but if the guy was in front of you and above you, it just auto-aimed up to him."*

- **The left wheel (`KIT3.on`).**
  - It shows HANDS / GUN / SWORD only, on a thicker ring (`r1` 116 against 106, span 108, so the far tip stays on a 390 px screen).
  - The hammer, the board and the launcher are filtered out of `gearSync` and of the kit cycle (`kit3Hid`). The slots still exist, so
    quests and GOD are untouched.
  - While the launcher is out, GUN is the lit button.
  - The outer ring (Clancy / revert) moved out with it (`OUTROW` now follows `WEPROW.r1`).
  - `mel.KIT3.on = 0` brings the old wheel back, but it needs a reload.
- **The gun's row on the right.**
  - It reads CHARGE / AUTO / ROCKET (`gunRowBuild`, `gunPick`). ROCKET takes the launcher out; a trigger picked while the launcher is
    out puts the blaster back.
  - It shows for either gun.
  - A new OUTER ring above it, `#aimRow`, has one gold button: **3D AIM**. It toggles `AIM3.on`, which is remembered
    (`mel.aim3` in localStorage).
- **The 3D aim (`aim3Gun`).** This is her flight trigger (m271 `bladeGunFly`) on foot:
  - **Arm.** A right thumb held still for `holdT` .18 s arms it. A tap is still the jump, and a thumb that travels first is still the
    camera.
  - **Aim.** From then its offset is the aim: across, up to `yaw` 60 degrees either side of the lens; up and down, up to `pitch` 60
    degrees.
  - **Fire.** Lifting the thumb fires the charged ball, or a ROCKET from the launcher.
  - **The aim point.** `aimPoint` walks the 3D direction, `aimRaw` skips the locks while it is live (`aim3Live`), and the reticle and the
    shot agree because both read `aimTarget`.
  - **The body.** The body turns to the aim through the ONE facing writer (`faceTgt` gets `cam.az + p.gYaw`). The camera drag stands
    down while aiming (`flyAim`).
  - **The lens.** `cam.a3` eases the camera in: `dist` x .55, the look point `side` .75 m to his right (over the shoulder) and lifted
    .25, and the elevation tipping with the aim's pitch (`el` .6).
- **ROBITS' vertical (`mechAim`).** In the ordinary 2D aim, a MACHINE within `MECHAIM.cone` .16 rad of the lens's line, at any height, now
  pulls the shot up or down to it, the way a body already pulls it to his chest. Examples are the turret on the tower and the ballista on
  the wall. `mechTargets(dyMax)` takes a height limit now.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED. Everything is on `mel` (`KIT3`, `AIM3`, `MECHAIM`).

## m1255 -- the look-up: the lens glances up at a shot coming from above (his request)

*"When there's guards up on towers, or a sentry gun shooting rockets down, or arrows or cannonballs, there's no way to look up, so it's hard
to melee or block. What if, when somebody shoots something at you from above, your camera slightly pitches up to show you, while still keeping
its normal position -- it would also alert you that you need to counter it."*

`upLookW()` (UPLOOK) picks out the shots that should cause it:
- **Which shots.** Every live incoming shot from `threatList`: turret rockets and bolts, plus ARROWS, which covers archers, ballista
  bolts and cannonballs.
- **Above and soon.** It counts if it is more than `dy` 2 m above his chest and due to reach him (`threatTTA`) within `tta` 2.2 s.
- **Strength.** The weight grows with how far above it is and how soon it lands.

The weight is eased into `cam.up`: in fast (`in` .07) and back out slowly (`out` .6), so it reads as a glance. It acts in `stepCam`
alone, and only in the arena and the forge:
- the elevation drops by `el` .24 x the weight (the lens sinks a little)
- the look point lifts by `lift` 1.4 m x the weight

The azimuth is never touched, so `cam.az` keeps one writer and the camera stays where he put it. `mel.UPLOOK` is live, and
`mel.UPLOOK.on = 0` is the A/B. Not covered: the trebuchet's boulder, which has its own red ring. SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1254 -- Zoom Ramp Tower pass 1 (his request R1)

*"A tower shaped like a really tall ramp -- you do the speed run and it's just tall enough that your whole run gets you to the top, and you hit
it perfectly; the very top is a ledge you just barely grab, then pull yourself up into a guard tower."*

`ZRAMP`, `zrampBuild` / `zrampStep` / `zrampClear`, at (-60, -56); SPAWN > BUILDINGS > Zoom Ramp Tower.

**The course.** In the order he runs it:
- a red torii start gate on a stone slab
- a flat run-in of `run` 8 m
- a ramp rising `Hr` 5 m over `ramp` 16 m (walkable triangles, with bronze and neon edge rails)
- the SHEER FACE of a sandstone tower: ONE solid box, so the ledge hang takes his hands at its lip, and the run-up (m1251) starts on it
  by itself

**The solve.** A full zoom launches at 17 m/s, holds .7 s and bleeds 3.2 m/s^2. Over the 24 m that is about 1.43 s, arriving at about
14.7 m/s. The run-up climbs u^2/(2 x 12), about 9.0 m. His hands catch within `LEDGE.band` .55 of `LEDGE.hang` x his height. So the gold
lip at Hr + `lift` 10.1 = 15.1 m is made by a FULL zoom with about .3 m to spare, and missed by a 90% zoom (about 13.9 m/s, 8.1 m up).

**The caveat.** The arrival speed is a PREDICTION, because the ramp's effect on a zoom is not measured. So `mel.ZRAMP.lift` is the dial.
Respawn the tower after changing it: the geometry is built from it.

**How close he got.** Neon ticks mark every 2 m up the face. Every try leaves a MARK on the face for 8 s at the height his hands reached:
red for a miss, gold for a catch, and a catch also gets a beam and sparks.

**The summit.** A guard house with a door and a roof, a burning brazier (R2 will put it out), and rails on three sides only (the lip is
left clear). A ZIPLINE runs from the back corner down to the gate (pushed into `ZIPS`, taken out on clear).

`mel` also exports `MECH` (m1249). SHIPPED UNVERIFIED. Next for it: pass 2 (a timer and best mark, bars round the rim, a second line up).

## m1251 -- the wall run-up needs no tap, and its height comes from his speed (his report)

*"I don't think we ever made a wall run where you run straight up the wall. If you jump and hit a wall straight on, his velocity should just
go straight up... the speed run gets you velocity, so you could really wall run up a wall."*

The run-up did exist, but only on a TAP, and always at a fixed `upV` 7.2 m/s, about 2 m.
- **No tap (`wrunAuto`, every frame).** It starts by itself on a tall face (`minH`), any wall now including breakable ones (m1250),
  when he meets it SQUARELY head-on (`autoInto` .9, so the ~45-degree wall-to-wall jump stays a side run):
  - in the AIR at `autoAir` 3 m/s or more into it
  - on the GROUND only at a ZOOM's speed (`autoGround` 9; a sprint is 7.2, so running into a wall stays running into a wall)
- **Speed buys height.** The upward launch is his into-speed x `upK` 1, capped at `upMax` 17, and the run's time scales with it:
  - a sprint jump climbs about 2 m (as before)
  - a half zoom about 6 m
  - a full zoom (17 m/s) about 12 m

  The tapped run-up gets the same speed rule. The lip still hands over to the ledge hang, and a tap still kicks off backwards into the
  flip.

BUILDINGS.md: his three requests are queued FIRST:
- R1, the Zoom Ramp Tower, tuned so that a full zoom just makes the lip
- R2, the Four Fires that open a drawbridge
- R3, the INTERIOR KIT, modular chamber pieces for an underground level

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1250 -- wall running on breakable walls; the x-ray in the forge's buildings (his report)

*"You should be able to wall run on pretty much any wall, even the destructible ones... [the Observatory] would be a really fun
exercise -- wall run up the whole thing, wall to wall, in a spiral. Problem is you can't wall run on walls that are destructible."* and
*"When you're inside the building the camera doesn't see through walls... we need some kind of x-ray vision."*

- **Wall run.** A breakable wall is in `BOXES` as .6 x .3 m chunks plus its posts. `wrunFind` refused every piece on `minLen` 1.2 (the
  rule that says a post is not a wall). Now any piece of a breakable wall stands for the WHOLE wall: `cwRunBox` gives one turned box
  along its length, the full height of the wall, cached on the wall (`W.rb`). The side run, the run-up and the wall-to-wall jump all
  work on it. The run holds across holes already broken in it. A run-up on a breakable wall does not hand over to the ledge hang,
  because the ledge finds chunks and not this box.
- **X-ray.** This reuses the kit worlds' x-ray (m181) rather than adding a new one: `kitCutMat` on a material, switched on by
  `kitXrayStep`. Anything nearer the lens than his chest, above his feet and inside a circle round him is dithered down to `xrayMin`.
  - Every `BLDG` build is now wrapped so that whatever it adds to the scene is tagged (`bldXrayTag`). Only plain meshes with built-in
    materials are tagged: no shader materials and no skinned bodies.
  - The step now also runs when `WORLD.now === 'forge'` (`BLDX.on`), with the indoor circle `xrayWIn` 2.4 m.
  - Only buildings spawned after this build are tagged, so respawn one to see it.

SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

## m1249 -- machines are melee targets: the charge stops ON a turret (his report)

*"I make it up a tower and there's a sentry gun or a turret or the giant crossbow... I charge-attack it and I launch over it or through it,
it doesn't stop on it. It does that with humans, but not with these."* He is right, and the cause was not the dash.
- **What was wrong.** Every melee lock (`meleeLock`, behind the charge's `chargeAim`, the swipe's lunge `meleeGo`, the air kick, the
  swipe segment) only looped `DUMMIES`. A machine was empty air to it, so the charge flew its whole hold-length (`wantD`) straight past.
- **The fix.** `mechTargets()` hands the lock a stand-in body for every live shooting machine:
  - every turret (tower guns, the zeppelin, airship and skiff guns, the sentry guns)
  - the Gatehouse ballista
  - the Siege Yard's ballistas and trebuchet
  - the Flying Ship's cannons
  - the Rampart's wall sentries

  Each stand-in is scored exactly like a man. Its standoff is widened by how much fatter the machine is than a body (`dr`), so the
  dash stops at arm's length from its surface. Only machines within `MECH.dy` 2.2 m of his own height count, because the dash is flat.
- **The indicator.** The charge's existing floor RING (`markRing`, the one that closes as the hold fills) now draws under the locked
  machine as it does under a man, so a lock is visible before he lets go.

The swipe lunge gets the same lock, so an ordinary cut steps in to the gun too. SHIPPED UNVERIFIED.

  so it never leaves the water.
- **Chase.** Wade in (inside the ring, below 1.2 m) within 14 m of it and it comes for you at 1.6x `eelV`.
- **Bite.** Within 1 m it bites for `eelDmg` 10 with a shove, at most once every 1.4 s.
- **Killable.** Any plate takes hits through `bldHit` (`keepEelHit`). At `eelHp` 5 it bursts and sinks, and it surfaces again
  `eelBack` 20 s later.

Wading was already slow (m1180), so the moat is a real hazard now; the drawbridge is the safe way in. Pass 4 is an extra on a
done building, so it moves no sandbox box. Next: alternate -- Floating Islands pass 2.

## m1196 -- Floating Islands pass 1 (Building Forge loop, Set 2 #19)

`FISL`, in BLDG.list as `fisl`. Three rock islands hang in the air round (44, 32):

- **The middle island** at (52, 32), top 7 m.
- **The high island** at (42, 42), top 9 m.

**Each island:**

- **Chains:** three iron chains run to stakes in the street. A stake that would land inside the Forge-Workshop is turned
  60 degrees.

**Rope bridges** (`bridgeSpan`, with prayer flags that flap) climb from the low island to the middle one and on to the high one,
about 7.8 m each at a .26 slope. The high island carries a red TORII and a little hokora with a lamp.

rope above the rim and jump in. A second ring hangs over the shrine.

## m1192 -- Jin Lighthouse pass 2: the searchlight (Building Forge loop)

**The beam is a JIN SEARCHLIGHT now.**

  STOPS and tracks him for `lockT` .9 s while it and the crystal turn red.

## m1191 -- Spider-Bot Hangar pass 4: the spiders pounce (Building Forge loop, extra pass)

Until now the spider bots climbed every building but never touched him. They hunt now.

from its patrol loop, halfway up a wall or from a rooftop.

appearing at the door.

Pass 4 is an extra on a done building, so it moves no sandbox box. Next: alternate -- Jin Lighthouse pass 2.

## m1163 -- SPIDER-BOT HANGAR pass 2: THE SPIDERS CLIMB THE WALLS

His: *"spider robots climbing the walls."* Each spider is now a little state machine (`sphangStep`):
- `loop` round the bunker for 3-16 s, then picks a RAID target (`sphangPick`): any tall box in BOXES within `raidR` 40 m of the hangar
  (top 2.5-26 m, footprint .6-30 m a side; turned/dynamic boxes and turrets left alone) -- a building's wall, a tower, a deck, a crate
  stack, the bunker -- so they climb whatever is spawned.
- `go`: scuttles to the nearest point of its footprint; works out the face it reached and that face's outward normal.
- `up`: climbs the face at `climbV` 1.6 m/s, belly to the wall (Euler YXZ: yaw into the wall, pitch -90 deg), legs still walking.
- `top`: crosses the top to the far edge.
- `down`: climbs down the far face head-first (yaw out, pitch +90); a box that floats (a deck) it climbs to its underside and DROPS
  (gravity, a thud). Then `home` to its loop.
Still killable anywhere on the route. Pass 3 (polish) next. Shipped unverified.

## m1140 -- HOTFIX: m1139 was a BLANK PAGE

A `//` comment inserted MID-LINE (the Market cable stake change) commented out the rest of that line, the file stopped parsing. The check
said exit 1 and the push went anyway, because the check and the push were in separate commands -- from here the push is chained on the
check's exit (`npm run check && git push`). Comment moved to the end of the line. (The same mistake as the cave's `ry`, once before.)

## m1122 -- HIGH BARS AT ANY HEIGHT (his: "Why do they only work at ground height?")

**Why:** `HBAR.h` (2.55) was one global number, and every bit of the bar code -- the catch, the swing circle, the hook, the hands' pose,
the finger curl -- measured from it as an absolute world height. So a bar could only exist 2.55 m above y = 0. Nothing deep; it was the
first thing built on a flat floor.
**Fix:** `hbarMake(x, z, yaw, y = 0, posts = 1)`; each bar carries `B.top = y + HBAR.h`, and everything between `hbarCatch` and
`hbarPose` reads `B.top` (all uses had `B` in scope). Old callers pass no `y` and are unchanged.
**Used:** the Watchtower's three perches each get a bar across the tip (2nd deck x2, lookout x1) on a timber footing that is walkable --
walk out, jump, catch, swing out over the drop. Removed with the tower (`bldClear` already handled `R.bars`).
Shipped unverified.

## m1107 -- the running jump-slash; flips that carry you where you flick

**What he said:** *"When I'm running and flick up on the right stick he just stops and hits with his sword... a lurch forward and down to
the ground -- a smaller version of the charge attack, only when actually running."* / *"the flips should be accompanied by a direction --
flip forward, he moves forward; flick left, he moves left... in guard, the front and back flips don't move him much."*

- **RUN SLASH (`RUNSLASH`, TOOLS > RUN SLASH):** blade out, on the ground, running over `minV` 4.2 m/s, not mid-chain, a flick UP = the charged
  swing's release at `k` .7 of a full charge (`chargeRelease`: at whoever is in front, the slash, the landing) plus a hop to `apex` 1.1 m, so he
  leaves the ground and the slash comes down with him. Not the standing chain's link 1. The deflect lock never applies (it wants a FULL
  charge). Real loop: at 7.2 m/s, a flick up -> the charged release, 11.6 m covered, apex 1.04 m.
- **AIR FLIPS MOVE (`airPush`):** every left-stick flick in the air adds `push` 6 m/s along the flick's world direction (his facing held, the
  horizontal capped at 9), and air steering is held off it for `pushHold` .8 s so it is not steered away. Real loop: a flick to his side took
  his side speed from 0 to 6.1 m/s.
- **GUARD FRONT / BACK FLIPS (`CART.vFB` 4.5 -> 6.5):** a front flip in guard now travels 4.1 m (was ~2.9).

perfect timing, or a fully charged lock."* (The charged 360 spin: back burner, his words.)

- **Threats** are the turret's shots and the archers' arrows that are still coming: not stuck, not already sent back, and passing within
  `missR` 1.6 m of him (a shot that will miss is not a target).
- **The swipe** (`meleeGo0`): a flick within `cone` 1.15 rad of a threat that reaches him inside `tta` .75 s / `reach` 7 m turns to where it
  will be, does NOT lunge at a man, and anything inside `catchR` 1.7 m of his chest in front while the swing is live goes back
  (`deflectThreat`: rockets to their turret, arrows to their archer, a little faster). The swing's own sweep catches arrows now too.
- **The charge lock** (`deflStep`): while the blade charges, the threat nearest his aim (left stick, else his nose, `lockCone` .7 /
  `lockR` 16 m) wears a pulsing gold ring that turns WHITE when the charge is full. Released FULL, the dash goes for it, and when it is inside
  `catchR` it goes home PERFECT: back at its shooter at x1.45, a white flash, hitstop.
- **A returned arrow** hits any body it reaches (6 damage, a launch); it never hurts him.

**Real loop:** rockets (`defl.cjs`): 3 swipes thrown 40 deg off the rocket, 3 turned to it, 2 sent back. Arrows (`defla.cjs`): one swipe
caught an arrow and it went back into an archer; the other test arrows were misses that passed 1.1-2.2 m wide, which is why `missR` exists.
Charge (`deflc.cjs`, the right pad really held): locked and ringed while charging; full, released at a rocket 4-12 m out: the dash met it 12
frames later, PERFECT, and it went back and destroyed the turret.

knock six + `bow_draw` 1.07 s (Standing Draw Arrow), `bow_overdraw` 3.8, `bow_recoil` .73, `bow_aim` 3.8, the four aim-walks, `bow_idle`,
`bow_equip`, `bow_shoot`), left hand on the grip. The kind (`ARENA.kinds.ARCHER`) names its own bake (`K.forged`, new: `forgedMerge` /
`knockAct` read it before the file's stem).

**What he does (`ARCH`, `archerAI`, `archerBow`, `ARROWS`, `arrowStep`, SPAWN > ARCHERS):** 4 a tap, on the dais edge across from you. He

HORDE: SLICE they come apart. RED: the rival's YIQ hue turn at +28 deg on its own uniform, plus a multiply. The first try (-15, then -40)
came out YELLOW. The direction was settled offline through the shader's own matrices: orange hue 34 -> +28 deg ~5.

**Real loop (`archer.cjs`, 4 archers, you standing in the middle):** all four held 13 m; 10 s: 8 arrows, 5-6 hit, the rest stuck in the
floor. The aim offset off his nose measured 1 deg (the stance aims along his nose). Renders: the bow in his left fist, strung to his right
hand, the glowing nocked arrow, an arrow in flight.

**What was wrong:** a horde body is not an arena body, so `bodyLaunch` put `d.hp` back to the kind's on every knock-down and the get-up
refilled it. Nothing ever ended one.

**What changed (`HORDE.life`, `d.hordeHp`, `hordeDie`, `HORDE.slice`, TOOLS > HORDE):** each body carries `life` 8 of damage in the same

slice dummy (`limbs: 1`), so every katana cut also takes an arm or a leg and the last one blows him up. The HORDE button reads
`<n> left, <k> down`.

**Measured (`hdie.cjs`, 25 slicing samurai):** 179 draw calls with all 25 standing, the same as the plain horde. A body only costs extra
once a limb is CUT (each piece is a mesh of its own until it settles). Two 5-damage blows: down, lie, blown apart, 24 left, 1 down.

## m1100 -- the start-of-world stutters: every disguise skin is built behind the loading card now

**What he said:** *"When you load anything other than the arena, the white box or Weirdport, it does the glitchy load thing for like 10
glitches... why are those not warmed up, why didn't they load when the loading bar said loading?"*

**What was wrong (measured, `hitch.cjs`: every frame for 20 s after the card, with the renderer's program / texture / geometry counts):**
m965's warm-up already compiled the scene and uploaded every texture behind the card. What it did NOT cover was `WARM`: the DNA gun's
disguise skins, built in the BACKGROUND after boot, one kind per tick (`warmStep`). Each is a retarget of 135 clips (290-390 ms here) plus
the morph's measures, and they compiled 11 new shader programs as they went. One stutter per kind on the street, which is his "like 10".

**What changed (`warmBoot`, before `bootWarm`):** the whole queue runs BEHIND THE CARD, a kind per tick so the bar moves ("warming up
<name>"); the lazy knock bakes (m1099) are awaited there too. After: 0 skins built and +1 program in the 20 s after the card (was 11).
**The price is a longer load**: 19 kinds took 21 s on this container's software GPU. The phone should be much faster but that is his to
see. TOOLS > PRELOAD: ALL (no stutter) / FAST (the old background build, with the stutters).

## m1097 -- a running landing, sound that survives leaving the app, and the course pad off

**What he said:** *"the landing that we play is a stationary landing and if you're running... it just looks weird... there should be a
landing that you play when you're running."* / *"when I navigate away from the game and come back the sounds no longer play and I have to
restart."* / *"I keep running into a door... I just go to the acrobatics level... keep it locked to only when I spawn it."*

**1. RUNNING LANDING (`RUNLAND`, TOOLS > RUN LAND: DIP / STOP).** No rig of his has a moving-landing clip (checked every GLB: only
`landing_soft` / `landing_hard`, and Colin's own `landing_roll`). So a SOFT landing at more than `at` 2.5 m/s with the stick held plays
NO landing clip and keeps the full run speed (the old landing braked to .35 for its length). The cover duck's procedural knee-bend
(`duckPose`: feet kept where the run puts them, knees take the drop, spine curls) fires as a quick dip, `t` .2 s, `drop` .13 x height,
deeper for a harder fall (`fullV`). A high fall still rolls. Real loop: speed 7.2 before, 7.2 minimum after, no landing state,
dip weight peaked at .96.

**2. SOUND AFTER BACKGROUNDING (`sfxRevive`).** iOS suspends or 'interrupts' the AudioContext when the page goes away and never resumes it,
and `sfxWake` returned early once a context existed, so nothing ever resumed it. Now every touch (pointerdown and touchend) and the page
returning (visibilitychange, pageshow, focus) asks a stopped context to resume. If a touch still leaves it not running 0.4 s later, the
context is closed and rebuilt from the kept raw files, along with the persistent voices (the hum). `SFX.rebuilt` counts rebuilds. This
cannot be tested headless: it is his phone's call.

**3. THE COURSE PAD IS OFF (`COURSE.padOn` 0).** The dais ring no longer exists, so walking over it does nothing. The course boots from
SPAWN > COURSE only. `mel.COURSE.padOn = 1` brings the pad back.

## m1095 -- every cut of a multi-cut katana swing connects; the blue dragon's (and the dog's) padded clips trimmed to their real motion

*"A lot of the katana attacks are two strikes... only one of them registers."* / *"There's a bunch of extra frames on every animation in the
blue dragon, so when it runs it just floats, because the end of its animation finishes and it has all these extra frames baked on."*
- **Multi-hit:** a strike's hit window closed on its FIRST connect (`!p.melFired`), so a two- or three-cut clip only ever landed its first.
  It re-opens `STRIKE.rehit` .22 s after the last connect (`p.melHitT`); a man's own `cool` still guards a single cut counting twice.
  Measured (`multihit.cjs`, real loop, a held dummy): `katana_spin` 2 hits a swing (was 1), single cuts 1.
- **The padding** (`beastPrep`, `BEASTTRIM`): measured off the files -- every blue dragon clip is 5.03 s (the dog's 4.40); the dragon's RUN
  moves for .83 s. The old trim ("any change over 1e-4") found motion to the end because (a) the padding drifts a hair and (b) its LAST key
  snaps a few bones (.03-.045 at 5.03 s after 4 s of nothing). Now: the end is the last frame past 4% of the clip's own 90th-percentile
  motion, ignoring a blip in the final .07 s. In game: dragon run 5.03 -> .83, attack_air 1.83, attack_ground 1.53, idle 1.37, hit 1.0,
  dizzy 1.37, entrance 2.03; dog run .73, attack_1 1.23, hit .87. The mech dragon's clips were never padded.
- Next in his list: the fireball, aim at fliers, bosses that feel heavy (weak spots / armour / the dog's heads), the katana finisher flurry,
  the air stroke combo.
- Shipped unverified on the phone.

## m1092 -- the top speed is the medium run's own clip, sped up (TOOLS > TOP SPEED)

*"At medium speed his arms do a nice gait, hands near his hips. As soon as he goes faster his arms come up, elbows at a very tight angle...
why don't we just do the medium run, sped up, for the fast run?"* The STD set's top band was the library `Sprint` (`sprint_std`).
`GAIT.topRun` (default on): `runSetUse` registers a COPY of the run band's clip (`<run>^top` -- a separate action, so the run and top rows
can play at their own rates in one blend) and makes it the top band on the run's own measured ref and phase, allowed up to `topHi` 3x
(7.2 m/s on his 2.68 m/s run = 2.7x). The stride set's leap is off with it (its contact windows were measured on the stride clip).
Measured (`toprun.cjs`, real loop, STD, unarmed, full stick): at 7.2 m/s the top row `run_std^top` holds weight 1.0, the old run 0;
rendered two strides 7 frames apart (arms low, a long stride). TOOLS > TOP SPEED: RUN SPED UP / OWN CLIP (the old sprint). Shipped unverified.

*"Swipe left and right on the right stick should be a single sword spin, like Link in Smash Bros -- the full 360 -- rather than that kick.

## m1076 -- the samurai rival gets a brain: he runs in, reads you late (by level), spaces, and his chop breaks a turtled guard; difficulty is timing only

*"The samurai AI is stupid... make the difficulty just the timing -- when he swings, when he blocks... a fully functioning player... moderately
challenging, not so easy."*
- **What was wrong, measured** (`turtle.cjs`: MEDIUM, you holding the guard 12 s, real loop): **0 swings**, `stateFrames {idle 720}`. The arena
  gives every boss `notice` 60, and the generic walk-up only RUNS past `notice x V.dash` = **31 m** -- in a 17 m arena he WALKED at 1.1 m/s
  (trace: 0.38 m per 20 frames) and then circled. With the cover in, he also ground into a half wall at 7.8 m. Not a cover bug alone; no cover
  he still took 14 s to arrive and never swung.
- **`mirrorBrain` (samurai only, `K.mirror`)** replaces the generic approach. `mirrorSee` records you every frame; `mirrorSeen` hands him what
  you were doing `react` s ago. Runs in past `runAt` 4.2 m; stuck (`stuckT` > .35) he DETOURS (a side heading for .8 s, alternating) instead
  of grinding; outside reach he comes IN or STRAFES at `foot` 1 m outside it (`katana_strafe_l/r`, `katana_walk_b` for a step back); in reach
  he swings. A guard he has SEEN held `turtle` .45 s gets his chop (`KATANA.breakers`) every time -- was a dice roll on your live state.
- **`arenaMirror` reads the late picture too**: your slash -> his guard, your finisher/charge -> a roll, every time unless he MISREADS it
  (`misread`). After the guard he always counters if you are still in reach. A parry needs his guard up `parryLead` .12 s before your blow
  (then 35%), so a faster read parries more.
- **Difficulty = timing only** (`RIVALAI.lv`): EASY react .45 / think .55 / misread 30%, MEDIUM .25 / .32 / 15%, HARD .12 / .16 / 5%, plus the
  level's wind-up and recovery. `ARENA.duel.levels` lost `dmgK` differences (all 1), combo (all .3), rush speed (all 6) and the guard / parry /
  break / dodge CHANCES -- for every arena body, not just him.
- **Measured after** (same harness, MEDIUM, cover in): ran in, detoured round the half wall at x -4.5, `katana_down` at 6.0 s @2.0 m -> **guard
  broken** (`brk` 1, you thrown 8 m), walked back in, second `katana_down` at 11.1 s. EASY / HARD not run (same behaviour, other clocks).

## m1071 -- the katana's charge HOLDS until the thumb lifts, and the thumb's height AIMS it: up = the flat launch, lower = a higher leap + slam

*"I charge it up, it locks, and I slowly move my thumb back down to neutral or all the way to the bottom and it releases -- it shouldn't, I'm still
holding. What if as you move your thumb down you're aiming the height... move your thumb to the bottom and he launches really high in the air and
slams down."* (The rest of his message -- a move panel over the thumb after a charge, Android-unlock-style swipe patterns, unlockable moves --
is ideas for later, not this build.)

  While held, the guard cannot arm (`busy` gains a held katana charge). The high-jump crouch / ninja sprint cannot either (`R.far`).

  an arc of orange dots shows the leap before he goes.

  solved from the slam's clock to land where the flat launch would have (the man in reach, or the hold's distance) -- carried by `p.cLeap`
  (m1065's) from the first frame. Thumb up -> the flat launch exactly as before.
- **Real loop (`kaim.cjs`, goblin, katana, charge 0.83 s with the thumb up, then 30 frames at the new height, then lift):** thumb up -> held,
  aim 0, flat launch 10.68 m. Neutral -> HELD (no release), aim .30, arc shown, leap apex 2.47 m, slam 11.42 m out. Bottom -> HELD, aim 1, arc
  shown, apex 5.08 m, slam 11.25 m out. Guard never armed. Render: up past 4.7 m, katana overhead.

  in some states; it runs at frame level now (after `stepKit`). (2) Even then it drew: `show` was the NUMBER 0, and three skips an object only
  when `visible === false` -- `!!` it. Re-rendered: arc false from the release on.
- Shipped unverified on the phone.

## m1067 -- rockets launch you (even in GOD), you land and get up (no juggling); guard turn un-inverted; rockets reflect off the blade; steel flash

*"Have the turret actually launch my character through the air when the rockets hit him and explode. He lands on the ground and you can get up.

  across the blade turns round, the part along it carries on (it glances down the blade), x `SHOTBLOCK.rest` .8; then ballistic
  (`S.ric`: gravity `grav` 9.8, the rocket tumbling, smoke). m1029's random side angle and its sine wobble (`S.sput`) are gone from the
  block. The perfect block still sends it home.

  every shot block (bigger on a perfect one).

  (M1061's state): before -- hands **1.64 m** off the bar, his up-axis **-0.59** (tipped over); after -- .09 m, upright. Caught mid air flip,

## m1055 -- why the climb / vault looked unchanged on the phone: every "measuring pass" read NOTHING after boot. Fixed; bar grip on a switch

*"In the screenshots you sent, climbing and hurdling looked super good... but in the game it's exactly the same... and the hands on the bar look
weird, it almost looked better."* **The harness was right and the game was not running what it tested.** Played through the REAL frame loop
after boot (scratch `game.cjs`: `frameBody`, the left stick pushed into the beam's platform, the right-pad tap): the climb began, held him at
the floor for the whole pull and popped him up on the last frame. `mantleCurve` measured the hands FLAT (1.25 -> 0.95 everywhere; `rel` 1).
**Cause:** the measuring passes (`gaitMeasure`'s pattern: zero every action's weight, put one at 1, step the mixer at each time) never ENABLED
the measured action. Before boot every action is enabled (the harness ran there); in play an action not in use is disabled, so the mixer
applied nothing and the pass read the bind pose. **Fix:** the measured action is enabled / unpaused / started for the pass, and every action's
`enabled` / `paused` is saved and put back with its weight and time -- in `mantleCurve`, `vaultHips`, `vaultLift`, `hbarReach`, `beamToeH`
and `gaitMeasure` (and the save/restore in the arena's measure). **After, in the real loop:** the climb rises 0 -> 1.0 over the pull and
crosses the edge (no pop); the vault reads its real hand / hip travel (hands .57 -> .67, hips +.83) and carries him over.
**The lesson:** a harness that runs before boot can pass what play fails -- run the moves through `frameBody` after `rig.ready`.
- **Bar grip:** he preferred the look before m1052 (which was the wrists, by accident). TOOLS > BAR GRIP WRIST (default) / PALM.
- Shipped unverified on the phone.

## m1034 -- THE HIGH BAR (scaffold): SPAWN > HIGH BAR; jump to catch, HOLD the right pad to pump into giant swings, let go to fly off

*"Jump up onto a bar... press and hold, and as you press and hold he pumps once, pumps twice, and the third one goes around until he's looping,

## m1023 -- the cover arm, again: axes measured off his shoulders, the elbow bent so the weapon is held UP

## m1022 -- one weapon size on every body, held every frame (the launcher shrank after a disguise and back)

*"I am the goblin... I turned into him and then back into a goblin and my rocket launcher was super tiny... It needs to be a
consistent size no matter what -- a small character, the launcher is huge; a big character, it's small. That's the fun of it."*
- **Why:** m968's `WEAP.unit` (one weapon-file unit = .01321 m on every hero) was applied ONCE, in `mountWeapon`. The disguise's
  re-host (the m925 block, `w.group.scale = tip / fileTip`) re-sized the weapons by the BORROWED rig's tip ratio, and the revert did
  the same on the way back, so the absolute size was lost.
- **Fix:** `weapUnitKeep` runs after the mixer every frame: each visible worn weapon with `userData.unit` is re-sized to
  `WEAP.unit / its hand's world scale` (when it is off by more than .5%), and its muzzle (mount space) re-derived from `muzzleFile`
  with it. Any body, any disguise, any re-host -- the launcher is the same metres long.
- Shipped unverified.

## m1021 -- the left flick never breaks a wall (cover, or a slide); repaired bricks arc up off the ground into place; the air slam smashes down through a wall

*"when I'm unarmed and I'm using the left stick flick, instead of covering on the wall he just does the melee stuff and breaks the wall.
Breaking the wall should be reserved for right stick... make the bricks, when you're repairing, do this arc thing like in Fortnite...
when you jump in the air and do a slam down on a wall, it doesn't break down through the wall."*
- **Left flick:** `slideGo` refuses while a swing / roll / landing plays, so a flick thrown mid-acrobatics fell through to MORE
  acrobatics, which `wallMelee` let break the wall. Now cover found down the flick (`coverSeek`) cuts whatever is playing and slides in;
  a breakable wall there that is NOT cover (full height, `wallAhead`) gets a slide (or the roll), never a strike; the left pad's slides
  are `slide.soft` (no `wallHit`) and its strikes `p.melFist` (`wallMelee` returns) -- carried through the queue (`p.melQf`).
  Breaking is the right pad's: its strikes, its down-flick slide tackle, the charge, the slam.
- **Repair arc:** `wallRepair` no longer pops the chunk in: `repairFly` starts it on the ground on his side of the wall (up to `REPFLY.out`
  .9 m out, a little scatter, a puff of dust) and `repairFlyStep` arcs it home over .42 s (`peak` .7 m), tumbling to square and growing
  from .75 to full; the sparks + clang land with it. Drawn only -- the collider is back the moment the repair is taken. Broken again in
  flight: dropped.
- **Slam:** driven down, `wallHit(..., 'blast')` under his soles every frame (radius .55, 99 dmg), grid rebuilt that frame so
  `integrate` does not stand him on it -- he goes down THROUGH; `slamLand` then hits the walls within 1.1 m (3 dmg).
- Shipped unverified.

## m1020 -- the weapon reach plays in cover (its top half over the cover legs); the weapon arm lifts off his side in cover (TOOLS > ARM)

*"make the hybrid take the torso-up animation from the weapon change so you can play it while he's in cover... when he's in cover and

  never rewound -- so the reach could start mid-clip anywhere. `swapGo` starts `__ups` too.
- **The arm:** `coverArm` turns the right upper arm OUT from his side (`CARM.out`, default 25 deg, about his own forward) and FORWARD
  12 deg (about his right), after the mixer, eased with crouched cover while something is in the hand, not while popped up or
  swapping; `coverArmUndo` takes it off before the next mixer pass (`spineUndo`'s pattern -- the mixer does not rewrite an unchanged
  bone, so an edit left on accumulates). Signs derived: +X is his left, so about +forward a negative turn takes the right arm away.
  TOOLS > ARM 0 / 15 / 25 / 35 (0 = off), remembered.
- Headless: boots clean; the harness could not seat him in cover this pass (stale `mel.rig`), so nothing about the pose is checked.
- Shipped unverified. If the arm goes INTO him instead of out, the sign is the one thing to flip.

## m1019 -- TOOLS > SWING: the katana's swing set is his pick (ORIG / WHOLE / CUT / FISTS), default ORIG

*"maybe we just go to kind of the original katana attacks before they were chopped up... or we just use like the unarmed attack, but
with the katana for now... the original katana attacks weren't that bad. It's just that they were kind of long."* A taste call, so a switch.
- **ORIG** (default) = the m1014 chains WHOLE: right/left the big 360 spin and its mirror, up spin -> slash_1 -> combo3, down slash_3 ->

## m1016 -- walls break in PIECES on a frame that stays; every strike meets the wall in front of it; repair by holding the left pad still

*"He'll do a crazy flip and the wall does nothing, then an uppercut breaks bricks... I want the wall to take damage before it's gone, pieces
flying off so you can still cover on it, a frame left like the kit city... a rocket blows it, a pistol takes a few hits... repair like Fortnite,
hold down on the stick and it rebuilds... half walls: can't be shot, but you can melee through them."*
- **The wall** (`coverBlocks`, `CWALL`): each block is a grid of CHUNKS (.6 m x ~.3 m, one InstancedMesh per wall) between a FRAME that never
  breaks: a .2 m sill and an end post each side (3 meshes). Every chunk is its own collider box with 2 hit points; a chunk with nothing under
  it comes down too (holes go up). Cover reads the COLUMN's standing height (`wallColTop` in `lowFind`), so a full wall with its top shot off
  is crouch cover, and a half wall with a hole in it is cover either side of the hole.
- **`wallHit`** is the one entry: 'shot' = the nearest chunk, never a HALF wall (shots fly over those, `b.half`); 'melee' = the nearest two;
  'blast' = every chunk in the radius. A bolt is 1 + its charge (two bolts to a chunk), a rocket a 1.3 m blast of 3, the katana's charged
  slam a blast, the turret's shots the same as his.
- **Every strike meets the wall** (`wallMelee`): from just before the blow, the first chunk within reach in front of him (.65 m, the
  katana 1 m, at three heights) takes it, once per strike, whatever the move -- the swept-limb test only ever touched a wall with the
  FASTEST limb inside its window, and a flip's fast foot is over the wall. The slide tackle (when it is a tackle, not a slide into cover)
  chews through what is in front of it.
- **REPAIR** (`wallRepair`): the LEFT pad held STILL (its free slot) for .4 s within 2.4 m of a broken wall puts back the nearest missing
  chunk every .16 s, bottom first, with a blue spark.
- Old block-at-a-time code (`coverHurt` / `coverBolt` / `coverMelee`) is gone. `WALLS` was already the kit's, so this is `CWALL`, declared
  above `ARENA` (the arena stage builds it at LOAD: the m1008 blank-page trap, which `check:boot` cannot see).
- **Checked headless:** 4 walls, 72 boxes; 6 bolts on the full wall -> 25/30, + a rocket -> 6/30 (frame standing); a shot at a half wall ->
  untouched; Zap's flip (`melee_01`) into a half wall -> 8/10; cover on the damaged wall; holding the left pad 80 frames -> 10/10.
- **Open (his call):** with the left flick now cover-or-acrobatics and the right pad melee-only, the slide TACKLE is only reachable with
  TOOLS > LEFT ROLL. A flick at a wall is always the slide INTO cover.

## m1015 -- swings chain: one strike per swipe (the katana's clips cut into single strikes), a queued swipe cuts the recovery, and the SMEAR

*"Make it so you can interrupt animations, or speed them up, or chop the ends off... there's a stutter step at the end of every one, he lands and
adjusts his feet back... one attack per swing so you're button-smashing swipe swipe swipe... cut them up, play different ones every time... and
we never did the smear technique."*
- **One strike per swipe** (`strikeSplit`, at load): each katana clip in the direction pools is played on the bind-ready rig and its RIGHT
  HAND's speed (relative to the hips) sampled at 30 fps. Every separate peak over 45% of the clip's fastest is a strike; each is cut out
  (`clipCut`) from .42 s before its peak to .3 s after, never past the quiet before the next one, as `<clip>#<k>`, with its own `at` (the
  peak). A single-strike clip is cut too, which is what takes the foot re-set off its end. Measured on the goblin: `360h` 1, its mirror 2,
  `spin` 2, `slash_1` 4, `combo3` 3, `slash_3` 2, `down` 1, `jump_attack` 4. The pools are rebuilt from the pieces and dealt ROUND (no two
  in a row the same); left / right now hold three clips each (`360h`, `horiz`, `backhand` and their mirrors). The finishers / guard breakers
  read the base name (`baseNm`).
- **A queued swipe cuts the recovery** (`MELEE.cancel` .14): past the blow (`at` + .14 of the strike), a flick that is waiting takes
  over at once. Headless: a spin piece cut into the next strike at 19 frames (30 alone).
- **The SMEAR** (`smearMat` / `smearStep`, TOOLS > SMEAR): the weapon's vertex shader knows each vertex's world position last frame; the
  trailing ones (normal facing away from the motion) are pulled back along it by 2.2 frames' worth, broken up with noise, at most 1.1 m.
  Only while a strike, the charge or the slam plays. Checked: all 5 katana meshes carry it, it compiles, `uSmear` 2.08 mid-swing with the
  blade moving .14 m a frame. Whether it LOOKS right is his call on the phone.

  .2 s). Also `mixNow`: every Forge layer re-writes every binding after its mixer update, because three's PropertyMixer skips a bone whose

## m1012 -- the launcher twitch in cover (a Forge bug, every hero, every clip), the right-pad swipe DOWN slides, a LEFT TAP takes cover, cover in/out 4x faster, the pop-up drops the moment the shot leaves

- **The twitch.** *"Holding the rocket launcher in cover, every round of the animation it twitches, like the hand snaps back."* Measured:
  in every baked clip of every pipeline hero, KEY 1 of each hand was 45 deg off keys 0 and 2. The Forge's `wristLayer` (m998's "wrists
  out" 45) writes its turn onto the bone, and the mixer does NOT rewrite a bone whose sampled value is unchanged from the last frame
  (a clip that holds its first frames still), so the next frame turned it AGAIN. Isolated by baking one clip at wrists 0 (steps 0.0)
  and 45 (45.0 / 44.6). Fix: the bone is put back after each frame's read; also the turn's direction is decided ONCE per clip (it
  was per frame, and a crouched hand's two turns tie). After: `cover_idle` max hand step 0.3 deg, `idle_01` 2.3. samurai / orc /
  goblin re-baked. (Left for later: three clips with 120-178 deg left-hand steps -- `weapon_swap`, `weapon_melee_01`/`_finish` --
  a different layer, not this one.)
- **The right pad's DOWN flick = the SLIDE** (`downSlide`), standing or running, in the way he is going (his nose when still), into
  cover if a half block is that way. Unarmed, blaster, launcher; the katana keeps its own down (Zap's acrobatics) for now. In the
  air down is still the slam.
- **A LEFT TAP within `COVER.tapR` (1.4 m) of a half block takes cover on it** (`coverTap`), at once; in cover a left tap stands him
  out. Otherwise the left tap still jumps.
- **Faster:** cover in .55 -> .22 s, out .75 -> .2 s (*"way, way faster"*).
- **The pop-up drops the moment the shot leaves** (`p.wallPop` = the trigger HELD; it was `committed()`, which holds on after a shot).
- **Checked headless** (goblin, blaster): a left tap beside the block -> `hold` in 14 frames; trigger -> popped; released -> down 2 frames
  later; a right down flick standing -> sliding.

  takes him out of cover on the spot and swings. Headless: flick in cover -> `katana_360h` once -> `katana_idle` 200 frames on.

  flank) = a wall that stops shots, with no crouched cover. *"Nothing ballistic runs into the half-height cinderblocks; they run into
  the full-height ones."* Half blocks carry `b.half`, which `boltBox` and `boxRay` skip; walking and the camera still treat them as solid.

  enemy). The dragon's lobbed fireball still lands, since it is not a flat shot. No arena enemy fires flat yet, so this mostly waits

## m1007 -- THE NINJA SPRINT: hold the right pad still while moving = her arms-back run, fast, with a wider lens and speed lines; let go and tap = the long jump

*"There's this one run where both of her arms are back... when you hold down the right stick she does this run... you go really
fast... if you're just still and you hold that button he'll do the wind-up for the big tall jump... if you're running and you hold

Mario."*

  played and both hands' position along the body's forward (the head's lean past the hips) averaged over the cycle. Only
  `Running_Arc` holds both hands behind the hips with a hard forward lean, and its description is *Female Ninja Run Arc Right*.

  straight line and taken out, and so is the curve of the travel that remains, so it runs straight.

  stick is pushed past `NINJA.minMag` = `p.ninja`. Held still with the left stick idle it is still the backflip's duck. Letting go
  does nothing and opens `NINJA.win` (.4 s); a tap inside it is the long jump.

  2.08 m/s on the goblin) with its own clamp (`tsHi` 3.4, anime legs; the gait's 1.6 would slide the feet). The lens widens by
  `fov` 9 and SPEED LINES fade in at the screen's edge (`ninjaLines`: one CSS div, no draw call).

  state owns the body and bled the speed to 3 m/s), and the speed held to the landing (`p.ljump`).

## m1006 -- mirrored clips (`clipMirror`): the left spin and the left air spin kick; the landing roll only from a real fall; the katana slam lands in its own clip; the blade leaned back on the run

- **Mirror.** *"The spin attack only goes one direction despite which direction you flick it... it should be mirrored."* Left was
  `katana_360l`, a LOW spin the same way round. `clipMirror` builds the mirror at load, on the bind pose. Per frame, each bone's
  turn from its rest in the model frame (D = Q W^-1) is reflected across x (q -> (x, -y, -z, w)) and given to the opposite bone over
  ITS rest. That holds whatever way an auto-rig's left and right axes point; the Hips' travel is flipped too. `MIRROR.clips` =
  `katana_360h`, `hurricane_kick` -> `_m`. Left flick = `katana_360h_m`. Headless: right and left spin, front view, the same
  moments read as reflections, body intact.
- **Air left / right = the spin kick** (`MELEE.spinKick`): the library's `hurricane_kick` (in place, 1.87 s), its .12-.78
  stretch in .65 s; right flick the clip, left the mirror. Up in the air is still the flying kick, down still the slam.
- **The roll.** *"He does a roll every time he lands... it should only be from a certain distance."* `MOVE.hardLand` 8 -> 11 m/s.
  An ordinary jump (apex 1.6 m at g 20) lands at exactly 8.0, so 8 rolled him off nearly every jump; 11 is a fall of about 3 m.
- **The slam.** *"The sword slam gets cut off early because he goes into the roll."* `slamLand` always handed to `landing_hard`.
  Now a slam with its own clip (the katana's `katana_jump_attack`) plays on from where the fall left it, for what is left of it,
  as the landing (`p.landClip`). The impact, the shockwave and the mark are unchanged.
- **The blade on the run** (`katRunTilt`, TOOLS > TILT 0/30/45/60, default 45): the Great Sword run holds the blade straight up by
  his head. Now it leans back over his shoulder, weighted by `katana_run`'s own mixer weight; the left hand follows the grip.
  Checked side-on: back, not forward.
- **His hands question** (re-rigging himself): see the reply. The pipeline takes a rigged file at the `arp2mix` step.

- **Hands.** *"Their hands are always really messed up... the big red orc's idle pose, his right hand is super messed up... like

  2. The Forge curls a mitt chain like three finger joints, which folds a whole glove-mitt under the palm (the little hand).

  hero. So the cause is not the bake, and I am asking him which run, sword or not, and when.
- **`pipeline/hero.sh`** (blender-addons): his zip -> game GLB in one command, every step and fix above in it, so the next hero
  is not done by hand. Written from the steps run on these two; not yet run end to end.

## m1003 -- every strike goes where he faces; the left-hand grip is the stance only; the door walk loops; the samurai leaps out

- **Unarmed (and every) strike by facing (`MELEE.dirBy` 'face').** *"Implement the same technique with the unarmed melee so it follows
  the orientation of the character locomotion rather than the swipe direction."* m1000's katana rule (the stick's heading when
  moving, his nose when still), and m1001's flying kick along his velocity, now apply to every slot. `'flick'` brings back the
  camera-relative way. The flick still picks WHICH chain plays.
- **The left-hand grip is the idle / walk / run only.** *"I just wanted that one adjusted... the idle, or where he's walking around
  holding the sword."* m999/m1001 held the hand on the hilt for everything that was not a jump, including the charge wind-up, the
  roll and the swings. Its weight is now the sum of the mixer's own weights on `katana_idle` / `_walk` / `_run`, whole-body actions
  only (an upper-body move puts the `__legs` halves in, and those do not count), and it is zero in any melee, roll, slam or charge.
  So it hands back at the rate the body does.
- **The CEO froze and slid out of the door.** `enter_walk` was never in `bodyLoops`, so it played once and clamped on its last frame
  while `arenaEnter` kept moving him. Measured headless: the walk now cycles 0.08 to 0.83 four times on the way to the taunt.
- **The samurai's door leap was his idle pose.** He has no `enter_leap`, and the fallback was the idle on a parabola. Now the kind
  has `leap: { clip: 'katana_runjump', w0 .25, w1 .47, arc 3.2, end .62 }`. w0 and w1 are measured off the clip's hips (up at .25,
  down at .47), and `arc` is the lift the in-place clip does not carry. Headless: runjump plays, peak y 2.6, lands at r 9.

## m1002 -- THE DRINK CRASH: a cached vector kept on `userData` does not survive a clone (`handFrame`'s mitt forward)

*"I got this when I had the katana out and I tried to pick up a drink to throw at the CEO"* -- FRAME `handFrame` <- `socketAuto`
<- `pickHolder`. **Reproduced headless before the fix** (arena, samurai, CEO spawned, katana drawn, a can at his feet, `pickTap`):
`TypeError: mittFwd(...).clone is not a function`, every frame, and the cup never reached his hand.
- **The cause:** m997 cached the mitt's bind forward as a `Vector3` on `hand.userData._mittT`. three's `Object3D.copy` deep-copies
  userData **through JSON**, so any rig cloned after the cache was set (the mirror samurai, the disguise, the Forge's copies) has
  hands carrying a plain `{x, y, z}` with no methods. Any mitt hand going through `socketAuto` after a clone threw.
- **The fix:** the cache is a `WeakMap` keyed on the bone (`handFrame._mitt`), which a clone cannot copy. And the bind search
  stops at the top of his own model, never the whole scene, passing over any skin with no usable inverse for this hand.
  `tools/forgesync.mjs --write` carried it into `forge/core.js`.
- **Checked after the fix:** the same run ends `carry true`, with no throw. **Never cache a three.js object in `userData`.**
