## m997 -- THE SPINNING LAUNCHER (a mitt's hand frame, read through the CURRENT turn), AND THE FLYING KICK FLIES LEVEL
*"When the samurai holds the rocket launcher, it's just perpetually spinning... maybe fix the spinning first."* And: *"if I'm in the air
and do a flying kick, he should launch straight forward -- the downward trajectory shouldn't matter. Unrealistic, but more fun."*
- **FOUND BY STEPPING AT 60 FPS**: the launcher's world turn alternated between two orientations every frame (y -4 / +64 deg); his root
  was steady; per bone, only `mixamorig_RightHand`'s LOCAL rotation flipped -- 70 deg every frame. In the FILE: his `rocket_launcher` is
  a two-key pose whose two hand keys differ by 70 deg (and `idle_rifle`'s hand had a 154 deg step, `shoot` 68, `rifle_run` 63).
- **CAUSE**: `handFrame`'s MITT branch (m978, the samurai has one finger chain) took world +Z through the hand's CURRENT world turn --
  right only in the T-pose. Animated, the frame turned with the world instead of with the hand, so in the Forge's `weapLayer` the
  weapon's wanted turn changed with the pose and the arm solve chased it. Now read at BIND (the skin's inverse bind for that bone),
  cached on the bone (`mittFwd`). Shared text: the game and the Forge (`forgesync --write`).
- **AND `weapLayer` TURNS, REACHES, AND TURNS AGAIN** (3 passes): solving the arm swings the hand, so the turn set before `legTo` was
  undone by it (the left hand already re-took its turn; the right did not).
- Re-forged: every right-hand step in his weapon clips under 4 deg (launcher pose 0.0); in game the hand moves < .5 deg a frame with the
  launcher out (was 70). Screenshots: the launcher sits on his right shoulder beside his head, as on Zoar.
- **THE FLYING KICK** (`MELEE.kickLevel` 1): its vertical is held at 0 while it lasts (one frame of gravity pre-paid so `integrate`
  nets zero), then he falls. Stepped: kicked while falling at 6 m/s from 3 m -> held at 2.53 m, 9.5 m/s forward, for its .85 s
  (`MELEE.airDur`) -- ~8 m of level flight; `airDur` / `airV` are the dials if that is too far.

## m996 -- THE SPRINT'S STUTTER, CAUGHT AT 60 FPS: leftover root motion (a sawtooth) and a bad first frame (`clipSeam`)
*"With the run sequence there's still a duplicate frame and a camera stutter... the last frame is a little farther forward, hips-wise,
than the first -- a subtle stutter and a duplicate frame at the same time."* (Two screenshots .02 s apart: the same pose, the world moved.)
- **HOW IT WAS FOUND**: `mel.frameBody` (exported for this) stepped by hand at an exact 60 fps with a mocked clock, unarmed, full stick:
  the hips' forward offset from his root, every frame. `sprint_std` crept ~16 cm forward across its 0.57 s cycle and snapped back in
  ONE frame at every wrap (12-16 cm, where every other frame moves 1-2). Headless real-time runs at ~2 fps and could never show it.
- **CAUSE 1 -- THE SAWTOOTH**: the Forge takes a clip in place by the drift from its FIRST key to its LAST. Since m992 kept the closing
  key, the last key is a full copy of the first, ROOT INCLUDED -- so the drift read zero and the Sprint's travel stayed in.
  Now FITTED (least squares over every key but the closing one) on the level axes, taken out, centred on the root, closing key = first.
- **CAUSE 2 -- A BAD FIRST FRAME**: the same sprint's key 0 sits ~14 cm off the path (its first hips step ~10x the clip's median). On a
  closed loop that happens, key 0 is dropped and the loop closes on key 1.
- **SCOPE**: m996's first pass ran both on EVERY clip -- falls, get-ups, attacks, dances -- and moved them (caught in the touched-clip
  list). Now: only LOOPS (every bone ends near its start, relative to its own steps, and the hips end near where they began), and the
  hips fixes only for LOCOMOTION cycles (`SEAM.cyc` walk/run/sprint/strafe/stride/skate push/ladder, not turns/jumps/attacks). On the
  samurai: bad first frame on `sprint_std` alone; drift taken out of 45 locomotion clips.
- **AFTER**: sprint_std across the wrap -1.0 -> -0.7 -> -0.2 -> +0.4 cm (smooth, centred). katana_run: smooth except a ~2 cm hips hop in
  its closing interval (.60 -> .633 s) -- the library's Great Sword run does not quite meet itself; not touched (blending the last
  frames into the first is the fix if he still sees it).

## m995 -- THE KATANA RUN'S SLIDE, SWIPES GO WHERE YOU FLICK (camera-relative), THE AIR SLAM CARRIES YOUR MOMENTUM
*"At the end of every cycle he stutters back... it doesn't happen on the walking cycle... the swipe is not in relation to the camera
-- I swipe towards the enemy and he goes in relation to the character... in the air, swipe down and he just goes straight down; carry
his velocity... the original animation jumps up, brings the sword over his head and stabs down -- initiate it by which part of the
jump you're at."*
- **THE RUN**: ruled out by measurement -- the loop seams (0.0 cm at every wrap since m992), the hips' surge (katana_run 9.9% of leg vs
  the library source's 9.2%, Zoar's run 8.4%), the sprint's leap rhythm (not used in the katana stance). Found: **the katana stance has
  no sprint**. `katana_run` sells 3.53 m/s (`KATANA.refs.run`, planted-foot) x `GAIT.tsHi` 1.6 = 5.6 m/s; at `MOVE.max` 7.2 the clip
  was capped and the planted foot slid ~27% every stride. With the katana out his top speed is now what the run can show
  (`KATANA.runK` x that). **If the hitch is still there at a slower top speed, it is in the clip itself** -- next step would be
  looking at Great_Sword_Run_1's own frames (a skip in the source) or trying Great_Sword_Run's partner clips.
- **SWIPES ARE CAMERA-RELATIVE AGAIN**: `flickH` (the flick's screen direction through the camera) was being thrown away for the
  katana (m978: "he strikes where he faces"; m993: where he moves). Now the flick IS the direction: the magnetism cone (60 deg, 3.5 m)
  centres on it, he turns to it and lashes. The flick's screen direction still picks the chain.
- **THE AIR SLAM** (`slamGo`, every weapon): `SLAM.keep` .25 -> **1** and the per-frame horizontal bleed 4 -> **.5** /s, so your
  forward momentum carries. Flicked RISING he rides the jump to its top, then drives; flicked FALLING he drives at once (`hangFall`
  .04). AIMED: a body within 5 m and 50 deg of where he travels bends his path to land on it (horizontal only, up to 9 m/s).
  **With the katana it plays `katana_jump_attack`** (Great Sword Jump Attack: up, sword overhead, the strike down), entered at .22
  of the clip rising / .40 falling and paced so the measured strike (.53, the hand's speed peak) lands as he does.
  Headless (6 m/s forward): rising carried 3.3 m, falling .9 m (from 1.5 m up), and with a Warboss 4 m ahead and off the line he
  landed 1.0 m from it (its body's edge). Before: .25 kept then bled at 4/s.

## m994 -- THE FORGE ANCHORS A HELD WEAPON AT THE SHOULDER, BY ARM LENGTH (the samurai's rocket launcher)
*"I pulled out the rocket launcher as the samurai and he's holding it like crazy... I was really hoping that once we solve whatever
the problem is that happens every time we apply the same animations to a new character, it'd be implemented in the Forge, so you
don't have to tell your AI to manually solve it."*
The Forge's `weapLayer` (m794) already drives a held weapon by POSITION: the donor's weapon read in his chest frame, put in the same
place on the new body, the arms solved to it. What carried the donor's proportions was the SCALING: offsets from between the
shoulders, across x shoulder width, up/forward x SPINE. Old Zap (the donor) is a short spine under a big head, so on the samurai's
long robot torso the forward offset blew up -- the launcher a forearm out in front of his face, arms reaching (screenshots). Zoar
had needed a typed `x: .6` for the same reason.
- **`WEAPANCHOR.def` 'shoulder'**: offsets from the HOLDING shoulder's joint, every axis x ARM LENGTH (upper arm + forearm) -- the
  arm is what decides where a hand can be, on any body. `W.anchor: 'chest'` is the old rule; `W.x/y/z` still multiply on top.
- Zoar's profile pins `anchor: 'chest'` on his tuned launcher clips (his look kept on any re-bake).
- Re-forged the samurai (100 clips), resize/webp/draco, `hipshift`. Screenshots (before/after, 3/4 and side): the launcher comes back
  from in front of his face to up by his head and shoulder, arms no longer at full reach. It still sits a little further forward
  than Zoar's -- his head sits low between big shoulder pads; that is his build, not a per-character number.

*"This shows his gait, it's still super weird... the rival is basically dark, almost black, instead of tinted or hue shifted...
when you flick the swing, games have you lash toward the character... an assist... I was just standing there swinging... if I swing

      stance (hip widths)   Great_Sword_Run_1 1.12 | his katana_run **1.98** | Great_Sword_Walk 1.13 | his katana_walk **1.72**
  The Forge's FOOT CLEARANCE layer (m939, for the CEO's thick legs) read his armour/sheath as leg thickness and spread his feet to

  own 2 / 25 and 1 / 25; run_std 1.15 against Zoar's 1.22. **A body with armour or props at the hips: check `clear` first.**
- **THE RIVAL**: the tint was a multiply (`material.color` 0x4d5463), which can only darken an orange texture. Now a HUE rotation in

- **MAGNETISM** (`KATANA.lock`): the katana aimed where he FACED, inside 34 deg and ~2.7 m, and spread its travel over the whole

## m992 -- THE SAMURAI, ROUND TWO: the run's pop (loops must CLOSE), 3-hit chains per direction, the charge = the guard, knees out
*"Stutter on the run, or he's moving slightly during the run and then pops back... flicking forward his first swing just butts the
sword... I can only get through two... at least three if not four or five... the charge: you just turned the sword backwards, it
looks messed up -- use the same animation as the parry for now... his knees point inward, knock knees, like the CEO."*
- **THE POP WAS m960's FIX (and m991's).** three.js wraps a loop's TIME: past the last key it holds it, and at `duration` jumps to
  the first. With the "duplicate" closing key that jump lands on the same pose; trimmed, the last-to-first step happens in zero
  time -- a skipped frame of motion every cycle (1/22 of the run). Measured on the game's own clips (scratch mixer, his model):
  run_std's loop jumped 2.0 cm at the hips and 11.4 cm at the foot in one instant. **`clipSeam` now CLOSES loops**: a loop-shaped
  clip (per bone: first-vs-last within 2.5 x its own largest step) that is open (some bone's gap > .5 x its own MEAN step) gets its
  first pose back at last + one key. Per bone, because run_std has one bone with a 98 deg step that made the whole clip look closed.
  After: run_std, walk_fwd, sprint_std, katana_run, katana_walk all wrap with 0.0 cm. The Forge's `loopSeam` is OFF (`SEAM.on`).
  **Do not trim a seam again** -- the duplicate frame is not a hitch for an interpolating player.
- **THE CHAINS**: one flick slot (`p.melQ`) meant flicks 2 and 3 thrown during swing 1 were ONE queued flick -- "only two". It
  counts now (`MELEE.queue` 2). Each direction is its own 3-hit chain with its own finisher, the hilt butt (`katana_attack` =
  "Great Sword Hilt Melee") gone: right slash_2 -> horiz -> 360h; left slash_4 -> backhand -> 360l; up spin -> slash_1 -> combo3;
  down slash_3 -> down -> jump_attack. New, from the library's axe set (`Standing_Melee_Attack_*`, two-handed): right-hand peak
  speeds (m/s) horizontal 16.8, 360 high 14.7, backhand 12.8, downward 12.4, 360 low 10.3 (the great-sword slashes 4.6-8.9); each
  clip's `at` is its measured peak. `Bash` measured slow (5.75) and is baked but unused, as are `katana_heavy` and `katana_runjump`.
  Headless, three flicks 150 ms apart: right/left/up each played all three in order.
- **THE CHARGE** holds the guard pose (the derived frames are gone); the release is the LEAP and swing (`katana_jump_attack`, his
  "Marth"), full charge the 360 high spin. His side-on two-handed charge pose is his to make.

## m989 -- THE SKULLBACK ON HIS BACK WAS 10 FEET UP ON HIS TAIL (`tailLie`, `TAIL.lie`)
*"Whichever of the bosses that has the tail -- when you fuck him up and he goes on his back he's like 10 feet in the air because
of his tail... either he goes belly down or the tail curls or something."*
The Skullback (`rept_heavy_armor`, 6 `c_tail_*` bones). Two causes, both measured:
- **His own `fall_to_back` is baked propped on the tail**: at the end, hips .533 authored (the Warboss lying flat: .167; his own
  `fall_to_face_down`: .139), tail root .45 down to tip .13. In game, KO'd from the front: hips **2.0 m** off the floor, and the
  clip throws them to **2.8 m** mid-fall.
- **`tailSway` resets the tail to its rest every frame**, and his rest tail comes straight out of his spine -- into the floor
  when he is on his back. (It also skipped KO'd bodies past the fall, so the tail froze in whatever pose it had.)
Fix, on a switch (TOOLS > TAIL, remembered): **FLAT** (default) -- over on his back (`down` / `up` with `d.back`), the tail's
root aims along the floor toward his feet in proportion to how flat his spine is, the sway fades out, and the hips are held
under a ceiling that eases from `standH` .55 to `lieH` .19 of his height as he tips over (one writer: `model.position.y`, only
in that state). **BELLY** -- a tailed body always falls face down. **OFF** -- as it was.
Evidence (headless, KO'd by a shot in the face, side camera): OFF hips 2.0 m lying, 2.8 m peak; FLAT hips 1.5 m mid-fall, then
0.24 m lying, the tail laid out along the floor (screenshot). Face-down falls are untouched (the tail points up, fine).
Not built: a real curl; the get-up from his back reads the same rule (eases out as he sits up) but was not filmed.

## m988 -- EVERY OFF-CENTRE CHARACTER CENTRED: Zap 2 (+lib), Clancy, the rollerskater, the hipster (`tools/hipshift.mjs`)
*"Fix the tailed Zap too, any character that's not centred properly... anybody that's not centred definitely needs to be centred."*
Measured AS DRAWN (three.js, the character's own idle, hips vs the origin the game turns him on), before -> after:
    zap_02 / zap_02_lib     hips z .171 / .184 -> -.014 / -.001   (the tail had dragged the shell's centre back; proxy_zap2 moved too)
    clancy (+ktx2)          .119 -> .000
    alien_rollerskate_blue  .117 -> .000
    fat_hipster (+ktx2)     .055 -> .000
Body size identical before and after in every one (the skin moved with the hips; nothing stretched).
- **`hipshift` went general**: the vertices move by d expressed in the SKIN'S BIND SPACE, e = (Hips world x Hips IBM)^-1 d, and
  the inverse binds by T(-e); the Hips (rest local + every key) by the parent's inverse. **The first general pass used the
  mesh's world matrix for that space and blew the female, Clancy and the rollerskater up to 15-44 m** (caught by the drawn
  check, restored from backup, redone). For a plain rig the two agree, which is why the samurai and Zap 2 were fine.
- **`hipfix` read the BIND, and the bind lies**: it flagged the purple female at 48% -- her bind is off but every one of her
  clips puts her hips over the origin (as drawn: z -.001). It reads the node chain + the first clip's Hips key now. She is
  untouched. `forged/rept_heavy_armor` (83%) and `forged/zap` (17%) were the same kind of false alarm: played on their real
  bodies the forged clips sit within .1 m (charges travel). Untouched.
- **`proxy_zap2.bin`** (the MORPH proxy: raw positions bound with Zap 2's own binds) moved by the same -.1847, or the morph
  blob would have stood behind him. `clipXfer` (the Clancy stretch borrowed for the morph) is relative to rest: unaffected.
- Not run: the x-ray on Clancy/Zap 2 (it reads the binds, which agree with the drawn body now).

## m978 -- SWORD build a: THE KATANA, four directional swings (`KATANA`, `katanaScene`, the KATANA slot)
*"Yeah, start build a with the katana."* (SWORD.md: the four directional attacks first.)
- **The katana** is built in code (`katanaScene`) to the weapon-bone convention READ OFF THE HAMMER'S FILE: root in the fist, tip
  marker (-14.31, 0, 0), the weapon along +Y (the hammer runs -20 -> +42 there). A 0.29 m wrapped grip, iron guard, gold collar, a
  0.77 m curved steel blade; mounts at 1.08 m. A GLB of his replaces it as `file:` with no other change (`gen:` is the hook).
- **The slot:** KATANA on the weapon wheel (`melee: 'katana'`, `blade: true` = weapon damage). The loader and the swap clip
  learned that a `gen:` slot is armed, not empty.
- **Direction picks the swing** (Smash-style): the right flick's SCREEN direction -> `KATANA.dirs`, each its own short chain:
  right `katana_slash_2`, `_1` (rising, left to right); left `_4`, `_3` (right to left); up `katana_attack` (the thrust); down
  `katana_spin` (the overhead). MEASURED, not guessed: the right hand's path through each clip's fastest stretch on the samurai's
  rig (slash_2 -0.43 -> +0.28 m; slash_4 +0.2 -> -0.56 m; attack -0.16 -> +0.31 m forward; spin 0.88 m -> the floor), and each

## m973 -- BOSSES COME THROUGH THE DOORS, AND THEY RUN HEAVY (`arenaEnter`, `ARENA.door`, `ARENA.heavy`, three new Forge bakes)
*"Those big doors... opening to reveal monsters and beasts... they walk through the doors, beat their chest, then come at you."*
*"The charge is dinky... a walk sped up, it makes them look light... we need a better run, like an ogre... make bigger characters
feel heavy and clunky."*
- **THE DOORS:** each portal gets a light-grey blast door (10 m) that RISES into the panel above it, and a dark tunnel behind, lit red
  from the back (gradient: bright at the floor, black at the top), so a boss is a silhouette first. A boss spawns in the tunnel of the
  free portal nearest where the camera looks (`arenaDoorPick`), the door rises (`openT` 1.8, a thud and a shake), he walks out with
  `enter_walk`, stops at r 27.5 and plays his chest-thump taunt, then LEAPS onto the dais with `enter_leap` (Mutant Jump Attack,
  trimmed .3-2.9 s; airborne .3-1.33 s of it) -- the game moves him horizontally across that window, the clip carries the height.
  Landing: shake, thud + clang, dust, hitstop, a knock-back if you stand within 4 m. `dummyBlow` ignores him while `d.entering`
  (a blow outside the ring would strand him: the ring's colliders keep bodies out too). TOOLS > ENTRY DOORS / BEAM.
- **THE HEAVY RUN:** the rush plays `charge_mutant` (Mutant Run) by default; TOOLS > CHARGE cycles MUTANT / ZOMBIE (Zombie Running)
  / SWORD (Great Sword Run) / OLD (the warrior's run sped up to 2.6x, which was the "dinky" one). Pace is the CLIP's: speed =
  its measured stride x a time-scale capped at `tsMax` 1.5 (Mutant Run measures **2.30 m/s** on the Warboss, so the rush is ~3.5
  m/s, not the old 5-7 -- slower and heavier; `rushV` is now only an upper bound). Every footfall is a stomp (`arenaStomp`: thud,
  dust, a shake that fades out by 22 m).
- **THE SPEEDS ARE FOOT-MEASURED, NOT ROOT MOTION.** The Forge's `forge_ref_*` came back ~4e-5 for these: the library clips are
  authored in place, there is no root travel to read. `arenaRef` measures the planted foot on the live body (gaitMeasure's method),
  once per kind and clip. It read 0 at first because a skin's actions are not all PLAYING the way the hero's are -- the measure
  now plays the clip for the sample and stops it after. enter_walk measures 1.45 m/s.
- **Forge profiles** (private repo, retarget-anims/library/profiles): `brute_warboss_armor`, `ceo_alien`, `rept_heavy_armor`, 5
  clips each; bakes in models/characters/forged/ (0.16-0.38 MB each), merged into the kinds by `forgedMerge` at `bodyProto`.
- Checked: `npm run check` ok; headless: the whole sequence runs (door 0->1, walk -36.5 -> -27.5, taunt, leap to -9, door closes),
  rush runs on charge_mutant. Open: whether it FEELS heavy is his; the door/tunnel size and the walk length are dials.

## m965 -- THE FIRST SECONDS ARE CHOPPY: the warm-up moved behind the card (bakes, shapes, every shader, every texture)

*"When I boot Weirdport, the first 5 or 10 seconds it's choppy and laggy... once you're in game it's like warming up, then it goes
away, but it's consistent."* MEASURED headless in the kit city (renderer.info + requests + logs, from `rig.ready` on): the files are
all in by then, but (1) three.js compiles a shader / uploads a texture the first time something is DRAWN with it -- 132 textures at
ready, and the fog + small-things culls hide 446 objects that `renderer.compile` (it walks only what is visible) never saw, so they
compiled as they came into view; (2) the Forge bakes (m933, "off the boot path") and the DNA shapes (0.8 MB, processed 1.4 s in)
arrived after the card -- their decode landed in the first seconds of play. New in this repo, which is why Weirdport never did it.
Now, last thing before `rig.ready`: wait for `FORGED.ready` + the shapes (capped `BOOTWARM.wait` 8 s), then `bootWarm` -- every
hidden object shown for the compile and hidden again, `renderer.compile`, `renderer.initTexture` on every texture a material holds.
Headless after: "boot warm: 78 programs, 90 textures uploaded, 446 hidden shown", NO request and NO log after the card. The card
stays up correspondingly longer (2.3 s of it under software rendering; a phone GPU is far quicker). `BOOTWARM.on = 0` is the A/B.
Not measurable here: whether that was all of what he feels on the phone (no GPU in this container). Shipped unverified.

## m960 -- THE DUPLICATE SEAM FRAME at the end of the run: dropped by the Forge for every clip (`loopSeam`)

*"Check if there's a duplicate at the end of the run sequence, where the last frame is the same as the first."* There was. Per
rotation track, first key vs last: `run_std` 0.02 deg, `sprint_std` 0.03 (against 18.6 / 18.0 for the frame before last) -- a Mixamo
loop ends on its first pose again, so a looping clip holds it for two frames each cycle. The CEO's library walk / run were not
(4.4 / 5.2 deg after his layers). `editLayer` now ends with `loopSeam`: when EVERY rotation's last key is within `SEAM.deg` (.5)
of its first, the last key goes and the clip is one frame shorter (a one-shot that ends where it began loses 1/30 s). After:
`run_std` 23 keys to 0.733 s (the source: 23 frames, 0.7333), `sprint_std` 17 to 0.533; seams now one ordinary step apart.
The BODY decides (finger tracks carry the hand layer's noise, which is not periodic -- Zoar's first bake kept the seam because of

## m958 -- THE WEAPON DRIVES THE HANDS (Forge `weapLayer`): position-driven arms on every weapon clip, Zoar holds guns as Zap does

*"I thought when transferring animations from one rig to another... the hand would be the determining position... I want to do it

the pose, POSITION + IK wherever a hand touches something. For a weapon clip that is the weapon:

  shoulder-width ratio across, x spine-length ratio up / forward);

- his left hand where the donor's is ON the weapon (in the weapon's frame, x the weapon's size ratio = hand-length ratio, m794),
  weighted off when the donor's left hand is `WEAPIK.near/far` (2.5 / 4 hand lengths) from it -- it lets go when Zap's does.

## m948 -- HIS HAND OPENS ROUND THE CUP (a Forge WRAP, solved on his own fingers), and the cup doubles as he picks it up

*"You could see his fingers through the cup... the placement of the cup in the hand, his fingers intersect it. We need to open his
fist quite a bit bigger so that it physically goes around the cup. Also make the cup double its size when he picks it up."*
m947 read "shows through his fingers" as a see-through cup. It was the fingers: his hand was the captured `cup` pose -- nearly a
fist -- and nothing related that pose to the size of what was in it.
- **`wrapPose` (forge/core.js), a computed hand pose `wrap`.** A cylinder of radius `r` HAND LENGTHS (wrist -> middle knuckle),
  axis = the socket's +Z, seated on the palm side: palm normal = the socket's X, its sign from the middle knuckle's own curl axis
  x the finger (a fingertip's open->fist movement was tried first and is dominated by the tip pulling back toward the wrist --
  it put the cup BEHIND the hand, then on its BACK); near surface `WRAP.palm` (.14) off the palm, centre level with the knuckles
  less `WRAP.back` (.15). Then every finger, knuckle outward: each joint curls about its rest->fist axis until its own segment
  touches the cylinder skin (+ `WRAP.fr` .1 for the finger's half-thickness), capped at the fist. Seen in a headless Forge render:
  the fingers lie on the cylinder.
- **The bake carries where it sits**: a `hold_hand_r` node (hand-local centre, `extras.r`). The game reads it (`FORGED.holds`)
  and `drinkHand` puts the cup THERE at THAT radius -- the hand and the cup are measured against each other, nothing typed twice.
- **Double**: his hand is 0.136 m in game, so the floor cup x2 (radius .036 x 1.05 x 2 = .076 m) is `r` .555. The cup GROWS from
  its floor size to that over `DRINK.growT` (.3 s) as it lands in his hand (`drinkGrow`). No bake -> `DRINK.heldK` (2) at the socket.
- **The straw reaches his mouth, not the socket**: `set_wrap tip` 4.43 radii up the axis (the cup's straw top), and the reach layer
  lands that point (`R.p`). `drinkPour` now pours from the straw's TOP (it was the lid).
- Profile: `wrap {r .555, tip 4.43}`, pick_up + drink right hand `wrap`. MCP `set_wrap`; app verb `setWrap`; `wrap` in the hand list.
Shipped unverified on the phone.

## m936 -- HAND POSES: clean hands from the library over the donor's fingers, per side, per clip, with finger noise
*"my donor character came standard with fucked up fingers and it's just transferred to every other character... you only need a
handful of hand poses -- neutral, fist for holding, flat for running, a cup, a point -- choose the hand positions per animation,
override... maybe some noise, so an idle hand has a little finger motion"*.
- **The poses come from the library, chosen by MEASUREMENT** (`forge/hands.json`): 925 candidate clips (idle / punch / point /
  rifle / drink / run ...) sampled at 6 fps, 12,491 frames, each hand's per-finger curl (summed joint angles) and spread
  (index vs pinky). Picked per side: relaxed (Happy Idle / Situp To Idle, curls ~80 each, spread ~20), fist (Boxing / Jab To
  Elbow Punch, ~320), grip (Rifle Put Away / Rifle Rubbing Eyes, ~245), cup (~112, fingers together), flat (~10, spread 0),
  open (curl < 30, spread >= 40), point (Pointing: index 27, the rest ~300).
- **`handsLayer` (core)**: each pose is CARRIED onto this body like any clip (`poseCapture` = `retargetW` of that frame, the
  finger bones' local rotations read off), so it is hand-relative and lands on any rig. Per side: slerp from the clip's fingers
  to the pose by `amt`. **Noise**: each finger curls in and out about its own rest->fist axis, two sines on its own phase,
  degrees + Hz. Order: carry -> sliders -> HANDS -> FK -> grip -> ground -> trim/speed, so a bone key can still move a finger.
- **Forge**: BODY "His hands" (right, left, amount, noise, speed) is his default for every clip; PACK "This clip" can choose its
  own per side ("his default" / "as the source" / a pose). In his profile, so it bakes into the game with everything else.
- MCP: `set_hands`.
- Tested headless: old Zap's idle_01 on the hick, right hand close up in all eight states (source + seven poses) -- seven visibly
  different hands, ~0.7 s each to carry; no page errors.

## m935 -- SOCKETS: `socket_hand_r` / `socket_hand_l`, where a hand holds a thing -- in the Forge AND the game
*"Mixamo doesn't add a weapon joint... make it so we have the ability to add the weapon joints and adjust them... maybe they're
hand item position joints -- a soda, a gun, a pole, a cat"*. The standard: Unreal calls them sockets (hand_r -> weapon_r), Unity
a hand attach, Godot a BoneAttachment3D -- one idea, a named point on the hand with a position and an orientation.
- **The convention** (`SOCKET_BASIS`, `socketAuto` in the game; lifted verbatim into forge/core.js by forgesync, now with consts):
  origin in the grip (old Zap's weapon point, `ZAP_MOUNT.o`), **+Z along the handle out of the thumb side, +Y the way the fingers
  point**, +X = Y x Z. Placed from the hand's own frame (`handFrame`: hand->Middle1 and the Pinky1->Index1 knuckle line), so any
  rig with fingers gets both, however its bones are oriented. A rig that already carries a socket keeps it.
- **Forge**: sockets made on load (after the rest snapshot), drawn as axis triads in POSE; Move / Turn / Reset socket. An
  adjusted one is saved in the profile and marked `forged` (exported as glTF extras). Props now mount by what they are built
  around: a `socket` node -> his socket, identity; a `weapon_root*` -> his own joint of that name (identity, old Zap) else where
  old Zap held it in a hand like his (`mountPlace`), sized by hand length (old Zap's hand is 7.55 cm in his file) and moved by his
  socket's adjustment; nothing -> his socket at the file's units (the cleaver and the maul are bare meshes: fit by hand).
- **Game** (`forgedSocket` in `mphMounts`, `FORGED.sockets` from a bake's `forged` sockets): a disguise's weapon mount on that
  hand moves by the same hand-local delta (user x auto^-1).
- **Fixed on the way**: the rest snapshot captured the Forge's own nodes, so `restore` (every export) put an adjusted socket back
  to auto. The snapshot now skips anything the Forge hangs on him (`forgeMade` / `forge_*`).
- Tested headless: the launcher on old Zap (his own weapon_root_right), the hick and the fat biker (old Zap's grip from their own
  hands) -- the same grip on all three by eye. A hick profile with the right socket moved 3 cm and turned 30 deg -> baked -> the
  game read the socket back exactly and the weapon mount moved with it. Test bake removed. MCP: `set_socket`.

*"when he holds the rocket launcher, the gun is cutting through his body. His hands aren't even in the right positions"*.
- **Prop in his hand** (POSE): the eight Zap weapons, or upload a GLB (kept in the browser). A prop built around a
  `weapon_root*` joint hangs from his `weapon_root_right/_left` with IDENTITY -- the game's own rule -- else from the bare hand.

  the carrying hand, FK keys and all -- and re-solves the other arm onto it (two bones, elbow in its plane, the hand following its
  forearm). Order: carry -> sliders -> FK -> GRIP -> ground -> trim/speed.

  gripping arm into the clip; the prop itself is not exported (the game mounts its own).

## m930 -- THE FORGE, step 3: the FK layer -- POSE tab, rotate a bone with rings, keyed at the playhead, eased between keys
*"clearly this rotation-based application, his arm is not over his shoulder. So you use the FK layer to pull his arm up"*.
- **POSE tab**: dots on his joints (fingers 2-4 and end bones left out so a thumb can hit them); tap one or pick from the list;
  TransformControls rings, bone's axes or world axes. Letting go KEYS it at the playhead. One key holds for the whole clip, a
  second key at another time eases between them (smoothstep + slerp). Keys list: tap to jump there, ✕ to drop; clear a bone or all.
- **`fkLayer` (core)**: a key is a rotation in the bone's PARENT frame added on top of the clip (`L' = D * L`), so a lift stays a
  lift whatever the shoulder is doing. Order: carry -> his sliders -> FK -> ground contact -> trim/speed. Keys are stored in the
  clip's SOURCE time, so re-trimming does not slide them. The new key is the difference from what the clip gave the bone with the
  old key undone, so re-grabbing a keyed bone edits that key rather than stacking.
- **Fixed: `skeleton.pose()` collapses a rig whose armature carries a scale** (it treats a root bone's world matrix as its local
  one) -- loading a profile shrank the fat biker to a point at the origin, and m928/m929's export wrote that wrong rest for the
  cast's 0.01 armatures (the clips themselves were right). Every node's rest is snapshotted at load (`tg.restore`).
- The source body's stick lines were scaled twice (the helper was parented under the scaled ghost): in the scene now, and only
  for a bare skeleton -- a donor with a skin shows its skin.
- Tested headless (phone size): old Zap's rocket_launcher on the fat biker, Left Arm turned 46 deg -> keyed, hand moved 14 cm, the
  key listed, no page errors.

## m928 -- THE FORGE, step 1: `forge.html` -- a body, the motion library, his pack, his PROFILE, export (app + command line)
*"upload the character... tick little boxes of which animations you're adding to his pack... preview live... adjust... export"*.
Design: `retarget-anims/DESIGN.md`. The idea it hangs on: a per-character PROFILE (pack + layers + later his FK keys), so a fix
is made once and re-applies to every clip and every re-bake, instead of being baked into one GLB and lost on the next body.
- **`forge.html` + `forge/app.js`** (desktop and phone): BODY (pick one of the cast or load a GLB/FBX; the measured hip height;
  which bones never count), LIBRARY (2,288 motions: search + tag chips; a shared name is told apart by Mixamo's description
  and length on the row; tap = preview on him, + = into the pack), PACK (role names the game asks for, editable), EXPORT
  (clips-only GLB for me to merge, or character + clips). The library body plays beside him as a stick figure.
- **`forge/core.js`**: `bindPose` and `retargetW` are the GAME's text, lifted verbatim (`tools/forgesync.mjs`, now part of
  `npm run check` -- it fails if the two drift). New: `rigOf` (one spelling for every Mixamo rig: `mixamorig:`, `mixamorigHips`,
  `mixamorig1:`), `skinInfo` (each sampled vertex's strongest bone; a non-Mixamo bone -- his TAIL, a marker -- never counts as
  his body), and **LAYER 3, GROUND CONTACT**: per frame, his lowest skin point is put where the library body's lowest joint is
  above its own rest low point, scaled by hip height. Keeps a jump a jump (the library body is off the ground too).
- **`tools/forge.cjs`** (`npm run forge`): the same page headless -- `node tools/forge.cjs <char.glb> <profile.json> <out.glb>
  --lib <folder>`. Zap 2 + 3 clips: 0.21 MB in seconds.

  4 cm, Falling Back Death 23 cm (mean 13). **Seen, not fixed: lying on his back the TAIL goes through the floor** -- it holds its
  rest angle out of his back. A tail layer (bend away from the floor) is the next thing for the "lands on his back" report.
- Bug found and fixed on the way: the clip already on screen blended into the ground measurement (`stopAllAction` first).
- Vendored three r180 addons: OrbitControls, TransformControls (for step 3's FK gizmo), GLTFExporter, FBXLoader (+ fflate,
  NURBSCurve, NURBSUtils).
- **The library is not online yet**: LIBRARY connects to a GitHub repo with a token kept in the browser (meant for the private

## m920 -- he eases into the stretch instead of snapping to its first frame
`act.ease` .4 s: `tmActOn` keeps the clips he is in (frozen, weights normalised to 1) and `tmActEase` hands them over to the stretch
every morph frame (stretch e, the rest w(1-e), smoothstepped). **First try flashed toward the T-POSE at t .1**: `skinWeights` runs
on an arena body every frame from `stepDummies`, and its rule for a clip whose target weight is 0 is `setEffectiveWeight(0);
a.stop()` -- so the held clips were STOPPED under the crossfade and only 16% of the stretch was holding the bones. While a morph is
driving his weights (`st 'morph'` + `actPrev`) it is skipped. Strip at t 0 .1 .2 .3 .4: walk -> hunch, no flash, no snap.

## m919 -- the CEO stretches through his morph (Clancy's `idle_02_stretch`, carried onto both bodies)
*"There's an idle in the mutant pack -- he stretches with both arms out -- the perfect animation to play during the transform,
it looks like the werewolf stretch."* Found by clip name across every GLB: `idle_02_stretch` (3.04 s) is in CLANCY's file with the
rest of the mutant pack (`mutant_flexing_muscles`, `mutant_roaring`...); the bosses were baked from the warrior donor and never had it.
- `clipXfer(S, clip, K)`: WORLD-DELTA retarget, sampled at 30 fps -- per target bone Wt(t) = Ws(t) Ws0^-1 Wt0, made local down the
  TARGET's own chain; hips travel x (target hip height / source hip height). Bones the source lacks (fingers, `root`) keep their
  rest. Clancy (27 joints, no fingers) -> the CEO and the CEO alien (53 / 59). Cached per kind (`K.tmAct`). This is the narrow
  first cut of the motion transfer tool (ROADMAP ASSETS) -- `retarget`'s raw local copy would not survive his re-oriented bones.
- Both bodies on it at `from`, frozen; each frame the morph sets both actions' time, `mixer.update(0)`, and RE-SKINS both proxies
  from the live skeletons (`tmSkin`: premultiplied bone matrices, a flat loop -- 4.0 ms/frame for both on headless swiftshader);
  normals every `nEvery` 3 frames. The morph runs the clip's length / `speed` 1.15 = 2.64 s. `ARENA.morph.act.on = 0` is the A/B.
- Strip (LIMBS): hunched, arms rising, flung wide overhead, the limbs turning in order. Known: a pop from his walk into the
  stretch's first frame at the start.
- `tmStep(dt, force)` + `ARENA.morph.hold`: step a morph by hand (headless strips).

## m918 -- the wave's SHAPE: LIMBS (directed) and NOISE; m917 had swallowed `ARENA.morph.simple`
*"A spherical falloff with a growing noise pattern, so parts of his body grow at different rates -- or a vertex map, really
directed: one arm, then the opposite leg, then the other arm, the other leg, then the middle."*
- `tmDelay(src, wave)` builds a per-vertex DELAY map (`aDly`) once per morph from the proxy itself -- its REST positions and its
  dominant joint -- so it will not shift as his limbs move. LIMBS: regions by joint name (`waves.LIMBS.order` LA, RL, RA, LL, T),
  each turning from its TIP inward (hand / foot), the trunk from the chest out. NOISE: a sphere out of his chest (.55) plus two
  octaves of value noise (`f` 5.5 cells per height). Each wave has its own spread `s` and turn width `w` (LIMBS 1.5 / .38: one
  part after another; FEET .55 / .6: one sweep). Default LIMBS; the WAVE button cycles LIMBS, NOISE, FEET, CHEST.
  Strips of the CEO: LIMBS -- left arm, right leg, right arm, left leg, head last; NOISE -- patches.
- **m917 PUT A COMMENT MID-LINE AGAIN** and it swallowed `ARENA.morph.simple = ...` -- his own DNA turn threw and fell back to
  the blob for one build. Fourth time (m904, m909, m917). Split.
- NEXT (m919): his stretch (`idle_02_stretch`, Clancy's file, the mutant pack) retargeted onto both CEO bodies and played
  DURING the morph, the proxies re-posed every frame.

## m914 -- THE CEO MORPH: no T-pose, no 180 flip, no walking during it
*"When he transforms he goes ghost stiff, into T-pose, transforms into the other T-pose and goes back. Also he flips 180 -- he
transforms facing away and then all of a sudden he's facing me. There's also some walks going on."*
- THE FLIP AND THE WALKING: `tmGo`'s `b.st = 'morph'` sat at the END OF A `//` COMMENT (m909), so the new body never froze: a
  boss in `idle` with aggro, turning toward you and walking on the spot (pinned) behind the frozen proxies. The proxy was taken
  at the old heading; the real body appeared at the swap already facing you. Headless, CEO set to h 1.57: before, b.h drifted
  1.57 -> 1.41 -> 1.00 during the morph; after, 1.57 throughout. **Third mid-line-comment bug in this file (m904, m909).**

*"The shield... goes through their arm... needs to be out on the outer part. Every time I would shoot them they would have the

## m902 -- THE SHOCK: a spiky electric bubble, lightning arcs, cartoon zaps; he convulses; a skeleton per species

## m901 -- THE STUN ZAP: the x-ray skeleton as rigid pieces fitted to ANY rig (his method)
*"If we broke the skeleton into its bone segments... and aligned them rigidly to any Mixamo skeleton... it would work for
everybody."* `ARENA.stun`, `xrayFit`, `xrayMake`, `arenaStun`, `arenaStunStep`.
- FIT (once per KIND, cached `K.xrayGeo`): each skeleton triangle goes with its first vertex's dominant bone; each bone gets a
  frame on both rigs from the BIND joints (`boneInverses`): head -> next joint (`next` table) as the axis, +Z forward projected
  as the twist reference. Piece = victim head + victim frame x diag(stretch, g, g) x skeleton frame^T (minus skeleton head).
  `g` = torso (Hips -> Neck) ratio; stretch = joint-to-joint length ratio clamped to g x [.55, 1.9]; end bones (Head, Hands,
  ToeBase) take the parent axis and a uniform g. Every vertex 100% on the VICTIM's bone -> a SkinnedMesh bound to his own
  skeleton: one draw, no per-frame work. Hick: 22 pieces, 1 dropped (the skeleton's `root`), 34,350 verts. Warboss: the same.
- **RAW VERTEX SPACE, NOT bindMatrix**: the first cut went through the skeleton's `bindMatrix` and out through the victim's
  `bindMatrixInverse` -- right on the Warboss (both ARP: the two cancelled) and 100x too big and lying down on the hick (Mixamo,
  identity bindMatrix). glTF's inverse-bind matrices and the raw positions already share one space; nothing else is needed.
- THE ZAP: STUN on the arena bar -> a bolt that lands (and is not shield-blocked) stuns instead of hurting: `flash` 1.0 s
  strobing body / skeleton at `hz` 12, a jitter, arcs (`spkCling`), `zap` buzz; then dazed to `dur` 3.2 s (idle, twitches,
  sparks dripping). The first stun loads the skeleton (`xrayLoad`; turning STUN on preloads it). SPAWN > PEOPLE: Hick, Hobo.
- Headless: hick and Warboss both fitted and posed (screens). Open: the DNA CLAW, how it looks on his phone, and the finger
  bones (the skeleton has none: the hands are rigid).

Colin's screenshots at m884 show the hero and most NPCs as black silhouettes, with the blonde protester fine. ## m881 -- STEER: the main game dies on his phone at m875 (art window)

Colin's screenshot shows the FRAME error card at m875: `shaderSource@[native code]`, under three's `acquireProgram`, under `frameBody`'s `renderer.render`. In WebKit, shaderSource throws only on a null shader, which `createShader` returns when the context is lost, so this reads as iOS dropping the WebGL context for GPU memory on the first frame. The STEER at the top of ROADMAP asks for three things: survive a lost context (`CTXLOST` in the chip); put programs, geometries, textures and MB in the chip; and stop building or uploading far regions until he goes toward them. The art window's dressing loop is paused so it does not add to the load. No index.html change was made here.

## m856 -- T7m pod_deck.glb, and the drawn-box scan comes up empty (art window)

This pass re-checked buildIslandSkate, buildIslandXing, buildCarts and buildIslandBase. Almost every drawn-only box left in them is a fallback behind an existing campPlace (it is built only when the art is missing), or a flat paint splash, or an effect. The two real leftovers were the cart pod's deck and the skate pier's light poles, and both are now art. For the turn: a code box turned ps has its length along (cos ps, -sin ps) in (u, v), which is a turn of -ps about Blender Z. The second slab's boards sit 5 mm proud so the overlap does not z-fight. With this, the campaign detail pass has art for every place still drawn as code boxes. What remains is ribbons that follow terrain (roads, decks, flumes), canvas signs and effects. Shipped unverified.

## m853 -- T7l mill_shed.glb: Hollow Creek Lumber's shed (art window)

The mill's machines (m541) and its floor (m693) were art already; the shed they stand in was still tin boxes with m499's ribs stuck on. It is now one shell at 1,726 faces and one loft at 786. While building it I found that the code's right wall has a .5 m full-height gap at v -10.5..-10. Its long segment is centred at S.v + 2.5 with length S.d - 5, so it ends at -10, while the slot ends at -10.5. The art closes the gap and the collider still has it; ROADMAP says so and leaves the fix to the game window. Shipped unverified.

## m850 -- T7k freight_bits.glb: the halts' platforms, legs, wildflowers, the log load (art window)

Most of buildFreight was already art: the trestle deck and bents (m709), the trestle kit (m587), the halt shelter and tank (m571), the extras (m706), the stairs (m728) and the train (m555). Its 28 drawn-only boxes were mostly fallbacks behind those. What was really left was the platform deck itself, its legs, the flowers, and the logs, which the code still builds even when `ft_flat` is art. The logs piece is in the car group's frame, where three +z is Blender -Y, so the load's centre (three z -2) is at Blender +Y 2. The platform's end fascias run up to the board tops: an earlier render with them stopping 5 cm short showed every board gap as a black slot. Shipped unverified.

## m847 -- T7j ready_room.glb: The Ready Room (art window)

A re-run of the drawn-box scan found buildReadyRoom with 18 drawn-only boxes, about 25 geos and no art placement at all. It is now six pieces. The two big ones are `rr_shell` (866 faces) and `rr_inside` (1,396). A fresh `rr_pickup` was built rather than reusing `rp_pickup`, because that one sits on cinder blocks and this one is driven to the bar. The battens are modelled per face, not repeated in a tile, so they never read as a pattern. Shipped unverified.

## m845 -- T7i highway_bits.glb: the road bridge's rails, lamps, piers (art window)

The gang's end of the bridge was already art: gang_road, the pickup, the barrel, the chairs, the bikes, the trackside litter and the broken-down car. The long run of the bridge was still a pearlSeg rail ribbon, box lamps and box piers. That run is now four small pieces (18-78 faces). The rail is a 3 m tile with half-posts at its ends, so neighbouring tiles share a post. The game pitches it to the arch per piece rather than bending it. The pier is a 1 m stretch piece, so its rustication strip stretches with it; that is fine for a vertical strip. The deck ribbon, the shoulders and the centre line stay code, because they follow the arch. Shipped unverified.

## m842 -- T7h tower_shell.glb: Dump Tower's curtain wall, stairs and vestibules (art window)

The floors' furniture (m623), the roof and the lift (m624) were already art. What was left was the shell, drawn as gold sticks: about 36 mullions and 4 bands a floor over ten floors, plus the stairs and the two vestibules. The new pieces are small tiles meant to be instanced. They come in at 12-30 faces each, except the flight at 246, the screen at 138 and the vestibule at 108. The glass is deliberately left in code, because it is the collider and the transparent material. The flight is built rising +Y from (L.u, L.v0), so lane B is turned pi. The screen is symmetric, so it needs no turn. Shipped unverified.

## m839 -- T7g town_trailer.glb: the town edge's trailers (art window)

The rest of buildTownEdge already had art: the houses, pickets, mailboxes and stand (m661), the gas station (m659), and the billboards and poles (m663). The trailer park was the one block still drawn as boxes. `tv_trailer` is 1,796 faces, at the code's 12 x 3.4 body on its .55 footing, with the deck at (2, 2.6). `tv_chair` is 120 faces. The `tw_` prefix was already taken by the walks, so these pieces are `tv_`. The turn is the one open question: the code's length axis is (cos r, -sin r) in (u, v), and campPlace mirrors z, so ROADMAP says to flip the sign if the deck lands on the wrong side. Shipped unverified.

## m837 -- T7f farm_bits.glb: tractor, cupola, hay hood (art window)

The farm's last pieces still drawn as code boxes are now art, at the code's own numbers. The tractor is 642 faces, the cupola 129 and the hood 126. The vane stays code because it turns, and the tractor's collider stays code. The prefix `fp_` is shared with farm_props.glb; the names were checked and none clash. Shipped unverified.

## m834 -- ranch.glb: Shadowhide Ranch (T7e)

The ranch (m822) had no art at all. These five pieces cover every drawn structure in it. The corral keeps the code's gap: post k 3 is skipped, which drops the rails k 2..4, so the opening faces the house exactly as the code's does. Shipped unverified.

## m832 -- tower_secret.glb: the Dozen's room and the aerial tram (T7d)

The re-scan for drawn-only boxes put Dump Tower first (41), most of them in the newest rooms. The Dozen's room (m783) is the code's ring of twelve, eleven red and one black at k 0. The tram's cabin is built in its group's frame so the shuttle carries it. The chairs' bevels went from 2,680 faces to 760. Shipped unverified.

## m829 -- skate_pier.glb: the skate pier's deck, piles and rails (T7c)

The pier under the park as tiles at the code's pitches: deck seams every 1.2, rail posts every 2, piles every 4.5. With T7b the pier skate park is all art apart from its string lights and paint splashes, which are code on purpose. The island thermal checked this pass is all effects (shimmer, cloud, gulls) and is skipped. Shipped unverified.

## m827 -- skate_park.glb: the pier skate park's obstacles (T7b)

The park's hangout and graffiti wall were already his. The obstacles were still slabs under walk quads. The quarter pipe follows the code's own curve, 4 m to 55 degrees, and the kicker and funbox banks match their `strip()` points, so the art sits on the surface the board actually rides. Shipped unverified.

## m824 -- ship_hall.glb: the mothership's belly hall and pod (T7a)

The hall was a BackSide open cylinder, two tori, a circle and a sphere around his eggs and glyphs (`ship_belly`). It is now one piece at the code's R 12.5 / H 6.5 / glassR 7.5, with the doorway gap at +X where nW leaves it. The pod rides the tether, so it is built in its group's frame like the diner saucer. Shipped unverified.

## m822 -- foot_dress.glb: the footbridge's foot on the beach (T6z)

m490 made the foot a place: a flagstone path, a works hut, a CLOSED board, a lifebuoy, a tideline and a bench. Each now has a piece at the code's spot and yaw. The board's face is one white material, so the code's red-while-closed / white-once-fixed switch becomes a tint, as with every other `_paint` piece. Shipped unverified.

## m820 -- footbridge.glb: the footbridge's span (T6y)

The footbridge's dock end was already dressed (pearl_dock, the bollards), but its span was still chords, posts and rotated BoxGeometry diagonals. The art is the code's own 2 m panel as a tile, both trusses and the deck together. Each `deck()` run gets n = round(L / 2) of them, which is exactly the code's panel count, so the posts land where the code's do. Shipped unverified.

## m816 -- shore_steps.glb: the cliff ladder pads and the ferry stair's treads (T6x)

A fresh scan of the builders shows the campaign is now mostly art. Of what is left: `buildSite` and `buildFarm` are his kits already (the count is high because their boxes stay as colliders), `buildBridge` is the m291 river and is skipped whenever the channel bridge is live, and `buildNeighbours` was checked before. This pass takes two small pieces that were still plain boxes. Shipped unverified.

## m814 -- gap_ramp.glb: the island gap ramp (T6w)

The in-run, the kicker arc and the landing are all point lists the code fits so a board clears the ground (m484). The art is one segment, given each pair's length and pitch, so the curve stays the code's and the walk quads stay the surface. The landing reuses the segment, widened. The site builder (`buildSite`) turned out to be his `site_kit` already, so it was skipped. Shipped unverified.

## m813 -- swing_span.glb: the swing bridge's moving span (T6v)

It is built in the group's own frame and parented under `O.grp`, so the existing swing turns it with no new code. The truss is the code's: nine verticals each side at k * half / 4, rising 3.2 + 2.6 (1 - |k| / 4) to the middle. Pairs with T6u's fixed parts. Shipped unverified.

## m811 -- swing_bridge.glb: the swing bridge's fixed parts (T6u)

The moving span is a group the code turns, and its barriers and warning lights animate, so they stay code. Everything that stands still is art: the two fixed spans as 1 m tiles, the piers and the pivot drum stretched to the river bed, the lamps and the red gate posts. Shipped unverified.

## m808 -- ferry_landing.glb: the ferry's landing stage (T6t)

The jetty runs to wherever the island's ground meets the water (`vEnd` is computed), so it is a tile. The piles reach the seabed, so they are stretched. The pontoon's float drums first showed through its deck: their tops were above deck level, so they now sit below it. Shipped unverified.

## m806 -- wf_barge.glb: the barge under crane 1 (T6s)

The cranes are already his. The barge they work over was the last piece of `wfCranes` still drawn as boxes. Same lesson as the crates: the deck plate first rendered black because it shared the hull's top face, and lifting it 2 cm fixed it. Shipped unverified.

## m802 -- island_exit.glb: the BASE-jump exit point (T6r)

The deck is the code's IBASE numbers: 3 wide and 9 long, 5 m of it over the edge. That puts the edge (dE) at local Y -.5 from the deck's centre, and the braces run from under the end down 4.35 m to land just behind it, as `pearlSeg` does. The way-on steps fit the ground, so they are one step piece placed per step. Shipped unverified.

## m798 -- metro_core.glb: the metro core's tower kit (T6q)

The metro core's towers are rolled at load: size, height and one of four palette materials. A fixed tower model would fit none of them. What every tower shares is a lobby, a roof tank, sometimes a roof unit, and the sky-bridges between them, so that is the art. The window bands stay code because each tower's band material is its own (m700: the grip dims one). Shipped unverified.

## m795 -- under_safe.glb: the crossways ladders and the safe house (T6p)

The last of the Underneath. The safe house is meant to be warm light at last after the tunnels (m524), so it is the one room in the kit with soft furnishings and crockery. The laid table's bowls sit at the code's own .7 + k * .55, staggered +-.25. Shipped unverified.

## m792 -- under_market.glb: the pump room, the hidden market, the camp (T6o)

The pump wheel sits at the code's own `U.pump.wheelAt` and is built static, ready to spin on X. The market's tarps are one white material, so the code's `tarp` / `tarp2` alternation carries over as a tint. With T6m to T6o, the Underneath's tunnels, cistern, dig, vault, pumps, market and camp all have art waiting. The crossways and safe house are left. Shipped unverified.

## m791 -- under_cistern.glb: the cistern's catwalks, the dig's cart and strongbox (T6n)

The catwalks are the code's 19.2 m span between the ledges, on legs down to the pit floor at y - 2.4. That is the depth the water drains to (m522), so the legs read as standing in the water when it is high and on dry stone when it is drained. Shipped unverified.

## m789 -- underneath.glb: the Underneath's tunnel tiles (T6m)

The tunnels are built by `run()` and `room()` at whatever length the plan asks, so this is a kit of one-metre tiles, not a map. The first preview baked a growth patch and a damp streak into every tile. Down a straight tunnel that read as a row of lit windows, a stripe per metre. Both came out: the growth is its own piece, to scatter. Anything in a tile repeats, so a tile should carry only what is really periodic (courses, joints, the pipe). Shipped unverified.

## m784 -- bunker_camp.glb: the rest of Merle's camp (T6l)

Six pieces at the code's spots. One thing caught on review: the mast's guys first ran to (cos a, -sin a). The code puts them at v = sin a * 3.5, and Blender +Y is +v, so it is +sin. Handedness again; check every angle written into a piece against the code's own u / v. Shipped unverified.

## m782 -- bunker.glb: Merle's bunker, container and inside (T6k)

The container's corrugation is the code's own rib pitch (.3), and the door leaves stand open at the code's +-.25 spots. Inside, the string wall is a fresh scatter of the same 16 clippings and 14 strings. It is NOT the code's `pins` positions: the code uses its own LCG and this uses Python's random, so the cork board's layout differs. The dirt mounds belong to the hill and stay code. Shipped unverified.

## m781 -- diner_saucer.glb: the replica saucer and its yard (T6j)

The saucer moves (m761: it can leave the yard), so its art is built in the group's own frame to be parented under `O.saucer`, not placed in the world. Its dome and green light stay code because they are animated. The yard's fence gets the code's missing corner post, at the gap's far side. Shipped unverified.

## m777 -- diner_site.glb: the sign tower and the UFO museum (T6i)

The museum's clippings were first put at the code's own u (R - .45). At 2 m up, that is outside a quonset whose wall is only 2.75 m off centre there, so they poked through the shell. They now sit at R - .95. Worth checking in the code too: its paper boxes have the same problem. Shipped unverified.

## m776 -- diner.glb: Saucer Joe's, shell and inside (T6h)

The diner was 51 boxes and open cylinders. It is now one shell and one interior, both at the code's origin and numbers, so they drop in with no transform. The round ends are smooth arcs, not the code's four facets, and the facets stay as colliders. The roof's round-end discs shared a top face with the slab and rendered as black wedges, so the discs now sit 5 mm inside. The neon frame and canvas signs stay code because they glow. Shipped unverified.

## m772 -- hollis_props.glb: the last of Camp Hollis (T6g)

The firing positions are one 0.8 m bag segment that the code places seven times per horseshoe, already yawed. The rest are single props at the code's spots. With T6d through T6g, every drawn box in `buildMilBase` has art waiting. Shipped unverified.

## m769 -- hollis_yard.glb: Camp Hollis's trucks, net, mast and cage (T6f)

The camo net is a 15 x 15 grid that sags with distance from the nearest of the code's four poles, with a two-tone patch pattern. The mast's guys run from 12 m out to the code's 6 m radius at its three angles. The beacon sphere stays code because it blinks. The cage's chain-link is double-sided ribbons, as on the factory fence. Shipped unverified.

## m768 -- hollis_camp.glb: Camp Hollis's watchtower and tents (T6e)

The watchtower's parapet is laid in staggered sandbag courses with no bevels: bevels took it from 1,400 faces to 4,100. The parapet is open at +Y, where the code's two short runs leave the ladder gap. I first put the command tent's fly on the wrong side. The code's fly is at v -2.7, which is 4.3 m toward +Y from the tent's centre at -7, so it faces the gate. Shipped unverified.

## m767 -- hollis_wall.glb: Camp Hollis's HESCO ring (T6d)

Camp Hollis (m745) was the largest builder with no art: 57 boxes. This covers its wall. A basket is a mesh cage, a liner bulging between the uprights and fill showing on top, tiled at the code's own 1.1 m cage pitch. The wire is real concertina coils turned along the run, not tori. As with the parts crates, the first render had black tops where the fill shared a face with the basket. The rest of the base (watchtower, tents, motor pool, mast, cage) is the next pass. Shipped unverified.

## m764 -- factory_walks.glb: the factory's rails, legs and stair treads (T6c)

The code's `rail()` draws a top bar, a knee bar and a post every 2 m. The art is that as a 2 m tile, plus a last post. The west-wall stair's 33 solid `grate` blocks get open treads with yellow nosings; the blocks stay as colliders. The preview's stair first climbed the wrong way; the piece itself puts the nosing on +Y, matching the code, whose steps climb toward -v. Shipped unverified.

## m760 -- factory_line.glb: arm pedestals, the chrome booth, the lift shaft (T6b)

Three more of the factory line's stand-ins. The arms' pedestals get a bolted base and a turntable. The chrome booth gets mirror-chrome sides, a glowing ceiling and strip curtains at both ends. The lift's four bare posts become a braced shaft, tiled a metre at a time to 13 m, with its platform face left open. Shipped unverified.

## m759 -- parts_stock.glb: the factory's crates of arms (T6a)

There is one piece per height the code uses (1.1 / 1.5 / 1.9 by k % 3), with the 1.1 one in steel, because the code paints it `c7` grey metal. In the first preview the crate tops and corner posts rendered black: they shared faces exactly with the slats under them. Nudging each apart by a few millimetres fixed it. Watch for this on any slatted piece. Shipped unverified.

## m755 -- control_room.glb: the factory control room's consoles and lever (T5z)

The three consoles were dark boxes with a green slab on top. They now have a raked desk with the line drawn on it (one panel amber) and three monitors. The lever is a red-knobbed handle on a hazard-collared pedestal. Its knob sits where the code's sphere was, so `leverAt` and the prompt are unchanged. Shipped unverified.

## m754 -- factory_stations.glb: the factory line's arches, cage, hats and boots (T5y)

The two arches are 4.2 and 3.4 tall, so each one is split into stretched posts and a fixed head. Scaling one piece would have squashed the head beam with it. The hard hats taken off the line's workers were cylinders; they are now domes with brims, tinted the code's yellow / white. The boots were plank boxes. Shipped unverified.

## m751 -- shed_vents.glb: the transit shed's roof vents (T5x)

The shed itself is his `wf_shed`, but the three 2.2 m `steel` boxes on its roof are drawn outside that branch, so they stayed boxes. Each is now a louvred vent with a hipped cap and a turbine ventilator, at the box's own size. Shipped unverified.

## m749 -- factory_skin.glb: the factory's parapet and green screens (T5w)

The parapet was four `panel` slabs and the screens were three flat `screen` boxes. Both are now one-metre tiles. The screen's bright dashes come from a seeded random per tile, so a run of tiles reads as text crawling along the wall rather than one stripe repeated. It does still repeat every metre if you look for it. The first preview faced the wrong way (+Y is OUT). Shipped unverified.

## m746 -- factory_gallery.glb: the gallery over the fence (T5v)

The gallery was a grate, two tin slabs and a roof slab. It is now a one-metre bay, tiled: corrugated walls, a window ribbon lit faintly green like the factory's screens, and a portal frame every metre. It is tiled so the corrugation and mullions keep their pitch. The code's slabs stay the colliders. Shipped unverified.

## m744 -- shed_yard.glb: the transit shed's pallets and drums (T5u)

The existing pallet (`ce_pallet`) is leaned on its end and the existing drums (`pp_drums`) come as a pair, so neither fits the shed's one-pallet-per-.15 stacks or its five single drums. These are a flat pallet to stack and one drum with a tintable body, so the code's c1 / c5 colours carry over. The lid is painted with the body, not left dark. Shipped unverified.

## m741 -- factory_portal.glb: the factory's intake door (T5t)

The code striped the door with alternating yellow and black blocks. The art uses true 45-degree chevrons: each band is a parallelogram clipped to its jamb or lintel. The first version only kept bands that crossed the whole rectangle, which left the 0.5 m jambs plain yellow, so the clip is now Sutherland-Hodgman. The pieces it replaces were all drawing-only, so nothing about collision moves. Shipped unverified.

## m737 -- factory_roof.glb: the factory's roof units and stacks (T5s)

The four roof units were plain `steel` boxes and the stacks were two cylinders. Both now have art at the code's sizes. The stack keeps the code's taper (1.6 to 1.4) and its red band height (20..21), so it reads the same from across the river. Shipped unverified.

## m734 -- security_fence.glb: the factory lot's fence (T5r)

The fence round the factory lot is about 270 m, so its weave is a cost question first. The first build made the diamonds from boxes at 1,710 faces a metre: 460k for the lot. Flat double-sided ribbons in one mesh give 166 a metre, about 45k, and still read as chain-link. It is one metre TILED, not one copy stretched along a segment, because a stretched weave smears into zigzags. The outrigger leans outside, as real security fencing does. Shipped unverified.

## m730 -- gatehouse.glb: the factory gate's hut and boom (T5q)

This was a white box with a dark lid and a glass strip, and a red bar with four white stripe boxes laid on it. The art is the same hut at the same size: the window still faces the road (-v), plus a door, a lamp, a camera and a teal company band. The boom is striped in its own geometry, with a counterweight and a rest fork. The gate itself stays `GATES`' `uplift`. Shipped unverified.

## m727 -- outfeed_tower.glb: the outfeed tower's stair and platform (T5p)

In code the tower is 32 solid `grate` blocks rising from the quay, so it reads as a wedge, plus a slab on four sticks. The art opens it up: treads at the code's exact positions on two stringers and three bents, and a braced four-leg frame under the platform. The blocks stay the colliders. A stair you can see through is the point, because the turret on the platform (`wfTurrets`) is the climber's problem. Shipped unverified.

## m725 -- halt_stairs.glb: the halts' platform stairs and the yard fence (T5o)

The stair's step count depends on the ground (`gnd` per step, up to 40), so it can't be one baked flight. The art is one step and one leg pair per step: the step at the code's .28 / .45, the legs stretched down to each block's own foot. The fence is one bay at the code's spacing (a post every 3.6 m, rails .85 and .45). Shipped unverified.

## m722 -- dock_stair.glb: the stair down into the dry dock (T5n)

Sixteen `quay` blocks, a `steel` slab and two `yel` bars. The rise was not typed: Y - floor is 4.95, read back from the m683 stair tower (deck - Y = 6.25, deck = floor + 2.2 + 9), so each riser is .309. In the preview part of the landing renders black. That is the stand-in quay's top being coplanar with it, not the model. Shipped unverified.

## m718 -- caisson.glb: the dry dock's gate (T5m)

The caisson was one `steel` box, two `yel` bars with posts, and `iron` fender slabs. Now it has a dressed deck (seams, hatches, valve wheels, bollards), the rail as one 30 m piece at the code's own post spacing, fender piles, and a stiffened river face. The face and piles are stretched in height, so their rivets were taken out: a stretched sphere is an egg. Shipped unverified.

## m714 -- pearl_span.glb: the Pearl's roof links, steel and rope (T5l)

`pearlSpan` draws each link as n segments of `pearlSeg` slabs plus `bx` posts. The art is the same unit: one 1 m segment per piece, stretched along the span and pitched per segment, so the rope bridge's sag is the code's own `pt(t)` and nothing is baked in. Everything that stretches carries detail only along its length (tread ribs, ropes, rails); the posts carry the knots and caps and are never stretched. Shipped unverified.

## m712 -- pearl_ladder.glb: one generic ladder for every `pearlLadder` (T5k)

The 21 ladders were two `dark` rails and a stack of `dark` slabs. Now `pl_rail` (stretched in height, so it carries no detail that would smear), `pl_rung` (a round bar with welded ends and tread nicks -- instanced per rung, so the .32 pitch stays the code's), and `pl_cap` (the rails bending over to two wall plates). A rust band on the rail was taken out after the preview: on a stretched piece it smears to a metre. Shipped unverified.

## m710 -- the MX tape, the road litter and the patched potholes as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5j)

`models/campaign/trackside.glb`. For the MX track: the spectator tape's stake with its knot at the code's .9, and a 1 m length of
tape that sags and twists a little, one white material for the code's red and white. For Hollow Creek's highway bridge: a clump of
road litter (a crushed can, a green bottle, a coffee cup, a flattened box, a strip of tyre tread, scraps of paper) and a patched
pothole, an irregular dark patch with a lighter edge and cracks running off it, drawn flat. Shipped unverified.

## m707 -- the freight trestle's deck and bents as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5i)

`models/campaign/trestle_deck.glb`, for the trestle `buildFreight` carries over the strait. A 6 m deck section at the code's
numbers: two beams, eight ties (one in three creosote-dark) with tie plates, the two rails at the code's 1.5 m gauge with a head, web
and foot, and outer guard timbers; and a bent with its posts at the code's +-1.1, a cap, a sill and X-braces on both faces, 1 m tall
for the code to stretch to the ground or the seabed. Shipped unverified.

## m704 -- the halts' bench, churns and lamp posts as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5h)

`models/campaign/halt_extras.glb`, for the platforms `buildFreight` dresses at each end of the trestle. The bench under the shelter
at the code's .45 x 2.4: slatted seat and back on cast-iron ends, with the green timetable board and its four lines beside it; a pair
of steel milk churns with their bands and necks and two tied mail sacks; and the platform lamp post: a lantern under a hood, its
bracket and a hanging basket of flowers. Shipped unverified.

## m701 -- the fair field's poles and bunting as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5g)

`models/campaign/fair_field.glb`, for the field `buildFairground` hangs its bunting over: the code's 6 m pole tapered, with a red cap,
three hooks where the lines tie on and a guy rope to a peg; and a pennant at the code's .4 x .45, one white material for its three
colours, on a length of cord. T5g also maps the field's hay, the trucks at the gate and the stage's flag onto pieces already in the
repo (the MX hay bale, the rally truck, the rim flagpole). Shipped unverified.

## m698 -- the MX track's start gate and hay bales as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5f)

`models/campaign/mx_extras.glb`, for `buildBikeTrack`. The start gate on the hill's front edge at the code's seven posts across the
lanes: six drop-plates with blank number boards between them, the yellow bar along the top and the starter's release lever off the
end. And a hay bale at the code's 1.5 x .9 x .85, two twine bands and loose straw. Shipped unverified.

## m695 -- the trailer park's porches and awnings as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5e)

`models/campaign/trailer_porch.glb`, for `buildTrailerPark`. The awning at the code's 2.2 x 3.2: a corrugated tin sheet falling

## m495 -- the crash-site kit (scenery window, art only; the swap is ROADMAP T2e)

The detail pass's crash site. The wreck itself went in at m474; what was left round it was code: faceted berm ellipsoids over

into one ridge), three clods, a torn hull plate with rivets and a hazard stripe, a snapped strut with a glowing end, a cracked

per piece (`col_bld_cs_*`). Code untouched; the loop swaps it in (T2e). Shipped unverified.

## m475 -- the farm bushes (scenery window, art only; the swap is ROADMAP T2d)

Colin: *"bushes on the farm land."* `models/campaign/farm_bushes.glb`: four soft, rounded pieces in the Sites painting's greens --
`fb_hedge` (one 2.7 m hedge piece on an earth bank, the exact length of `FBOUND.piece`, so it replaces the bank ellipsoid and three
faceted ico0 clumps one for one), `fb_round`, `fb_cypress`, `fb_flower` (orange/red blooms: the five percent loud colour).
Every lump is flattened AT THE GROUND, not above it: the first render had every bush floating because the underside was clamped
relative to the lump's own radius rather than to y = 0. The hedge is subdivision 2 throughout (740 tris) because it repeats along
every field edge; the free-standing bushes can afford 3. No collider file: the hedge keeps its code box, the bushes are scenery.
Code untouched; the loop swaps it in (T2d). Shipped unverified.

## Landmines

- **RURAL TURF (m890, F6e-3, `TURF.AREAS` hc/fm, `A.on`).** Two more areas on m887's machinery: Hollow Creek (`HCREEK.bbox`, 5 x 5) and
  the farm (a box of `flWorld` at its four +/-A/+/-B corners, 5 x 5). **A rotated landmass's axis-aligned box takes in open sea next to
  Old Town** -- the farm's reached x 95 while Old Town's rect ends at 91 -- so `turfAt` answered for points in the strait and two
  places rows went BAD (`TURF ... OUTSIDE OLD TOWN`, `CROWD ... the spot off Old Town dealt`). Each rural area has `on(x, z)` (its own
  `hcEdge` / `flEdgeAt` > 0) and `turfAt` asks it. places 0 BAD, `prop spots 60/75`; play ch1 18 steps. F6 is done.

- **HELD BLOCKS SHOW IT IN THE OTHER REGIONS (m889, F6e-2, `TXD`, `txStep`, `txDress`, `txSpot`, `tx:<id>` flags, `mel.txGo(f)`).** For
  `TURF.xb` only: a non-current holder with `lead >= KSWAP.lead` for `KSWAP.hold` s (counted twice a second, the timer not saved) is
  SETTLED -- `progFlag('tx:<id>', faction)`, or the flag deleted when the NATIVE holder wins it back -- and `txDress` puts up one group
  of that faction's props (shared `txMats`, no colliders) at `txSpot`: the nearest point to the block's middle, on ground above the
  sea, with no box within .3 m of five probes 2 m apart at chest height. Saved settlements are dressed on the first `txStep`. places:
  `prop spots 20/25` (the five without are water). play ch1 20 steps.

- **BLACK CHARACTERS (m888, STEER 03:04, `KTX2SWAP`, the chip's `P/G/T`).** Baked `npm run ktx <glb> etc1s` for the fifteen
  characters still on WebP (alien_grey_medium, beautiful_asian/blonde, clancy, the seven fat_*, firefighter, hick_skinny, hobo_01,

- **THE LOST CONTEXT (m883, STEER 02:30, `CTX`, `ctxHook`, `ctxRender`, `REGG`, `regGate`, `regGateStep`, `CARRYK`).** His FRAME card at
  m875 was `shaderSource` <- `acquireProgram` <- the render: WebKit throws there only on a null shader, i.e. a LOST context (iOS, out of
  GPU memory). Now: `webglcontextlost` is `preventDefault`ed (so it can be restored), `ctxRender` skips the render while lost and
  swallows a throw that happens on a lost context (counted, `CTXLOST<n>` in the chip; any other throw still raises to the FRAME card).
  `CTX.info` = programs / geometries / textures / texture MB after the first render (`P G T` in the chip). **Region gates**: the seven
  far builds since m859 run through `regGate`, which reparents everything they added to `scene` into one group (their own `visible`
  untouched -- the Hills' clearing and the bus rely on theirs) and drops their frames from `FBATCH.frames` (a batched mesh would ignore
  the group); the group draws only within `pad` 220 m of the region's bounds. `S4.grey` is kept out (it follows him anywhere).
  Colliders and bodies are untouched. **m875's queue carries LEAKED** a geometry and a material per served person; now `CARRYK` shares
  one of each. That leak grows over minutes and cannot be a FIRST-frame crash, so the regions are the likelier straw.
  play ch1 18 steps in 319 s (faster than m874-m876's 385-611).

  KTX2Loader's `detectSupport` already ran at module top) once per hero, cached until `dispose`. Height: raw geometry bounds of the

`buildIslandSkate()`, which runs before `buildCarts()`, so it covers both.

**What the ranch's night gives:** surviving it (`ranch:night`) shows a round BLINK button above the right pad, in tkit only.

**How the blink works:**
- **Direction:** the way his horizontal velocity points, or his facing when he is still.
- **Distance:** marched in .4 m steps up to `dist` 7. Each step tests `camHit` at knee (+.45) and chest (+1.3) with pad .35,
  the same box test the bolt flies by, and the march stops at the first solid.
- **Too short:** under .8 m of clear air is a refusal, with a `ping`.
- **Effects:** sparks at both ends and a high swoosh.
- **Recharge:** `cool` 2.5 s, during which the button dims.

**Why a button:** the pads' unassigned gestures (left hold-in-place, a second tap) would fight the walk and the double jump.

**Untested:** whether a blink can carry him through a TRI-only (no box) surface, such as a kit wall's triangles. If it can,
the march wants a `groundAt` / SURF test too.

`play ch1` passed. Shipped unverified.

- **m797 (STEER): THE ALIEN GREY IS THE THIRD HERO (`HERO.files.grey` = `models/characters/alien_grey_medium.glb`, card ALIEN GREY,
  `?hero=grey`).** One table entry; the start screen's row lays three cards out with flex. His file was already hashed in `ASSETS`.
  Expect `WSC.011` with no turn: his tip is pure -X, 0.157 long. Expect the `HERO grey n/n` clip chip as on the lizard. He was
  built by the same pipeline, so expect `FLAT` on his flips if his hips came over flat too (m796 handles it).

- **m796 (STEER): FLAT HIPS ARE NOT A FLIP MEASUREMENT (`flipMarks`, `AIR.flatHips` .05, `AIR.flatAir` .81, `FLIP[*].flat`).** Read
  offline from both files: zap's `front_flip` hips go 33.4 -> 59.3 -> 29.3 cm (crouch at 0, apex .333, landing .708 of .875),
  while the alien lizard's are 0.00 at all 21 keys, and his `backflip` likewise. The argmin/argmax walk on a flat track returns
  noise, so `air` was a fraction of the clip, `flipDur` ran out early and `in_air` took the weight back mid-rotation. A hips range
  under 5% of their height now returns { from 0, air .81 x dur, off 0 }. The chip's flip token now carries the action's time,
  the clip length and the weight, plus FLAT. **The lizard's missing hips translation is his retarget dropping root motion**; it is
  reported to him, not patched over. `front_flip` is in `ONCE`.

- **m794 (STEER): A WEAPON'S FIT TO ITS WEARER IS MEASURED (`mountWeapon`, `weaponParts().tip`, `WEAP.fit`, chip `WSC`).** Identity
  was only right because zap's mount pair and the weapon files' pair are the same vector, (-14.3102, 0, 0), in centimetres under an
  Armature 0.01. The alien lizard's rig is in METRES, with its tip at (-0.140, 0, -0.072): 1/91 of the length and 27 degrees
  off -X. His guns were ~91x too big. The weapon group now takes `scale = |wearer| / |weapon|` and `quaternion = fromUnitVectors(weapon
  axis, wearer axis)`. **The muzzle is measured along the WEAPON's own axis in group space and then pushed through
  `group.matrix`**, so `muzzleWorld` (host.matrixWorld x muzzle) stays right. On zap the scale is exactly 1, measured: blaster and
  launcher tips -14.310176 against zap's -14.310177. This is not `weapFit` coming back: nothing is typed, both vectors are read off
  the files.

- **m793 (F5-4a): MOTHMAN (`MOTH`, `mothStep`, `mothAt`, `mothSite`, dormant quest `qmoth`).** He perches on the bridge's lamp
  arm half-way along it (`HCROAD.frame`: v on the lamp pitch, 24k + 12, u = hw - .9, the deck's `yv(v)` + 6.1). His states are
  perch -> fly (a smoothstep arc, `flyY` up at mid-flight, `flyV` m/s) -> omen (over the pod, the fuse running) -> rest
  (hidden for `rest` s). The pod is defused by standing within `r` for `hold` s; otherwise `fireStart` + `dhPushAt` -3. Being within
  70 m sets `qon:qmoth`; take-off sets `moth:follow`; a save sets `moth:saved`. **The fire cannot be put out by the player**
  (`fireDouse` has no caller but `mel.douse`). `places` 0 BAD; `play` ch0 and ch1 (run alone) pass.

- **m717 (F3-4): THE EM TELL** (`EMTELL`, `emAt`, `emSlow`, `emStep`). `emAt` = 1 - d / R (R 45, height counted at half) to the nearest
  `AIRT` target that is `on` (every orb), or .45 x the Hothouse twilight. `emStep` damps it to `EMTELL.k`. Above .05 it stutters
  every emissive material whose NAME says it is a light (collected once, base intensities kept, restored when it falls away), and
  above .25 it plays short irregular `zap` static. `emSlow` is folded into the farm vehicles' wanted speed (`vehStep`); it is
