- **THE HOTHOUSE'S TWILIGHT, SPREAD AND CUT (m642, F2d-2, `HOTH.tw/every/push/cap/cut`, `hothCut`).**
  - **The twilight** damps in by how grown the player's block is. **It snapshots the fog colour and the sun and hemi
    intensities when it starts, writes from that base every frame while it is on, and restores and drops the base at zero.**
    It is never a lerp of the live value, which would creep a little further every frame.
  - **The spread:** every 40 s a random held block pushes .1 share into a random non-held 4-neighbour (`turfPush`, saved),
    up to `cap` 18 held. It toasts when a block falls.
  - **The cut:** `boltHit` calls `hothCut`. A bolt in a grown, held block takes `cut` x (.5 + charge) off `skin` there,
    spits teal sparks, and toasts when the block is lost. The save is batched (`dirty`, at most every 5 s), not one write per
    bolt.
  The melee strike does not cut yet.

  the lip (s | v | grade | g | dy | arm | y): `11.9 16.1 ... a 3.93 A0.8 0.1`, `13.5 ... a -1.61 A0.9 -1.0`, `16.7 ... g ... -2.5`

  (`> landAt - .5`) rather than a typed 12. (2) **A lip at speed launched level** -- a frame at 16 m/s is 0.53 m, longer than
  the 0.4 m probe, so the integrator dropped him off the lip before `bladeSurfPost` could see it and the next frame read the
  downhill: `bladeSurfPre` now launches on the face behind him when the grade ahead breaks from it by `leave` (her skates get
  it too, which is the same bug for her); and the face test's .12 tolerance grows with the grade (a kicker is a curve).
  (3) **Bodies out of the world.** A spot is remembered only with a real floor under it (`groundAt`, every 0.5 s); a quest's
  body (`qTag`) in the sea counts as out of the world; one that never stood comes up beside him. (4) **A body turned or cured
  out of the world comes out where it last stood** (`virusGo`): the keeper, beaten in the shallows, came back in the water.
  Ch1 and ch4 replayed clean after all of it. **Harness:** teleports to a target's own level stop 0.8 m from it (a few metres
  short is water off a rock); a big boss step gets 200 s; the board run waits 0.5 s grounded before calling it short (the
  game's gap test reads `grounded` a frame later); the log tail is 10 lines.

- **TWO BOARD BUGS, AND THE ISLANDS' GAP IS CLEARABLE AT LAST (m483, `boardGrade`, `stepSkate`).** The playthrough's trace along the
  gap ramp's line (s | speed along the deck | grade | grounded): `-14.8 4.2 +0.65 g`, then `-13.6 6.6 -1.00 g` and rolling back.
  (1) **`boardGrade` read a steep DESCENT as a wall.** Each probe took floors only up to `MOVE.step * 2` (0.7 m) over his feet;
  `SK8.probe` is 1.2 m, so on anything steeper than ~30 degrees the deck BEHIND him was out of the window, the probe fell
  through to the ground under the ramp, and the grade clamped to -1 -- uphill, full brake. The window is now
  `MOVE.step * 2 + probe * 1.2` (up to a 1:1.2 slope). (2) **The board launched every kicker LEVEL**: at the lip, 16.9 m/s
  and vy -0.7 off a 25 degree kick, down 4 m past it in the sea (12 needed). Her skates had surface-following since m269
  (`bladeSurfPre/Post`: velocity along the face, a lip left on its angle) and the board never did; it does now (not the bike).
  **Both bugs were in every board ride in the game**, not just this ramp. With them fixed the driver clears the gap (102 s,
  several runs), the needle, the lighthouse. **Still open:** the keeper's Skinsuit at y -1000 (F0b-2b-4c).

  him RIGHT: `heading -= x`). Down inside the 6.5 m ring in about a second, every run. **The gap, measured:** as himself (a

  3.6 m of drop at g 20 is ~12 m/s and the board's slope term is 11 m/s^2 per unit grade. **Something on that deck is not
  giving him the grade, or the kick's first quads stop him** -- the next pass instruments `boardGrade` there before touching
  anything. The tip ("flat out from the top... a tail gust helps") reads as if it was never ridden either.

  (`kitObb` on his `col_bld_rb_*`, through the gate's transform). `npm run play`'s header: `roadblocks 2 dressed, 1 solid`.

- **THE BALLOON STOPS RE-WRAPPING (m471, `talkShow`, `talkLetter`, `#talk.comic`).** *"Based on how you're looking at them it's
  always adjusting the line wrap."* `#talk` was `width: auto` at a moving `left`, and a fixed box's shrink-to-fit width is the
  screen LEFT BESIDE IT -- so every camera turn changed the line breaks. It is measured once when a line opens, at `left: 0`
  (the whole screen to fit in, so `max-width` decides), and its width pinned; only `left`/`top` follow him after. **The
  lettering cannot move a break either**: the whole line is always laid out, the words not yet lettered in a
  `visibility: hidden` span. The tail is `--tail`, his projected x inside the balloon, so a balloon held off an edge still
  points at him. Comic style is on by default; the fonts come from Google Fonts with system fallbacks, so a phone offline
  gets Comic Sans rather than nothing. **A tap mid-lettering finishes the line** (the playthrough's six taps a talk still
  finish every script: ch1 18/18). **Handing off T2:** yes -- see Decisions; the level window owns `models/campaign/` art.

- **CHAPTER 3 PLAYS THROUGH, AND THE BIKER RODE FOR THE FIRST TIME (m470).** *Four game faults the playthrough found:*
  (1) **`boardBusy` refused the board to every disguise but her skates** (`p.mphK && !bladeOn()`, m263), and the biker IS a
  disguise -- so since m374 wearing him never put him on his bike, the race could never start, and `bikeOn()` read true the
  whole time. `!bikeOn()` joins the exception. **A derived state with two conditions needs both checked when a third mode
  arrives** -- the skates added an exception and the bike, one mode later, did not.
  (2) **The start hill's back was a staircase across the whole track** (`buildBikeTrack`), and the loop runs THROUGH the hill:
  lap 1 starts on top, lap 2 arrives at the back and stopped dead (0.9 m/s). It is a ramp now (h / .26 long, both windings),
  so the hill is the lap's jump. `places`' own race row said WON (it starts lap 1 and never asks about lap 2).
  (3) **A body knocked where there is no floor** (the creek under the stilts: `groundAt` -1000) fell to -1000 and stayed there
  -- a quest's biker gone. Every body remembers where it last stood (`d.okX/Y/Z`, at rest above -50) and is put back there.
  (4) **`texLoad` let `KTX2Loader.load` THROW at module scope** -- node's fetch does on a relative URL, so `npm run places` died
  at boot from m425 to now and no build since has had its place check. Caught into `onErr` now; places runs clean.
  *And one pacing fix:* the rally is called within 15 s while ch3c waits on the speech within 60 m of the stage.
  *Harness:* a race driver (`gang:respect`): the biker form, still at the gate for the countdown, then the line itself -- its
  nearest point in a window behind-to-ahead of the last one (never further back, so running wide cannot turn him round), aimed
  14 m past. The first version advanced its target only while he was near it, ran wide, turned round, and rode 2.5x the lap.

- **THE LOOSE SHEETS TO KTX2 (m425, F0a-2d-2, `tools/ktxpng.mjs`, `texTwin`, `texLoad`, `texLoadAsync`, `KTX2SWAP` +4).** A PNG
  through `TextureLoader` is sampled with `flipY = true`; a KTX2 through `KTX2Loader` with `flipY = false` -- so the twin is
  encoded `isYFlip: true` (the flip baked into the pixels) and the sheets' `grid`/`cut` maths reads the same frame. The fire,
  water and crack sheets set `minFilter = LinearFilter` and `generateMipmaps = false`, so their twins are baked `nomip` (a
  third fewer bytes); the atlas and the trim keep their mips. `texLoad` returns the texture object either way (`kl.load`
  returns its CompressedTexture up front like `TextureLoader` does), so `FL.sheetT = texLoad(...)` still holds one.
  **THE SKY'S PNG IS NOT A CANDIDATE**: `skyImgFog` reads rows of pixels off `skyImg`'s image for the fog colour, and a
  compressed texture has no image to read. It is 8 MB resident for the HDRI key's live swap. **`ktx2` HAD TO GO INTO
  `bump.mjs`'s `EXT`** -- the twelfth time the hash table was one entry short (CLAUDE.md's "check EXT too").
  Baked (the tool's own report, resident): impact_marks_atlas 8 -> 2, fire_01 8 -> 1.5 (nomip), fire_02 2 -> .3, fire_03
  5 -> 1, water 5 -> 1, crack 5 -> 1, weirdport_trim 21 -> 5.3; the GLBs zap 5 -> 1, alien_female_purple 21 -> 5,
  alien_base_01 21 -> 5, alien_tower_01 21 -> 5. Measured on the page: tkit 193 -> 176 MB, weirdport 240 -> 128, test
  202 -> 78. Left in the kit city: `hdri_game.png 8.0M` (above), `paint_atlas 5.3M` (a 1K canvas the paint shader makes
  in the page), an unnamed `5.3M`, Moussa's two at 5.3 (UASTC; ETC1S would be 1.3 each).

- **m421 HID EVERY BODY PAST 45 m, AND THE MEASURE COULD NOT SEE IT (m422, F0a-2g, `perfRegBodyParts`, `PERF.partFrac`).**
  The parts cull registered any mesh of a body whose `geometry.boundingSphere.radius x matrixWorld scale` was under .45 m.
  For a skinned Mixamo rig that product is ~0.01 m for the WHOLE MAN: the geometry is the authored metre-scale mesh (a
  hick's sphere 0.67), the matrixWorld carries the armature's 0.01 x the rig scale (0.0206), and the bones undo the 0.01
  at x100 -- the size is in the skinning, not in either matrix. The skinned sphere (`skeleton.update();
  computeBoundingSphere()`) is no better at spawn (no pose yet: the same 0.01) and 60 after a frame. **So every body's main
  mesh went into the cull and was moved to layer 1 past 45 m.** The tool's `bodies <drawn>/<near>` reads `root.visible`
  and said 74/74 while 50 of them were invisible; its `who` showed the crowd as `construction_worker 44` one run and
  `construction_worker 20` the next, which I read as the cull working. **A COUNT THAT DOES NOT MEASURE THE THING IT NAMES**
  -- the fourth time this repo has been caught by one, and the first I shipped.
  The size is RELATIVE now: the biggest geometry sphere in the body is the body; a part is anything under `partFrac` (.25) of
  it. Measured (`scratchpad/sph.mjs`, kept as `tools/bodies.mjs`? no -- the composition is in this note): the officer's
  eyes are 6% of him, Colin's trainers 21%, headphones 24%, teeth 13%, his head 43% and Moussa's head 28% -- heads stay. Most
  kinds are ONE mesh (hick, hobo, activist, hippie, hipster, biker, suit, Trump, the two women, the worker, Clancy); the
  officer is 2 (eyes), the warrior 2 (the mace), Moussa 2, Jack 2, Colin 6. A one-mesh body still measures ~2 draws in
  town (F0a-2h asks why). The shadow pass costs nothing here (560 draws with and without it: shadows are not rendering in
  the kit city).
  Honest after the fix: oldtown 610 (74 bodies drawn, 74 near), camp 251, islanding 350.

- **THE MEASURE'S BODY CULL CALLED THE WRONG FUNCTION, AND EVERY IN-TOWN NUMBER FROM m417 TO m420 WAS WRONG (m421, F0a-2f).**
  m417 put the body cull in `bodyCull()` (the function `frameBody` calls once a frame); m418 made the measure's settle call
  `perfStep` "so the cull runs" -- `perfStep` is the resolution governor and never touches a body. So bodies kept whatever
  `visible` the game's own slow frames had left them with: measured FIRST in a run, every body drew (oldtown 835); measured
  after the spawn, the crowd stayed hidden (4 of 74 near bodies drawn, oldtown 538-741). **A HARNESS THAT MEASURES A PATH
  THE GAME DOES NOT TAKE MEASURES A DIFFERENT GAME** -- the oldest rule here, and the tool now prints `bodies <drawn>/<near>/
  <all>` at every place so that disagreement cannot hide again. The far-place numbers (m417-m420) stand: there the game's
  frames had hidden the crowd and the tool's result matched the real one.
  **THE KIT'S PARTS AS A `BatchedMesh` PER MATERIAL (`KIT.multi`, `PERF.multi`, chip `md`).** `kitInst` builds one BatchedMesh per
  material + attribute signature + indexed-ness (`addGeometry` per distinct door geometry, `addInstance` per door) when
  `renderer.extensions.has('WEBGL_multi_draw')`, else the InstancedMesh sets as before; `kitInstSync` writes both through
  `setMatrixAt` and flags `instanceMatrix` only where it exists. `cellReg`/`cellStep` read `m.boundingSphere` for a
  BatchedMesh as for an InstancedMesh (its `geometry.boundingSphere` is null). SwiftShader has the extension; his phone is
  unknown and the chip's `md` says.
  **A BODY'S SMALL PARTS (`perfRegBodyParts`, `PERF.partR/partFar`)**: at `bodySpawn`, every mesh of the body under .45 m world
  radius (the armature's 0.01 is in `matrixWorld`) registered `cellReg(o, 45, true)` -- by layer, since `model.visible` is
  the morph's and the virus's. Bodies are clones of the prototype (`proto.clone(true)`, not of each other), so a layer set
  on one body's eye never reaches a disguise.

- **THE TOON CITY'S FAR COPY (m420, F0a-2e, `lodAdd` for InstancedMesh, `TCITY.lodOut`).** `lodAdd` takes instanced sets now:

  draws apiece). At 90 m: 360. The trade is draws for triangles (a far copy's sphere never leaves the frustum), which
  CLAUDE.md's rule settles: draw calls are the first thing that costs anything here.

- **THE FAR COPIES (m419, F0a-2c, `LOD`, `lodAdd(name, meshes, out, { flat })`, `KIT.lodOut`, `FBATCH.lodOut`, `cellStep`).** Each
  cell-batched set (`kitBatch`'s meshes per material per 48 m cell; `farmBatch`'s per material per 200 m cell) gets its
  cells merged once more into one mesh per material -- the far copy -- and `cellStep` decides per frame, per set, by the
  lens's distance OUTSIDE the set's rectangle (`L.out`): far -> the copies draw and every cell is off; else the cells draw
  and the copies are off. One writer (the cells' `visible` was already `cellStep`'s; `userData.lodOf` / `lodFar`).
  **THE FARM'S BATCHES SPAN THE WHOLE MAP** -- every farmFrame of every region goes through `farmBatch` -- so the first cut,
  one far copy for all of them, was NEVER far from the lens (its rectangle is Weirdport) and 21 MB of copies drew nothing.
  Now a copy per 200 m cell (`userData.fbCell`, parsed off the bucket key), FLAT: one shared `flatShading` vertex-colour
  material, no normal attribute (the shader takes the normal off the triangle), a third fewer bytes, the paint/metal/
  emissive keys folded (gone at 180 m). The kit's copy keeps its materials: `tcTint`/`kitCutMat`/`kitWobMat` hook them
  through `onBeforeCompile`, which `clone()` does not carry, so a flat kit copy would lose the city's tint.
  `mergeLeaves(G.g, flames + planks)` on every gate (46 grey posts at Old Town's cordon were 46 draws; `gateStep` only ever
  toggles the whole group).

- **THE FAR CULLS (m417, F0a-2a, `PERF.bodyFar`, `KIT.partFar`, `cellReg(m, ownFar)`, `npm run worlds --who`).** The measure

  material's name, else the nearest named ancestor's. The first `--who` of the kit city said the same thing at every place:

  Mothership's core alike. **THE KIT CITY'S FOG IS 950 m** (`KCITY.fog`, so the skyline reads from the farm), so the fog
  cull (`cellStep`) hides nothing inside Weirdport; everything that is small needs a distance of its own.
  Bodies: in `perfStep`'s loop, `d.root.visible` off beyond `bodyFar` from `camera.position` (the root, so sprites and props
  go with it), and `d.seen` cleared so a hidden body animates at `animHz`. Nothing else toggles `d.root.visible` (the virus
  and the morphs toggle `model.visible`, a child). Parts: `kitInst` computes each set's sphere, pads it 3 m for a door's
  swing, turns `frustumCulled` on, and registers it with `cellReg(im, KIT.partFar)` -- `cellStep` now honours a per-mesh
  `userData.ownFar` under the fog's. Every `farmFrame` merge is named `tag:material` so `--who` can name the rest.
  **`partFar` LANDED IN `TCITY` FIRST**: a `fog:` line matched in two objects and the replace took the first; `KIT.partFar`
  read undefined and the cull was silently off. Checked by printing the owning `const` of the inserted line.

- **THE MEASURE (m416, F0a-1, `perfMem`, `PERF.mem`, `PERF.bootMs`, `mel.mem()`, `npm run worlds`, `tools/worlds.mjs`).**
  `perfMem` walks the scene's materials (every map slot, shader uniforms, `scene.environment`/`background`), counts each
  texture once at its RESIDENT size -- a KTX2 `CompressedTexture` at the byte size of its mip chain, anything else at
  w x h x 4 (x 4/3 with mips, x faces for a cube) -- and every geometry at its attributes' bytes. The chip's perf line
  runs it every `PERF.memEvery` (3) s. `renderer.info.memory.textures` is higher than the material count (327 vs 147 in
  the kit city): render targets, the PMREM chain and the shadow map are GL textures no material names.
  **`npm run worlds` DOES NOT WAIT FOR THE GAME'S OWN FRAME LOOP.** Under SwiftShader a frame runs seconds (or none in a
  minute), and the first version's 2.5 s settle read the THREE camera where the LAST place had left it -- pearl and overlook
  came back identical to the triangle. `godPlace` moves `cam.pos`; only `stepCam` copies it into `camera`. So after
  `mel.go` the tool calls `stepCam(1/30)` ten times and `cellStep()` itself, then renders one frame and reads `info`.
  A settle-in-frames version (`info.render.frame` + 3, 60 s) never saw a frame at any place and was thrown out.

- **NIGHT SIGNALS (m415, E2, `RADIO`, `buildRadio`, `radioStep`, `radioNext`, `radioSay`, `radioNear`, `radioDeeds`, `radioSight`).**
  Art's roof is his `kit_010` (178 deg, so very nearly axis-aligned; interior x -24.0..-16.2, z 57.7..65.6; the hatch in the

  **THERE ARE NO CARS IN THE KIT CITY** (no car node in the visual, the collider or the breakables), so "every car radio" is
  every RADIO: `radioNear` names the source (the chip's line does not, the bar does not; `mel.RADIO` and `radioNear()`
  do). **The mast's legs are rods**: `farmFrame`'s `geo` takes an Euler (XYZ), so a cylinder between two points is
  `setFromUnitVectors(up, dir)` read back into an Euler -- written once as `rod` inside `buildRadio`.
  The hub reads `talk.cur.markId === 'radio_host'` once per conversation (`tipFor`); the payphone is a disc of
  `phoneR` and calls in every `rmdone:` without an `rmcall:`. **The ticker is its own element** (`#radio`, made on the first
  line, bottom 84 px above the toast, max 54 vw so it clears both pads), never the toast or the tip.

  joint, a SEAT marker), ridden round a ring in the test site only (`MOTO`) -- so it is loaded a second time in the kit city
  as the PLAYER'S (`PBIKE`, its own record; `buildMoto` is left alone because `MOTO.up` drives the ring bike). The physics
  is the board's, Rollergirl's pattern: `mode: 'bike'` on the BIKER kind, `bikeOn()` (worn, finished becoming him, the
  bike loaded, the kit city), `boardOut()` true, `p.bike` beside `p.blade`, and `stepSkate`'s numbers `BIKE` over `SK8`:
  a THROTTLE in place of the push stroke (`acc` 8 while the thumb points the way he is going, tapering to `top` 27 against
  the board's 19), a long roll, a hard brake, slower steering at speed, a smaller pop. OFF on a bike: both pads' flicks
  (`boardFlick` eats them -- no deck tricks, no body flips, no dismount: revert to walk, the skates' rule), the grind catch
  and the second jump. Drawn under him on his floor along his heading, LEANING into the turn, the fork STEERED by `MOTO`'s
  wheelbase arithmetic (`atan(L w / v)`, clamped at 20 degrees), the wheels at distance over the measured radius. He SITS:
  his root lifted by the seat's measured height (`PBIKE.seat`, off the seat bone) less his hips' height over his root in the
  driving clip, read off his posed skeleton a frame late (`stepRide`'s m109 rule), and his three driving clips blend by how
  hard it steers, summing to 1 (his idle if a clip is missing -- never a zero table, which is the T-pose).

  table (02, the one with the driving clips) first -- so Hollow Creek's bikers were already him. They say 02 now, the
  quest's sample says 02, and `places` fails a Hollow Creek biker who is not him.
  **UNVERIFIED, AND THESE ARE THE PHONE'S QUESTIONS**: which way it leans (`mel.MOTO.lean` negative flips it, shared with

- **NO GATE EVER LET ANY FORM THROUGH: `need` WAS A FILE STEM, `formNow()` THE DISPLAY FORM (m334, `mphFold`, `gateLets`).** The same
  bug as m332's `mkrKind`, one system over: `GATE_TYPES.cordon.need` is 'dummy_officer', `formNow()` is 'DUMMY OFFICER', and
  `me === T.need` never held -- from m285, every gate held everyone back (and no `fix` gate could ever be mended). **One
  fold now, `mphFold(stem)`, the same transform `mphName` applies to a kind's file**, used by `mkrKind` and by `gateLets`.
  **Any table that names a form by its FILE must go through it before it meets `mphName`/`formNow`.** Grep for the next one.

  mark's `K` false, not one body spawned, ever. `mphName(K)` is 'HOBO' / 'HICK SKINNY' (alien prefix and number off, `_`
  to space, upper case); `mkrKind` looked up `MKR.alias` ('hobo' -> 'hobo_01') and compared THAT to it raw. Never equal,
  never a prefix. So since m293 **every** `npc_*` marker -- his from Blender as much as the farmhands -- placed nothing,
  and the note `MKR NPC <id> kind?` went to the chip where nobody looked. The stem now goes through the same fold as
  `mphName` before the compare.
  **And `places` said "ok FARMHANDS" the whole time**, because it checked the marks' POSITIONS (on the farmland) and never
  whether they became anybody. It now runs `mkrNpcPlace` and fails a mark with no kind (`WITH NO KIND`):

- **WHO TALKS TO WHOM: A GROUP PER FORM, A BRUSH-OFF LINE FOR THE WRONG SORT, THE ALIEN RUN OFF (m332, B1f-3, `SOCIAL`,
  `socialGroup`, `socialMe`, `socialOk`, `socialBrush`, `QUESTS[].from`).** GAME_DESIGN "soft social friction". Every form
  is in a group off its name (`SOCIAL.groups`, regexes on `mphName`: country, street, law, worker, city, biker, crew,
  alien, else folk); undisguised you are 'alien' (`fearLooks`, the same test the fear uses). A speaker has `group`
  (default its kind's), `talks` (the groups it talks to properly; default its own) and `alien` ('flee' default, or
  'brush'), off its mark's props -- so his Blender `npc_*` markers can carry `group`, `talks` (comma list) and `alien`.
  - **The wrong sort** gets ONE line from `SOCIAL.BRUSH[their group][yours]` (else `.any`), `tap ×`, and it is over: not
    finished, nothing heard, no rumour, no `talk:` in the save. Light, never mean ("You lost? The coffee place is forty
    miles that way.").
  - **The alien**: m278's "a speaker with something unsaid does not panic" now only holds for `alien: 'brush'` -- by default
    a speaker runs from the alien like anyone (A4's fear). One who brushes him off gets the alien line.
  - **A task can come FROM somebody** (`from: '<talk id>'`): it is not available until that script is finished -- which
    only happens in a form he talks to. "Only a farmhand will get anything out of old Mabel."
  - The farmhands are `country` and talk to `country` and `street` (they are hobo bodies with farm jobs; a tramp gets a
    chat, a hipster gets the coffee line).
  **Checked headless**: Wendell existed (he never had), the alien got "Nope. Not today. Not ever.", wearing the hick he
  told his three lines and the rail-bridge rumour -- `talk:mk_farmhand_wendell` and `rm:trestle` saved. Chip `SOCIAL.brushes`.

- **RUMOURS: HEARD AS A SCRIPT'S LAST LINE, A ROUGH RING ON THE MAP, FOUND BY GOING THERE (m331, B1f-2, `RUMOURS`,
  `rumourHear`, `rumourStep`, `rumourCircle`).** GAME_DESIGN: "vague ... a separate list with no marker, or at most a
  rough circle on the map ... often how the best stuff is found". A rumour is a row: `title` (the card and the list),
  `gist` (what you remember), `say` (the line somebody tells it in), `at` (the place, read LIVE -- the crop circle off
  `FPLAN.crash.circle`, the trestle's farm end, the ford), `r` (how close counts as found) and an optional `circle`.
  - **Heard**: a mark's `rumour` APPENDS `say` to that person's lines (a copy -- a `TALKS` script is shared) and finishing
    the conversation calls `rumourHear` -> `rm:<id>` = who said it, a RUMOUR card. The farmhands carry three: Dale (the
    wheat) the ring in the wheat, Wendell (the west hill) the old rail bridge, Earl (the plough) the cows' way over
    the water. `hillman` is in the table for B1f-4's neighbour to give out.
  - **Listed**: the task list's RUMOURS section, the gist in quotes and who said it; found ones under DONE. Not
    followable -- no beam, no waypoint, no objective line. That is the whole difference from a task.
  - **On the map**: a dashed sky ring and a '?' on the FULL map only, its centre pushed .45 r off the true spot in a
    direction fixed per rumour (a hash of the id) -- so it says "round here", and the same thing every time you open it.
  - **Found**: twice a second (`rumourStep`, after `questStep`), within `r` of the place -> `rmdone:<id>`, RUMOUR FOUND,
    a task's worth of juice. Chip `RM<heard>/<found>`. GOD -> HEAR EVERY RUMOUR.
  **Checked headless** (the probe again: a throw in a per-frame step freezes the game): all four listed with "(GOD)",
  the full map opened with the rings, and GOD `stones` -> RUMOUR FOUND / A WAY OVER THE WATER, `rmdone:ford` saved.

- **TASKS: SEVERAL AT ONCE, ONE FOLLOWED, A CARD WHEN ONE ARRIVES, AND THE SAME METRES IN THREE PLACES (m330, B1f-1,
  `questAvail`, `questTrack`, `tasksOpen`, `questWpt`, `#tasks`, `#wpt`).** GAME_DESIGN "Direction and discovery": a task
  comes from someone, a card pops up ("New task: ..."), it goes in your list, and you get a map marker and a waypoint
  in the world that shows the distance.
  - **More than one task**: `questAvail()` is every quest unlocked and not done (m293's dormant switch still applies);
    the one everything follows is `SAVE.flags.qtrack`, else the first. m278 ran "the first one not done" only.
  - **The card**: the first frame a task is available and not `qseen:` in the save, `cardShow('NEW TASK', title)` --
    once ever, one card at a time (`newT` = the card's own life + .4 s).
  - **The list**: tap the objective pill (it takes pointer events now, `stopPropagation` so a tap is never a pad touch)
    or GOD -> THE TASK LIST. ON THE GO, each with its current step and, on the followed one, the metres; tap one to
    follow it. DONE below, greyed.
  - **The waypoint's distance in the world** (`questWpt`, after the camera, beside `skylineStep`): a gold label 2.4 m
    over the beam's target; off screen or behind, pinned to the side the target is on (camera-space x) with an arrow.
    **`quest.d` is the one number** the label, the objective line and the full map's gold dot all print -- "the map
    marker matches it" by construction (the minimap only keeps its rim dot: it turns, and text on it would too).
  - Steps can name a place READ LIVE: `at: () => [x, y, z]` on `reach`, `() => [x, z]` on `goto` -- so a task can point
    at the silo's landing or the bridge's checkpoint without a typed coordinate.
  - A dormant second stand-in, `qtour` THE LAY OF THE LAND (climb the silo, the terrace top, the bridge checkpoint),
    so the list has two to choose between. GOD -> THE STAND-IN TASKS.
  **Checked headless** (a throwaway probe on the shot tool -- a throw in `questStep` would freeze every frame, and no gate
  ticks it): both on, the card read NEW TASK / WEIRDPORT 101, the list showed both, tracking `qtour` turned the line
  to "Climb the silo · 19m" and the waypoint to "◀19 m", pinned left.

- **THE STAMPEDE: A PANIC SPREADS THROUGH THE HERD, A RUNNING COW IGNORES ITS FIELD AND RUNS HIM DOWN (m329, B1e-3,
  `cowPanic`, `cowFright`, `cowSpook`, `COW.stampede` ...).** REGIONS' signature system for the farm: "cows wander, panic
  and stampede when frightened, and block lanes". On the m294 brain (graze / look / walk / trot) a fourth state, `run`:
  - **What frightens a cow**: a SHOT -- `fireBolt` calls `cowFright(muzzle, fearR 34)` -- and the ALIEN, undisguised
    (`fearLooks`, the same test the humans' fear uses), within `alienR` 6 m. A man in a human form running past still
    only startles it into the old trot. There is no shared "noise event" in this game; `cowFright(x, z, r)` is the
    cows' own, and anything else loud (a blast, a cop's pistol) is one call to it.
  - **It spreads**: `cowPanic` sets every herd-mate within `spreadR` 14 m that is not already running to `spook` after
    `spreadT` .15-.7 s, along the SAME heading (+-.25 rad) -- so a herd bolts as a herd, in a ripple, not as one cow.
  - **Running**: the target runs 8 m ahead along the flight heading, wavering +-.3 rad; `stampede` 5.6 m/s (faster than
    he jogs, slower than he sprints), turning 3x a walk, easing off over the last 2 s of `panicT` 7-11 s. **It ignores its
    field** (no `fpOwnAt` test while running) -- through the gaps, out onto the tracks and the lanes, which is "block
    lanes" -- then walks back toward its field when the panic is spent (and may well stand at a fence a while: that is
    a cow). Walls, fences and drops still stop it: a running cow that meets one TURNS (+-1.3 rad, alternating by index)
    instead of dropping to graze. Brown dust off its heels every .3 s within 60 m (the smoke pool), a high short bellow
    every 1.4-3.5 s (`mooAt` x1.32), head low, a bigger bob and a full leg swing.
  - **It runs him down**: in the bulk shove, a running cow `playerHurt`s him -- 7 damage, push 7 along its run, a
    knock-down -- once per cow per 1.5 s. GOD takes no damage (playerHurt returns), so to feel it, leave GOD.
  GOD SWITCHES: **SPOOK THE NEAREST HERD (STAMPEDE)** (`mel.cowSpook()`); `mel.cowFright(x, z, r)`. Chip: `COW..p<panics>
  h<hits>`. **`places` now spooks a herd before it ticks the farm's steps**, so the 30 frames of `cowStep` run the
  stampede branch -- a throw there is caught by `frame()` and freezes every frame after it.

- **THE ORCHARD TERRACE IS BUILT UP, NOT CUT IN: FOUR STONE TIERS ON THE ORCHARD'S OWN OUTLINE (m328, B1e-2, `FTERR`,
  `buildOrchardTerrace`, `ftRad`, `ftEdge`, `ftIn`).** Measured first (a throwaway probe on the places harness): the
  orchard stood on a 1.6 m swell (1.35..3.02 m over 2,580 m2) -- nothing to cut a terrace into. So the tiers are BUILT:
  tier 0 at the highest ground inside it + .3, each next one `rise` 1.4 m up (3.33 / 4.73 / 6.13 / 7.53), the
  "exaggerated scale" rule -- a hill of apple rows you climb.
  **The outline is the field's, measured**: from the seed, `NT` 96 directions, march out while `fpOwner` gives the orchard
  at the point AND `margin` 3 m past it, then smooth twice (a 1-2-3-2-1 kernel: a noisy owner border would be a
  saw-toothed wall). Upper tiers are that outline x (1 - .22k). Base radius 13.7..34.8 m. `TERRACE NO ROOM` if under 6.
  **Walls**: dry-stone boxes every 1.8 m along each outline (360 samples, arc-length stepped), turned along it, from the
  tier below (or the ground - .4) to the tier top + a .25 lip; moss on the coping of ~half. **Stairs**: one flight a tier
  at `stepAt[k]`, nudged within +-.6 rad to the WIDEST ring there (the flight must fit on the tier below), .28 m risers,
  and the wall leaves a gap exactly its width. The way up winds round the hill.
  **The tops are walkable triangles (`isleAppend`), wound UP by a cross-product test** -- `triAdd` keeps up-facing floors
  only and `flWorld` is a reflection of (a, b), so the winding is derived per triangle, never assumed. They draw with the
  farmland's OWN material (`aSplat` all grass, `aFld` the orchard's tint), so the terrace grass is the same grass.
  **Built after `buildFarmWaters`, before `buildFieldBounds`** -- and the apple trees after the tops are in `TRI`, so
  `farmTree`'s `gnd` stands each one on its tier. **The field's grid rows skip the terrace (`ftIn`)** -- they fell on walls
  more often than not -- and the terrace plants its own: a ring down the middle of each tier every ~5.5 m (off walls and
  stairs by `ftEdge` 1.9), a ring and a centre tree on top; 54 trees, six apples in every crown and two in the grass,
  and two crates (one full) at the head of each stair.
  **Cost**: FBATCH static tris 114k -> 184k (the crowns are ico-1, ~550 tris a tree), draw calls unchanged (batched:
  77 batches). Triangles are the last thing that costs here; watch it if the farm grows more trees.
  GOD `orchard` is now the foot of the first stair, `terrace` the top. Judged with `npm run shot terrace` (new row).

- **THE COWS ARE ROUNDED AND THE HERDS GRAZE TOGETHER (m326, farm polish 5, `COW.round`, `COW.herdP` / `herdR`, `cowPick`,
  `FHERDS`).** The herd shot: two brick cows a long way apart on an empty hill. Two causes, two fixes:
  1. **every part was a unit BOX** (m294: one `InstancedMesh`, 16 instances a cow). It is now a ROUNDED box -- a unit box
     cut 2 x 2 x 2 with each vertex pulled `round` .5 of the way to the sphere through the face centres
     (`v * (1 - k + k * .5 / |v|)`: a face centre is exactly on both, so the part still fills its unit cube and every size
     in `cowDraw` means what it meant), `toNonIndexed` + flat normals. 48 triangles a part instead of 12: 39 + 3 cows x 16
     parts x 48 = ~32k, one draw call still. `COW.round = 0` is the old boxes (wants a reload).
  2. **a herd was five independent random walks over a whole field** (`cowPick` picked anywhere in its home radius, which
     is the field's). Now 70% of picks (`herdP`) are within `herdR` 7 m of a random herd-mate, and at build each cow after
     the first starts near an earlier one -- so a herd is a herd. The field test still applies to every pick (places:
     `COWS 39 ... all in their pastures`). Herds grew a little: far hill, ridge, east 7; pond 5.
  Judged with the new `npm run shot herd` (and `house`, whose camera lands in a tree -- a shot row, not a game bug).

- **THE WRECK IS THE HERO: x1.6, A BOW WAVE OF EARTH, MOUNDS FOR BERMS, A PATCHY SCORCH (m325, farm polish 4, `CRASH.S`,
  `buildCrash`, `crashHero`, `FPLAN.crash`).** m324's shots: a 3.3 m saucer sitting in the wheat like a dropped plate,
  at the end of what read as a purple canal between brown plank walls. STEER: "the wreck as a hero moment".
  1. **`CRASH.S` 1.6 scales the wreck and everything placed off it** -- hull, rim, canopy, core, panels, the two
     colliders, the fires, the smoke, Clancy's hatch, the spawn (`you`, now 15.2 m out), and in `crashHero` the core,
     the light pool, the crystals and the arc radius. **One number, read everywhere** -- a scale applied to the hull
     alone would have put the hatch and the fires INSIDE it.

     height and offset all jittered so they are not a row of sausage links (the first pass was), rising toward the
     wreck by a*a to ~1.1 m (colliders match). Clods are icosahedron lumps, not bricks. **A seeded `cr()` replaces
     `Math.random()`** here, so the furrow is the same furrow every load.
  3. **The bow wave**: the earth the nose ploughed up, an ellipsoid ahead of it 7.8 m across (+ collider), turf clods

- **THE HEDGE BANKS ARE MOUNDS, NOT BOXES; THE BOX IS ONLY THE COLLIDER NOW (m324, farm polish 3, `buildFieldBounds`,
  `buildLane` `banks` / `bankProf` / `bankEnd`).** m321's road shot: every bank a hard earth slab with vertical sides.
  Two builders, two fixes, one rule -- **`bx(...)` then `parts[mat].pop()` keeps the collider and drops the slab**, and
  something softer is drawn in its place:
  1. **the field hedges (FPLAN, 380 pieces)**: an ellipsoid (`ico1`) along the run, half-length (piece + 1.7) / 2, so
     each overlaps its neighbours by ~40% and the line reads as ONE lumpy bank; top at ~g + .46 against the collider's
     g + .45. Three clumps instead of two, at jittered heights, so the hedge's top line wanders.
  2. **the lane's sunken banks (1.9 m, walked on)**: a shouldered PROFILE run along the piece -- the foot spreads .55 m
     past the collider each side, the TOP keeps the collider's full width (so standing on the edge never floats over a
     visual slope), the crown .1 m proud. Built once per (W, H); **every face turned outward by a convexity test**
     (face centre minus the axis, dotted with the normal), not hand-ordered winding -- the profile is convex, so the
     test is exact. And **where a run starts or stops** (the lane's ends, the gaps at the barn's doors) an ellipsoid
     rounds it off: the flat cut end of the first piece was the most box-like thing left in the shot.
  Judged with `npm run shot town` (three passes: slab, profile, profile + ends) and `ridge`.

- **THE METROPOLIS ON THE HORIZON: A SCALED HOMOTHETY ABOUT THE LENS, ONE DRAW CALL (m323, farm polish 2, `SKYLINE`,
  `buildSkyline`, `skylineStep`).** m321/m322's shots: from the west hill the island city is a thin low strip, and from
  the crash site the hedges hide it entirely -- its buildings are two and three storeys at ~450 m (~3 deg over the
  horizon) and a 2 m hedge 30 m off stands 4 deg. Pushing the fog out would not have helped: there is nothing tall to
  see. **REGIONS says what the skyline IS**: the farm is the rural ring and the horizon is THE METROPOLIS -- skyscrapers,
  Dump Tower, "the skyline the aliens control from the top of Dump Tower". So it stands `dist` 1500 m past the island's
  middle on the line from the farm through it (centre (-1318, -718)), and from the fields the island city sits in front.
  **Placed by the table**: five DISTRICTS (core, The Pearl, Old Town, the waterfront with four cranes, the hill with the
  radio mast), each a named spot along the horizon with its reason, towers rolled inside it from seed 323; DUMP TOWER
  640 m, gold, three setbacks, a pulsing green beacon (it cuts the haze: k x .25) and a needle. 153 boxes, merged.
  **Its true distance (~2 km from the farm) is past every far plane here** (400 in the city, ~1,100 on the farm), so
  each frame (`skylineStep`, after `gradeStep`) the group is pulled toward the camera to `R` .86 x `camera.far` and
  scaled by the same k: world = cam + (true - cam) * k. **Every point keeps its exact bearing and angular size**, so it
  has real parallax as he walks, and depth still sorts it BEHIND the island and the hills (it sits at .86-.92 of far).
  Its own `ShaderMaterial`: per-vertex colour shaded off the sun's direction at build (sunlit faces warmer), floor
  bands and a lit window per ~16 cells, and its own haze -- `mix(c, scene.fog.color, haze * (1 - clear * h/400))`,
  thickest at the foot (`haze` .55, tops at .275) -- because scene fog would erase it. Tone-mapping and colour-space
  chunks at the end like `isle_water`. Every tower runs down to y -60 so its foot meets the water or the haze.
  **Tuned with `npm run shot`** (new rows `skyline` -- from the crash toward the city -- and `overcity`): haze .6 washed it
  into the pink; .46 made it read near and black; .55 sits it in the air. Lit windows at 12% read as night: 6%.
  GOD SWITCHES has **METROPOLIS ON THE HORIZON ON/OFF** (the A/B); `mel.SKYLINE` is live (`haze`, `clear`, `R`).
  `places` builds it and ticks `skylineStep`: `SKYLINE 153 boxes, centre [-1318,-718] one mesh`.
  **Not built: it is not reachable** -- it is the last region; nothing here pretends otherwise.

- **THE PATCHWORK READS FROM THE RIDGE NOW: A WARM FIELD DYES THE GRASS, IT DOES NOT MULTIPLY IT (m322, farm polish 1,
  `isleLandMat` FLD block, `FPLAN.dye`, `FPLAN.TINT`).** m321's ridge shot: every far field the same lime green.
  **Lime times gold is still lime** -- m308's tint MULTIPLIED the grass texture, so wheat [1.8, 1.38, .55] on a
  lime texel came out (.81, 1.03, .08), a yellower lime, and the crops (which carry the real colour) fade out with
  distance, leaving only the ground. Now, on the farmland only:
  1. the grass as a whole is taken a fifth of the way to grey and warmed (x 1.06, 1, .86) -- REGIONS' "golden
     countryside, straw", not acid lime;
  2. a tint whose red beats its green (wheat, hay, stubble, plough, the gouge, the scorch, the circle) DYES: the
     grass's LUMINANCE times the tint times `FPLAN.dye` (1.05), blended in by `(r - g) * 5`; a green tint (corn,
     pasture, orchard, reserve) multiplies exactly as before.
  So of 23 fields, 11 are warm (5 hay now STRAW, 3 wheat gold, 1 stubble, 2 plough brown with their furrows) and 12
  green, and corn [.62, .88, .42] is darker than pasture instead of the same. **Judged with `npm run shot ridge`**
  three times (before, dye .8, dye 1.05 + warm base), which is what the STEER's screenshot permission is for.
  `mel.FPLAN.dye.value` is live (a uniform); the TINT table wants a reload (it is baked into `aFld`).
  The GLSL is inside a JS template literal: **no backticks in its comments** (the first draft had them escaped, which
  is legal JS and was taken out rather than trusted to the GLSL preprocessor).

- **STEP 8, PROVED: `npm run places` AND THREE SCREENSHOTS, AND THE SCREENSHOT TOOL WORKS NOW (m321, `tools/shot.mjs`,
  `npm run shot`).** m295 dropped a screenshot tool because `page.screenshot` waits for the compositor to produce a
  frame and the kit city under SwiftShader takes longer than its 30 s timeout. **This one never asks the compositor**:
  it renders inside `page.evaluate` and reads the canvas with `toDataURL` in the SAME task, before the drawing buffer is
  cleared (no `preserveDrawingBuffer` needed). Boot ~25 s, one shot ~25 s, three in about 100 s. It serves the SHIPPED
  `index.html` and splices in exactly one thing, `window.__shot = { renderer, scene, camera }` in front of `mel`. Each
  shot is a row in `SHOTS`: a GOD place to stand at (`mel.go`), a settle time so the frame loop's steps (flora chunks,
  grade, culling) run round him, and a camera computed in the page from live state. Output to `shots/` (gitignored) or
  `SHOT_DIR`. Playwright is the global one (`/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright`), Chromium from `/opt/pw-browsers`.
  **`places` gained the NEW GAME row**: chapter 0, never in town, the shipped `crashSpawn` -- it lands 9.5 m from the
  wreck, on the farmland, on ground. Before this nothing checked the spawn itself, only the GOD place beside it.
  **What the shots show (the next polish passes, weakest first):**
  1. **From the ridge the patchwork does not read.** Every far field is the same lime green; the crops fade out with
     distance (as they should) and what is left is a ground tint that barely differs field to field. Wheat should
     read gold and ploughed earth brown from a hill, by the GROUND colour, because that is all there is at 200 m.
  2. **The city skyline is lost in haze** on the horizon from the overlook: the trestle reads, the towers do not.
  3. **The hedge banks are hard-edged earth boxes** with bushes on top -- from the road shot they read as rectangles.
  4. The crash shot reads well: wheat close up, the gouge, the saucer, fires, the hedge line and the farm beyond.

- **THE STEPPING-STONE FORD AND THE CREEK CULVERT (m320, step 7b-2, `FFORD`, `buildFord`, `FWATER.culvertAt`).**
  The third way over the channel and the lowest: flat stones a stride apart (`gap` 1.75 m) from the beach below the
  east pasture (`from` in the land's own (a, b)) out to the city's shore at bearing `toDeg` 79, the ray's coast
  point less 2 m, meandering `bow` 14 m off the straight line on a sine so it reads as a path found rather than
  laid. **Each stone is a box collider with its top just over the sea** (sea + .22, jittered +-.06) standing on the
  REAL seabed (the higher of `flHeightAt` and `isleBedAt`, floored at sea - 12, the trestle's own rule), drawn as a
  squat icosahedron top on a seven-sided cylinder, with weed at the waterline on about a third. Between them is the
  sea, and the sea's rule puts you back. A stone whose bed is over sea + .6 is skipped: on dry beach the shore is
  the step. **A stretch is under the tide** (`washed` .44-.6 of the way): `FFORD.gapM` measures it at **26.1 m** on
  a 172 m crossing, which nothing on foot clears (`MOVE.jump` 10.6 / g 20 is ~7.4 m at a run), so the checkpoint
  still teaches and it opens later. **Three cows stand drinking at its foot** -- `buildCows` puts them at `from` + 8 m
  in b with no field, so they are not counted against a pasture; `COWS` 33 still all in place.
  **THE CULVERT IS WHERE THE EAST TRACK CROSSES THE CREEK, AND IT IS FOUND, NOT TYPED**: a segment intersection of
  `FPLAN`'s `east_track` against the creek's own points, the bed read off `FL.cbed` there (-0.12). A stone box
  deck 2.9 m over the bed, walls at +-2.6 m along the track, kerbs, walkable quads on top, and earth embankments
  stepping down to the rims 12 m each side. **Each embankment step takes the LOWER end of its slice** (the first
  draft took the higher, which would have stood a lip in the way; caught before it shipped). **It is built inside `buildFarmWaters`, BEFORE
  `buildFieldBounds`**, so its floors are in `TRI` before the track ribbon is laid over it. GOD places `stones` and
  `culvert`; `mel.FFORD` is live. `npm run places`:

- **THE OLD RAIL TRESTLE: A SECOND WAY OVER THE CHANNEL, BROKEN FOR NOW (m319, step 7b-1, `FTRES`, `buildTrestle`, `ringHouse` gap).**
  REGIONS' connective tissue (never one road): west of the bridge an earth embankment climbs out of the south wheat
  (`FTRES.cut`, a margin in `fpOwner`: no crop on it, a gap in the hedges) to a timber trestle -- bents of two posts,
  X-braces and a cap every 5 m standing on the REAL seabed (the higher of `flHeightAt` and `isleBedAt`, floored at
  sea - 12), ties every .65 m, two rusted rails, no parapet -- that runs straight out, BENDS toward the city, and
  comes down a short ramp into the island's ring behind a house whose back fence is BROKEN (`FRING` row at 346 deg,
  `gap`): the way through the backyards into town without passing the checkpoint. No ring trees on its landing.
  **Measured, not assumed**: a probe along the whole 225 m every metre (`groundAt` a step above the last footing)
  found footing everywhere but the broken stretch. **The first break was 8 m in b, which removed ONE 5 m span and
  left a 4 m hole -- jumpable at a run** (`MOVE.jump` 10.6, g 20: ~1.06 s of air, 7.4 m at 7 m/s). It is
  b -170..-188 now and the probe reads 19 m with no footing, which nothing on foot clears: the extras are blocked
  so the checkpoint still teaches (STEER 7b); a form or Clancy opens it later.
  GOD `trestle` (the farm end) and `backyards` (where it comes down). 7b-2 (the stepping-stone ford with cows

- **THE FARM'S STATIC MESHES ARE BATCHED BY PAINT KIND AND CELL (m318, STEER step 7, `FBATCH`, `farmBatch`, `fbKey`, `farmPaintKind`).**
  Every builder since m288 works in its own `farmFrame` with its own materials and `commit` merged per material only
  WITHIN that frame: 108 static meshes, a draw call each, most in view from a hill with the fog at 950. After every
  frame-based builder (`buildCityRing` is the last), `farmBatch` takes each mesh `farmMerge` made (`userData.fbatch`,
  set there and nowhere else -- so the windmill's head, the washing, cows, vehicles and crops are never touched),
  BAKES its material colour into vertex colours (THREE's colours are already linear, which is what a vertex colour
  is), and re-merges it TRIANGLE BY TRIANGLE (each to the 200 m `cell` its centre is in) into one mesh per key:
  paint kind (`FP_KIND`, or none), metal or not, glow colour. 108 -> 71 meshes over 13 materials, the camera culling
  by cell. **The paint still lands**: `farmPaintKind` is `farmPaint` with the kind given (the shader reads WORLD
  position and normal, and baked geometry is in the world with an identity matrix).
  **Left out on purpose** (`fbKey` null, 7 meshes): a map (the signs), transparent (glass, wire, water), not
  FrontSide (the hay barn's roof), already vertex-coloured -- and two whole frames (`skip`): the crash's and its
  debris's, whose GLOW is animated through their materials and would stop pulsing in a batch.
  **Colliders are untouched** -- `BOXES` were filed at each `commit`; the batch only moves what is drawn.
  `?batch=0`, or GOD's FARM BATCHING switch (reloads), builds the farm unbatched for the A/B. Chip `B<before>><after>`.
  STEER step 7 with m309's crop chunks and distance fade: done.

- **THE CITY STARTS THIN ON ITS OWN RING (m317, step 6b, `FRING`, `buildCityRing`, `ringHouse`).**
  The kit city ended at its rectangle with empty grass round it. The island's ring (city edge to beach top) now
  holds the thin end of town, each row a BEARING (the rays' convention, in degrees) and `s`, a fraction across that
  ray's own grass (`isleRayAt`, `gw`) -- so a spot is always on the ring however wide it is there. Where the bridge
  comes in (bearing 28.6): a WAREHOUSE at 18 deg (26 x 14 x 6.5, a half-open roll-up door, a loading dock with crates,
  a forklift, and a 12-step outside stair to a flat roof you can walk) and a chain-link LOT at 39 deg with three
  parked cars; ten low HOUSES round the rest of the ring facing into the city with fenced back yards and a tree each;
  and ~40 TREES planted right against the city's edge every ~9 degrees (none within 5 deg of the bridge's line).
  **One identity frame** (`farmFrame(0, 0, 0)`: u = x, v = z) for the whole ring, so it is one mesh per material; a
  house is TURNED by psi = atan2(dx, dz) of its ray, its local +v out to sea and its front (-v) to the city, and every
  part goes through `L(lu, lv)` (the frame's own mapping) with `psi + p0`. 171 colliders.
  GOD `warehouse` (exempt from `places`' OFF THE FARMLAND: it is on the city's ring by design). That finishes step 6.

  every 30 m along the bridge road 5 m off it with wires sagging in three pieces, and the bridge road PAVED for its

- **THE FARMHANDS AND THE FARMER ARE AUTHORED NPC MARKERS, SO THE SHIPPED MARKER PATH SPAWNS THEM (m315, step 5c, `FHANDS`, `buildFarmhands`, `fpCentroid`).**
  Five people on the land: Dale in the wheat by the bridge road, Wendell on the west hill's hay, Mags in the orchard,
  Earl at the foot of the ploughed field watching the tractor, and Farmer Gristle at his barn doors (B2's farmer).
  **No new spawning code**: each row is pushed into `MARKS` as a `type: 'npc'` entry (`src: 'FARMHANDS'`) by
  `buildFarmhands`, which runs in the farm's build sequence -- BEFORE the crowd's deal (`kitPopulate` resets `K.at`)
  and `mkrNpcPlace` (checked: line 34120 against 34191). `mkrNpcPlace` deals it to its kind's `at`, the body spawns
  there, and `mkrStep` finds it within 2.5 m and gives it its home, its heading and its `lines` with the "!" -- STEER
  2's "speakers only from authored places", exactly the path his own `npc_*` markers take. Stand-ins per
  CHARACTERS.md: farmhands `hobo_01`, the farmer `hick_skinny` (`MKR.alias` farmer). They roam their kind's `roam`
  round the spot. A field row stands at its field's CENTROID off the owner lattice (`fpCentroid`) plus `off`, and is
  refused (`FARMHAND .. OFF FIELD`) if that lands outside the field.
  **What `npm run places` cannot see**: the bodies themselves (it loads no GLBs). It checks the five markers exist and
  stand on the farmland; whether each body spawned and talks is the phone's (GOD lists every talker as `TALK · name`).

- **A TRACTOR PLOUGHS AND A PICKUP RUNS THE BRIDGE ROAD (m314, step 5b, `FVEH`, `buildVehicles`, `vehStep`, `vehLanes`, `vehMerge`).**
  **The tractor** works the field under the far hill: `vehLanes` walks lines along the field's furrow `dir`, 5 m
  apart, takes the longest run whose lattice owner is the field (and 3 m either side of it), and trims 7 m into the
  headland -- 12 lanes, driven boustrophedon and ping-ponged, at 2.2 m/s, turning 0.55 rad/s, so the U-turns happen
  on the field and not through its fence. **The pickup** drives the lane's own centreline from the barn door (the
  lane's points put through the barn's frame) to its mouth, then `FPLAN`'s bridge road reversed to the bridge (its last
  point IS the lane's mouth, so the join is exact), waits 9 s, and comes back. Both are KINEMATIC followers (steer at
  the next waypoint at a capped turn rate, slow in the turns and near a waypoint), sit on `flHeightAt` and pitch to it
  (Euler order YXZ: yaw, then pitch about its own right; nose up = -atan(rise)), push him out of an oriented box along
  its shallower side, and stop (damped hard) if he is in the 5 m in front of them. Dust (`smokeAt`, earth colours)
  off the back while moving and within 140 m.
  **Each vehicle is ONE draw call**: `vehMerge` bakes its parts into a single vertex-coloured geometry (box, wheel and
  plough discs, the pickup's cab glass, lights and a bale in the bed). The parked tractor is still the barnyard's.
  **No engine sound** -- a held synth voice like the wreck's hum is the obvious next step. GOD `ploughing`, `pickup`
  (beside each, facing it, wherever it is). `npm run places` ticks `vehStep` with the rest.

- **HERDS IN THE PASTURES, EACH KEPT TO ITS OWN FIELD (m313, step 5a, `FHERDS`, `fpOwnAt`, `buildCows`, `cowPick`).**
  The m294 cows were six in the paddock and a field beside the old crash. On the farm's own land: the paddock keeps
  three, and `FHERDS` puts 27 more in six pastures (far hill 5, the neighbour's ridge 6, the slope above the creek
  mouth 5, the pond 4, home pasture 4, the creek pasture 3) -- 30, still ONE instanced draw (16 parts a cow), still
  redrawn only within 140 m. **A herd cow's home is its field's CENTROID off the owner lattice** (a seed is not the
  middle of its noise-bent cell) with a range from the field's own area, and `cowPick` only takes a spot whose lattice
  owner IS its field (`fpOwnAt`, a lookup, not `fpOwner` again) -- the pasture fences already stop a cow; this stops
  it choosing to walk into one and standing there stuck.
  `npm run places` now fails if any herd cow starts outside its own pasture. **Its first version read `bad` above
  that `let`'s own line** -- the repo's oldest landmine, in the checker this time: the count is carried past it.
  GOD `herd` (the far hill's). 5b (a tractor working a field, a pickup on the tracks) and 5c (farmhands) follow.

- **THE NEIGHBOUR'S FARM ON THE RIDGE AND THE LONE HAY BARN (m312, step 4c, `FNEIGH`, `buildNeighbours`, `FARMLAND.FLATS`).**
  GAME_DESIGN's new "exaggerated scale and contrast" (tall and thin beside short and squat), on the ridge where the
  ridge track ends: a TALL, NARROW house (6 x 5.5, three lit floors, a 57-degree roof to 12.8 m, pale blue boards --
  not Gristle's cream), a LONG, SQUAT cattle shed (22 x 7, 2.9-3.4 m, open to the yard), a SKINNY water tower (12 m
  legs, a red tank, a cap, a ladder), and the FARM SHOP by the track (an awning, a counter, crates of apples, pumpkins
  and greens, a painted sign) where B1f's neighbour will stand. **The lone hay barn**: an open Dutch barn (ten steel
  posts, a curved roof) with its hay in three steps -- 1.5, 3.0, 4.5 m, each narrower -- climbable at `MOVE.jump`'s
  2.8 m, and 1 m of head room under the roof at the top step (the roof is at g + 7.3 over its 6 m-wide top block).
  **FLATS settle to their OWN ground's height**, not to the land's base: m306's yard flatten removes the hills (it sets
  `h` to 0), which on the RIDGE would have dug a pit into it. Each flat's height is measured at its middle with the
  flats off (`flatOn`), before the creek's bed and the pond's rim are sampled, then lerped in over r .5..1.
  **The curved roof** is a cylinder's top arc laid along u (`rotateZ(pi/2)`: (x, y, z) -> (-y, x, z), so its section is
  y' = R sin t, z' = R cos t, t in pi/2 +- .9) -- open-ended, so its material is DoubleSide or its inside is not drawn.
  **Caught before shipping**: the shop's awning slats tilted about the wrong axis (sideways): psi pi/2 and tilt -.25.
  The hay barn's footprint is a 15 m margin in `fpOwner` (no hay grows inside it). GOD `neighbour`, `haybarn`.

- **THE YARD IS TWO YARDS, THE HOUSE HAS ITS OWN, AND THE HEADLAND'S FIELDS STAND DOWN (m311, step 4b, `FPLAN.yards`, `FHOUSE.origin`, shed, coop, orchard).**
  The m306 parcel (one superellipse round everything m288-m305 built) is TWO small yards in `FPLAN.yards`: the
  BARNYARD where the barn, lean-to, silo, paddock and sunken lane always stood, and the HOUSEYARD 72 m north across the
  home pasture. **The farmhouse has its own frame** (`FHOUSE.origin`, th from `ub` - .12): its porch faces south to the
  barn, with a TOOL SHED (pent roof, a doorway, tools leaning, a drum) on one side and a CHICKEN COOP (a hut on legs,
  its ramp, a wire run) on the other. The ground the old parcel held is fields now (`home_corn` with the scarecrow
  moved into it, `home_pasture`, an `orchard` of small trees in rows, `creek_pasture`); a `home_track` runs barnyard
  to porch and the ridge and east tracks start from the house.
  **What stands down on the farm's own land**: `HROW` (the headland's hedgerow fields, plough, copse, bale stack --
  `FPLAN` does that job now), `FLORA.FIELDS` (the headland's crop rectangles -- `FCROP` plants `FPLAN`'s; the tufts
  stay), and the sunken lane's little BROOK with its culvert, ford and footbridge (the land has its creek valley).

- **THE FIELDS ARE AN AUTHORED PLAN, AND ONE RULE DRAWS THEM THREE TIMES (m308, step 3, `FPLAN`, `fpOwner`, `fpTint`, `buildFieldBounds`).**
  20 named SEEDS (crop + reason) and a superellipse PARCEL round m288-m305's cluster. A point of land belongs to the
  nearest seed, with the distance bent by per-seed value noise (`noise` 9 m) so borders wander instead of running as
  straight bisectors; **margins belong to no field** -- the beach, the creek's valley (9.5), the pond's bank (r + 11)
  and a 2.6 m strip either side of every TRACK, so a track is always the border it runs along and every boundary
  has a gap where a track crosses it. Measured: fields 2.2k-7.1k m2, the yard parcel 14.7k.
  **Use 1, the ground** (`aFld`, baked per land vertex in `buildFarmland`): rgb tints the grass (wheat gold, corn deep
  green, hay pale, ploughed brown), w = 10 + a furrow angle in the WORLD for a ploughed field, drawn as stripes in the
  land shader -- so the patchwork reads from the west hill before a single crop stands on it. The farmland got its
  own material (`isleLandMat({ fields, shareU })`) on the island's uniforms. **`m.defines = { FLD: 1 }` would have
  wiped MeshStandardMaterial's own `STANDARD` define** -- it is merged.
  **Use 2, the boundaries**: a 2 m owner lattice, a point wherever two owners meet, thinned to one per `piece` 2.7 m by
  a spatial hash, and each piece TURNED along its nearest same-pair neighbours either side (measured off the boundary,
  not assumed from the seeds -- the noise bends it). By the crops either side: hedge (bank, hedge collider, two
  clumps, an oak every `treeGap` 24), fence (post, two rails, one thin collider) where a pasture or a reserve is
  involved, a tree line (every `lineGap` 10) on a quarter of the crop pairs. 333 hedge, 303 fence, 95 trees.
  **(a, b) is a REFLECTION of (x, z)** (det[ua; ub] = -1): every ribbon here derives its winding off its first
  triangle, and the features frame takes (a, -b).
  **Use 3, the crops**: step 3b (not yet). **The tracks** are the lane's ribbon on the land's axes; `bridge_road` ends at
  the sunken lane's mouth, measured by putting the yard frame's (30, -9) through `buildFarm`'s placement
  (`fpLaneMouth`). The m305 fingerpost's TOWN arm now aims down it (it pointed down the m305 road, away from the bridge).
  GOD `swell`, `fplough`. Chip adds `h<hedges>f<fences>t<trees>` to `FL`.

- **THE CREEK VALLEY AND THE POND ARE CARVED INTO THE ONE HEIGHT FUNCTION (m307, step 2, `FARMLAND.CREEK`/`POND`, `flBase`, `buildFarmWaters`, `farmTree`).**
  `flHeight` is now `flBase` (m306's land) then two carves, so the mesh, the collider and the sea's depth all see the
  same valley and bowl. **The creek's bed is a RUNNING MINIMUM downstream** of (`flBase` - `dig`) sampled every 2 m and
  resampled to an even arc step (the per-segment sample counts round differently, so the raw array is not even) --
  its water can never run uphill or stand above the ground it is cut into. Measured: 5.19 at the source under the
  long ridge, -8.5 where it reaches the sea, 255 m long; where the land rises again (the low rise) it cuts a gorge.
  Profile: a slight channel `hb` 1.7 either side, then walls at `wall` .3 (17 deg, walkable).
  **The pond's level is MEASURED**: the lowest of 24 points on a ring 1.25 r out, minus .35 (and never under sea + .6),

- **THE FARM IS ITS OWN LAND ACROSS A CHANNEL NOW (m306, STEER "farm rebuild" step 1, `FARMLAND`, `buildFarmland`, `buildChannelBridge`).**
  He walked m302-m304: *"it's like 12 feet away from the border of the city... a very small city block tacked onto the
  edge of the city... the border between the city and the farm is just a line."* The docs had said "intimate, empty
  ground is a failure" and "SMALL and DENSE"; both are rewritten ("Scale follows the place", "No borders that are
  lines"). Step 1:
  **THE LAND**: a superellipse 460 x 340 m (`A` 230, `B` 170, `pw` 3.2, coast wandering `wob` 9%) centred 404 m out
  on bearing .5 rad (the sun's side, so from the farm the city is lit from behind you), `gap` 70 m of channel from
  the city island's waterline. Authored `HILLS` and `RIDGES`, each with its reason; the yard's patch settled level
  (`yard`, r 75) so m288-m305's pieces stand on it. **One height function** (`flHeight`) feeds the mesh, the collider
  (12,344 floor tris through `isleAppend`) and the water's depth; normals by central differences off it, so the nine
  chunks (`chunk` 40 cells of 5 m, culled by the camera) do not seam. The island's land material, shared.
  **THE WATER, AND WHY IT IS A SECOND MESH**: the city's sea is radial and its skirt is single triangles out to 1,800 m,
  so it cannot carry a second shore. The farm has its own grid IN ITS OWN FRAME, depth = sea - max(`flHeight`,
  `isleBedAt`), on the sea's own uniforms (`wmat.clone()` with `uniforms` re-shared, `FARMW` defined); the city's water
  discards inside that turned rectangle (`uCut`, `uCutA`). **First cut was an axis-aligned box round the turned
  island: it reached back to x -14, over the city's own coast, and drew 23,810 water tris -- the turned rect is 8,254.**
  **THE BRIDGE** (`buildChannelBridge`, dispatched from `buildBridge` while `FARMLAND.live`): 166 m from just past the
  city's edge to the farm's beach top (both feet MEASURED by marching the bearing), ramps at 16% off each shore, a deck
  on 5 piers with cutwaters, lamps, parapets, and the checkpoint (booth, striped arm) at the TOWN end --
  `BRIDGE.gate`. The m291 river/hairpin is not built in `tkit` now (`riverStep` and `cowClear` read `river.F`, null).
  **THE LONG VIEW** (`gradeStep`): golden hour by `flEdgeAt` (the whole land, fading over the channel), and the fog
  lerps to `FARMLAND.fog` (150 / 950) with `camera.far` following it +150 -- which also lets `cellStep` (culls past
  the fog) draw the city's far cells. The skyline is the real city.
  **STILL IN THE OLD SHAPE** (steps 2-6): everything m288-m305 built came along as one cluster round the yard, in its
  old frame; the crash is still beside it; no creek valley or pond in the land yet; no track from the bridge to the
  yard (the m305 road needs `BRIDGE.foot`, which the channel bridge does not set, so it is not drawn).
  GOD `overlook` (the west hill, facing the city) and `channel` (the bridge's farm end). Chip `FL<chunks>/<floor tris>`.

- **THE FARM HAD NOBODY'S HOUSE (m304, farm pass 9, `FHOUSE`, `buildFarmhouse`, `farmhouseStep`).**
  REGIONS.md: *"the farmer and his family"* -- and the yard was a barn, a silo and a lean-to. Pass 9 is the farmhouse,
  the biggest silhouette that was missing: two storeys of cream board-and-batten (`cream`, FPAINT kind 1) on a stone
  plinth, an oxide-red roof with the ridge along the porch, a stone chimney on the +u gable, every window LIT (`glow`,
  emissive 0xffc56a), green shutters, a deep porch facing the corn and the lane with chairs and a table and steps down
  the middle. **Vertical**: a rain barrel (1.05) beside the porch's east end, then the porch roof (~3 m, walkable
  `quad`) -- one jump each at `MOVE.jump` 10.6 / g 20 (2.8 m). **Alive**: chimney smoke (`smokeAt`, within 160 m) and a
  washing line behind the house, four sheets on ONE `InstancedMesh` swinging in `farmhouseStep`.
  **WHERE, MEASURED NOT GUESSED**: u 9.5..18.5, v 7.5..14.5 -- the one empty plot in the yard on m303's frame map,
  between the corn (v <= 2), the hay meadow (v >= 18.5), the paddock fence (u <= 6) and the yard's east hedge (u ~21).
  **Orientation, checked by hand** (the m288 fence rule): with psi = pi/2 a box's local x points -v, so a roof slab on
  the +v side rises toward the ridge with tilt +ang (the barn's is -s ang because its local x is +u), and the porch
  roof, higher at the wall (+v), takes -tl. The gables are the barn's extrude turned Ry(pi/2): shape x -> -v
  (symmetric), extrusion z -> +u, so they straddle the end walls. The cloth's Euler is 'YXZ' (Ry psi puts the sheet's
  width along the line, then Rx swings it about the line) in the frame group's own local space.
  **Caught on the read-back before shipping**: a step formula that multiplied its own height by 0, front rails that ran
  0.35 m past the porch's end post, a log-pile collider 0.65 m taller than its logs, and GOD's spot in the corn.
  GOD `farmhouse` (on the path, facing the porch). Ground paint `porch` (the worn path). Chip `FH<boxes+tris>`.

  built and in no field** -- the band from the paddock and the crash to the beach, and the whole north end past the
  creek. Two halves to the fix:
  **(1) the headland was too big for the farm** (`out` 34 -> 24): the shore sat at v ~55 off the yard against a layout
  drawn to ~31, so "the wheat down to the shore" stopped 24 m short. At 24 the farm's ray has 65.6 m (`need` 60).
  **(2) what is left is fields**: four hedgerow RUNS (bank .5 + hedge 1.45, over a man; leaf clumps on a collider; a
  piece on beach ground is skipped, so every hedge stops at the shore by itself), a tree standing IN each run every
  ~13 m, a gate in each (two posts and a five-bar gate swung open), a copse of nine oaks at the headland's tip, three
  willows on the river bank, the PLOUGHED field as one ribbon of ridges down the slope (20 cm, drawn not collided --
  under a step), round bales in the hay meadow and a stack of three to climb. Crops are rows in `FLORA.FIELDS` (hay,
  stubble, potatoes on the ridge tops via `jit`/`lift`, rough grass, ferns) -- no new draw call. After: **15% of the
  GRASS is bare** (grass only, not beach; the 56% counted beach too, so the two are not the same measure).
  **The creek and the wheat now reach the beach** (the creek was a fixed 40 m polyline that stopped mid-field; it
  meanders on until the beach filter takes it).
  **THE FLORA MESH IS FRUSTUM-CULLED NOW**: ~2,000 clumps became ~7,900 (68k -> 55k tris after thinning stubble,
  ferns and rough grass), and m297 drew it from everywhere, every frame. `InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere` covers
  every instance; +3 m for the sway.
  **Handedness, checked by hand**: a limb leans to (cos a, sin a) with Euler (0, -a, -.75) (Rz first, then Ry); a gate
  swung by psi - 1.22 opens toward the run's left; the bale stack's axes are perpendicular to its offset (dot 0); the
  plough's four triangle kinds all have +y normals (1.2 h > 0).
